entries.headline: A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-81578 +2exploitedupdatedNATOB1

CVE-2026-82078 / CVE-2026-81578, PaperCut NG/MF: an Apache Tapestry request-routing confusion chains an unauthenticated config rewrite to arbitrary code execution, exploited before a patch existed

PaperCut has been targeted before: Rapid7 notes that in 2023 CVE-2023-27350 was broadly exploited in the wild by multiple threat-actor groups, including ransomware operators, which raises the urgency of this new zero-day (Rapid7, 2026-08-28). PaperCut disclosed on 27 August 2026 that it was investigating active exploitation of a new flaw in the same product line, before any CVE, patch or public technical detail existed (watchTowr, 2026-10-09); Rapid7 relays PaperCut's statement that information supplied by a university customer's security team and its digital forensics and incident response team enabled PaperCut to reproduce the vulnerability (Rapid7, 2026-08-28).

PaperCut's Application Server runs on the Apache Tapestry web framework, whose "complex direct" request format lets a single HTTP request name one page to render and a different page's component to actually execute. PaperCut's own authorization check validates only the page selected for rendering, not the component that runs behind it, so a request that asks Tapestry to render the public, unauthenticated Error, Exception, or Home page while invoking the administrative ConfigEditor or UserList component bypasses authentication entirely (Rapid7, 2026-08-28). Through three such POST requests, /app?service=direct/1/Error/ConfigEditor/quickFindForm, .../ConfigEditor/$Form, and .../UserList/$QuickFind.$Form, an unauthenticated attacker rewrites four external card/ID lookup settings (user-lookup.db-driver, user-lookup.db-url, user-lookup.id-to-username-sql, user-lookup.enabled) that normally point PaperCut at an administrator-configured external card database (Rapid7, 2026-08-28). Redirected instead to an attacker-controlled JDBC target through PaperCut's bundled Apache Derby driver and its foreignViews feature, the connection reaches an attacker-controlled H2 database whose inline INIT statement creates a JavaScript-backed trigger; PaperCut's bundled Nashorn JavaScript engine then executes that trigger to launch an operating-system process, full remote code execution as the PaperCut server, triggered the moment the forged UserList search runs the malicious lookup (Rapid7, 2026-08-28). This is a two-CVE chain: CVE-2026-81578 (CWE-306, missing authentication) is the pre-auth entry that gains write access to the server configuration; CVE-2026-82078 (CWE-470, unsafe dynamic class loading) is the flaw that turns a reconfigured database connection into arbitrary Java bytecode execution once that write access is held (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10).

PaperCut treats all versions of NG and MF as potentially affected (Rapid7, 2026-08-28). Huntress observed two live customer exploitations: one on 26 August lasting under two minutes against version 25.0.10.75465, and a second on 27 August against version 24.1.5.71847, before Emergency Patch Release 2 extended coverage to the v24 line (Huntress, 2026-08-28). In both cases the attacker ran base64-encoded discovery commands (whoami & ver, and separately whoami & ver & tasklist) via a dropped, OS-agnostic Java .class file; in the first incident it wrote its output to a temporary file and then deleted both that file and the server's own server.log (Huntress, 2026-08-28). Huntress's own proof-of-concept reproduced the full chain against a stock PaperCut NG install and observed the code execution surface as an observable charmap.exe process running as SYSTEM, spawned under the PaperCut Application Server's own pc-app.exe process (Huntress, 2026-08-28). PaperCut released an initial emergency patch for v25 and v26 on 28 August and patches for v24 later the same day, and Rapid7 says the first patch could be bypassed by using the Home page for display while the newest version of the vendor patch remediates that bypass (Rapid7, 2026-08-28). PaperCut then superseded the earlier emergency patches with Emergency Patch Release 3 on 1 September 2026 and replaced all three emergency patches on 10 September with fully tested maintenance releases (see the updates below) (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10). There is no fix for v23 and earlier; PaperCut's guidance for that line is to upgrade to a supported version (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10), and Huntress estimated on 28 August that 47% of the roughly 2,500 PaperCut installations it tracks ran v23 or older (Huntress, 2026-08-28).

Detection, telemetry class first: alert on any child process spawned from pc-app.exe or the PaperCut Application Server's Java process, the lineage under which the observed exploitation ran its discovery commands. Web-access logs for the PaperCut Application Server should be checked for POST requests from an unauthenticated session whose service parameter puts a non-administrative page in front of the ConfigEditor or UserList component, such as /app?service=direct/1/LogonMessage/ConfigEditor/quickFindForm, because PaperCut checks authorization only for that first page (watchTowr, 2026-10-09); the Error and Home variants described above follow the same shape, so the signal is the page in front of the component, not the component. Two log artifacts are near-unique indicators: a server.log DB URL: line pointing at an in-memory Derby database, and a corresponding derby.log entry recording Derby booting an in-memory database under an attacker-chosen name (Huntress, 2026-08-28). PaperCut stresses that the absence of its file artifacts does not rule out compromise because the attacker may clean them up (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10), and Huntress observed the payload deleting the server's own server.log (Huntress, 2026-08-28). Requests to /rpc/api/xmlrpc that call api.setConfigValue or api.lookUpUserNameByCardNo from addresses outside the allowlist match the XML-RPC route, and Hunt.io advises disabling the endpoint where it is not needed (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). Hunt.io's recovered kit also adds changes to the user-lookup.* settings, unexpected files under custom/web/, and chisel or cron entries calling out to non-standard ports (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The later authentication bypass that watchTowr documents reaches the Setup Wizard pages through the Home page, so requests whose service parameter routes through Home to a setup page such as SetupAdmin on a server whose setup is long complete are the matching pattern (watchTowr, 2026-10-09). Triage: an unexpectedly truncated, gapped, or missing server.log on a PaperCut Application Server is worth investigating even where no other artifact survives, since Huntress saw the payload delete that log.

Defender takeaway
Any PaperCut NG/MF Application Server that has ever been reachable from the public internet should be assumed targeted; upgrade it to the maintenance release for its line immediately, and where v23 or earlier cannot yet be replaced, remove public exposure entirely rather than relying on detection alone. Set an explicit XML-RPC API token and allowlist on every server as well: Hunt.io says an instance hardened against the Tapestry bypass is not necessarily protected against the second route if its XML-RPC API is exposed with weak access controls (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15).
Update03 Sep 2026 05:05 UTCrun 2026-09-03T0410Z-intelcvesactionsimmediate_actionsummarytechniquesevidencesourcing_notebody

PaperCut's Emergency Patch Release 3, published 1 September 2026, supersedes Release 2 and is cumulative, customers do not need to install the earlier releases first (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-02). Release 3 addresses two known regressions, fixing broken SAML login flows and restoring support for legacy Microsoft SQL Server drivers used for external card lookup, and adds further, undisclosed hardening against the exploitation chain (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-02). PaperCut also confirms a second wave of attacks against servers that remain unpatched and internet-facing, whose post-compromise behaviour "has been more sophisticated than in the first days of this incident" (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-02). The vendor's own incident data, published 30 August as additional indicators of compromise, names a concrete follow-on chain from the original intrusion: after initial discovery commands, a PowerShell-delivered download installs a Windows service literally named "Remote Access Service" running SimpleService.exe, a SimpleHelp remote-access agent, as LocalSystem with auto-start, followed by a further download of AnyDesk; the bulletin does not state whether this specific chain recurred in the second wave or belongs only to the earlier intrusions it was published alongside (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-02). Mobility Print and Print Deploy server components are unaffected; Site Servers and secondary/print servers do need the same update as the primary Application Server (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-02).

Update10 Sep 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-09-10T0410Z-intelsummarytechniquesactionssourcesevidencebody

GreyNoise's Global Observation Grid documents an AI-agent-orchestrated exploitation campaign against this chain beginning 31 August 2026, run by a likely Russian-speaking operator already tracked since July 2026 for attacks on Palo Alto, Ubiquiti, Citrix, SonicWall and Proxmox VE targets (GreyNoise, 2026-09-09). The operator built and tested both CVEs' exploits in a self-hosted PaperCut/Active Directory lab, sourced target lists via the Netlas.io scanning service, then deployed hundreds of AI agents, built on OpenAI's Codex harness paired with a DeepSeek model, to opportunistically "compromise at least 440 instances of PaperCut MF/NG hosted by 395 identified victim organizations in 48 countries" (GreyNoise, 2026-09-09). GreyNoise reports the adversary "went from an empty workspace to first achieving RCE against a real victim in just under four hours, first domain admin in an additional two hours, and once the full campaign launched, compromised at least 11 organizations in 26 seconds" (GreyNoise, 2026-09-09), with one US high school reaching full domain admin in seven minutes from initial access. At its last observation, GreyNoise had seen domain admin reached against only twelve victim organizations, "GreyNoise observed the adversary achieved domain admin against only 12 victim organizations" (GreyNoise, 2026-09-09), via three paths: LSASS credential harvesting for pass-the-hash against the domain controller when the PaperCut host was domain-joined; the 2021 noPac flaws (CVE-2021-42278/CVE-2021-42287) where those remained unpatched; or directly adding a new account to Domain Admins when the PaperCut host itself ran on the domain controller or under a domain-admin service account. All three paths finished with a DCSync-based full NTDS.DIT credential dump; Cloudflare's WAF defeated the adversary against at least one targeted instance. This delta is reported by GreyNoise alone; a second independent source had not corroborated it as of this update.

Update29 Sep 2026 22:55 UTCrun 2026-09-29T2134Z-auditsummaryimmediate_actioncvesactionsevidenceheadlinetagssourcesbody

PaperCut published security maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 for NG and MF on 10 September 2026. Unlike the emergency patches, they went through the vendor's full release testing, carry new version numbers and release notes, and address all the CVEs in the advisory with the same protection as the emergency patches plus additional hardening. PaperCut's instruction is plain: "These releases replace the emergency patches. If you are running an emergency patch build, move to a maintenance release. If you have not yet patched, upgrade now." A server already on Emergency Patch Release 3 is protected against both CVEs and can schedule the upgrade through normal change control, while one still on Release 1 or 2 should move now. Site Servers and secondary/print servers should be updated to a patched version, not just the primary Application Server (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10).

Nothing changes for v23 and earlier: there is no emergency patch or maintenance release for that line, and the only route to a fixed build is an upgrade to a supported line (24, 25 or 26), with web access to the Application Server restricted to trusted addresses until then. PaperCut also reports that new compromises have slowed considerably and that most customers now have the Application Server behind a firewall or on a patched build, but that publicly reachable, unpatched servers are still being targeted (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10). For an estate that patched in the first week, the task is to move each server from its emergency build to the maintenance release and confirm the version on every Site Server and secondary server, not only on the primary. CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-31 (CISA KEV).

Update10 Oct 2026 03:46 UTCrun 2026-10-10T0255Z-intelprioritysummaryimmediate_actiontagscvesactionssourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

watchTowr Labs published a write-up on 2026-10-09 that follows the emergency patches build by build (watchTowr, 2026-10-09). Its timeline: the patch released on 28 August (26.0.4-PO build 76508) fixed two bypasses watchTowr had reported; watchTowr then bypassed the fix for the authentication bypass again (tracked internally as WT-2026-0143, no CVE assigned) and found a new post-authentication code-execution flaw in Scan-to-Fax (WT-2026-0144, now CVE-2026-82077), which together gave a full unauthenticated chain against build 76508; the patch released on 1 September (build 76530) fixes WT-2026-0143, and 26.0.5, released on 10 September, fixes CVE-2026-82077 (watchTowr, 2026-10-09). The authentication bypass abuses the Setup Wizard forms, which the earlier patches had ignored: every stage can be reached through the Home page even after setup is complete, and watchTowr shows it modifies the administrator password (watchTowr, 2026-10-09). watchTowr also publishes a Detection Artefact Generator that tests a server's exposure to the authentication bypasses but does not run the full chain (watchTowr, 2026-10-09).

PaperCut's September security bulletin lists CVE-2026-82077 as a code-execution flaw in the Scan-to-Fax component that needs an authenticated administrator, rated CVSS 4.0 7.3, fixed in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13, and says servers already on the latest release are covered (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-24); in that text it named no 24.x release and no emergency build, and its revision of 2026-10-13 lists 24.1.10 for the 24.x branch (see the update of 2026-10-17). The unauthenticated chain watchTowr describes is closed by the 1 September patch, but an administrator-level foothold still reaches code execution through Scan-to-Fax until the maintenance release is installed. No source names exploitation of CVE-2026-82077 or of the Setup Wizard bypass. PaperCut says Emergency Patch Release 3 closes off additional attack vectors it has observed being exploited in the wild, without naming them (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10).

Update17 Oct 2026 03:38 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-inteltitlesummaryregionstechniquescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Hunt.io found three open directories on one attacker host and reconstructs the operator's toolkit from the files in them; it says the recovered material aligns with GreyNoise's published account of the AI-driven campaign (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The operator's notes record a second route to code execution that does not use the Tapestry bypass: PaperCut's XML-RPC API at /rpc/api/xmlrpc accepts api.setConfigValue when its network allowlist is too permissive or no explicit API token is configured, because the handler then falls back to the built-in admin password as the token, and the same user-lookup settings are then rewritten (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). Hunt.io says an instance already hardened against the Tapestry bypass is not necessarily protected against this one if its XML-RPC API is exposed with weak access controls (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15); it does not report the route used against a victim. PaperCut's documentation says the API's authentication token should be defined in the advanced config key auth.webservices.auth-token and that the address allowlist can be set in the admin interface or through auth.webservices.allowed-addresses (PaperCut Software, 2026-01-30).

The files also show what follows a compromise. A Linux kit keeps a chisel reverse SOCKS5 client alive through cron entries (periodic and at reboot) and a watchdog script that checks the process (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The Windows playbook exports the SECURITY and SYSTEM registry hives from a compromised host to recover LSA secrets, the domain machine account's password among them, offline (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). The scale comes from the actor's own files: a reconnaissance pool of 1,005 hosts in at least 45 countries (800 confirmed vulnerable and 205 flagged from version fingerprinting), 2,165 logged attempts, 46 Active Directory domains packaged as victim data and 45 targets with a live reverse SOCKS5 pivot at the time of capture (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15). Switzerland is among the countries listed for those 45 targets, with no sector or organisation named, and Hunt.io says it shared its findings and the victim data with the national CERTs of the affected countries (Hunt.io, 2026-10-15).

PaperCut's September security bulletin, last updated 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 on the 24.x branch as well as in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13, and recommends 26.0.5, 25.0.13 or 24.1.11 or later (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-24).

Correction19 Oct 2026 21:07 UTCrun 2026-10-18T1307Z-auditsummaryactionsbody

Four statements above are corrected. PaperCut's bulletin says Emergency Patch Release 3 "addresses two known regressions", broken SAML login and support for legacy Microsoft SQL Server drivers for external card lookup, without saying Release 2 introduced them, as the update of 2026-09-03 stated (PaperCut Software, 2026-09-10). The web-log hunt now covers requests that put a non-administrative page such as LogonMessage in front of the ConfigEditor component, the route watchTowr documents, since PaperCut checks authorization only for that first page; the earlier pattern listed only Error, Exception and Home and missed it (watchTowr, 2026-10-09). Huntress's estimate that 47% of the installations it tracks run v23 or older dates from 28 August (Huntress, 2026-08-28). GreyNoise counts twelve victim organizations where domain admin was reached as of its last observation, not as a final tally out of the 395 (GreyNoise, 2026-09-09). The detection text and the second action now describe the Derby artifact as an in-memory database under an attacker-chosen name, without printing the name itself, which is an indicator value (Huntress, 2026-08-28).

updates.summary: PaperCut shipped Emergency Patch Release 3 on 1 September 2026, superseding Release 2 and fixing two regressions Release 2 had introduced (broken SAML login; lost legacy Microsoft SQL Server driver support for external card lookup). PaperCut also confirms a second, more sophisticated wave of attacks against still-unpatched, internet-facing servers, and separately published incident data naming a post-compromise chain installing a SimpleHelp remote-access service and AnyDesk for durable access.

GreyNoise documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this chain beginning 31 August 2026, using hundreds of AI agents to opportunistically compromise 440 PaperCut instances across 395 organizations in 48 countries, reaching domain admin against 12 of them in as little as five minutes via LSASS credential harvesting, the 2021 noPac flaws, or a PaperCut host running on the domain controller itself, all finishing with a DCSync-based NTDS.DIT credential dump.

PaperCut published fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 on 10 September 2026. They carry every fix from the three emergency patches plus further hardening, and replace the emergency patches as the recommended build. A server on Emergency Patch Release 3 is protected and can schedule the move normally; one on Release 1 or 2 should upgrade now. There is still no fix for v23 and earlier. PaperCut also reports that new compromises slowed considerably in early September while unpatched, exposed servers are still targeted. CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-31, which the status fields now record.

watchTowr published on 2026-10-09 how the emergency patches were bypassed in turn: the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and a new administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw, CVE-2026-82077, is fixed only in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13, not in the emergency builds. No source names exploitation of either, though PaperCut says Emergency Patch Release 3 closes off further attack vectors it has seen exploited. Earlier statements the cited sources do not support were corrected where they stood: the 2023 precedent, the university-customer statement, the emergency-patch chronology and the detection wording.

Hunt.io recovered the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) and reports a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API that does not use the Tapestry bypass and works when the API allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, an offline LSA-secret playbook and 45 victims with live internal pivots, Switzerland among the countries listed. Hunt.io does not report the XML-RPC route used against a victim; PaperCut's documentation names the token and allowlist settings that close it. PaperCut's September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11 as the v24 build.

Corrects four statements: PaperCut says only that Emergency Patch Release 3 addresses two known regressions, not that Release 2 introduced them (the record of 2026-09-03 says it did); the web-log hunt now covers the LogonMessage route watchTowr documents and is cited; Huntress's 47% figure is dated to 28 August; and GreyNoise's twelve domain-admin victims are its count at last observation, not a final tally out of 395. entries.headline: Exchange October updates fix an unauthenticated email-borne RCE; 2016 and 2019 get their last update, and only with ESU
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-70571 +1updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1)

Microsoft's October 2026 Exchange security updates, released on 2026-10-13, fix CVE-2026-70571, a stack-based buffer overflow in Exchange Server: an unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted email to an affected server, triggering an internal content-conversion process, with no user interaction (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Microsoft rates it Critical (CVSS 8.1, high attack complexity) and Exploitation More Likely, and says exploitation requires a deep understanding of the target environment and is not guaranteed to succeed (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). CVE-2026-70279 is a cross-site scripting spoofing flaw (CVSS 9.3, also Exploitation More Likely): an attacker who persuades an administrator to click a crafted link could act with that administrator's privileges (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Microsoft lists neither as exploited or publicly disclosed, and no other source reports exploitation.

The fixed builds are Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM 15.02.2562.056, 2019 CU15 15.02.1748.055, 2019 CU14 15.02.1544.050 and 2016 CU23 15.01.2507.077 (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). The 2016 and 2019 updates are available only to organisations enrolled in the Period 2 ESU program, and October 2026 is the last month those customers receive newly released updates (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13). After October, updates ship for Subscription Edition only, Microsoft's announcements and CVEs stop mentioning 2016 and 2019, and Microsoft says that does not mean those versions are not vulnerable and that it will stop testing them for vulnerabilities (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13); buying Period 2 ESU later only gets an organisation current through this release (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13). Exchange Online customers are already protected (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
On-premises Exchange Subscription Edition, 2019 CU14 and CU15 and 2016 CU23 that receive external mail for CVE-2026-70571, and administrator sessions in the web interfaces for CVE-2026-70279. The update also has to go onto machines that only run the Exchange Management Tools (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13).
Detection
No source describes exploitation behavior. Microsoft says a successful attempt is not guaranteed, so, as an inference from the mechanism, a failed attempt would more likely appear as a crash than a shell: watch for crashes and application-log faults of the Exchange transport processes right after inbound mail from outside, and for unexpected child processes of those processes.
Defender takeaway
Install the October update on every Exchange server and management-tools machine, because Microsoft rates both flaws Exploitation More Likely. An organisation still on Exchange 2016 or 2019 without Period 2 ESU has no update for CVE-2026-70571 and no further updates after this one; the choices are enrolling, which ends at October's release, or moving to Subscription Edition. On an Exchange host that also takes the October Windows Server update, do not uninstall that update: Microsoft says the OWA failures, growing mail queues and lost DAG quorum that can follow are not caused by the Exchange security update, and its workaround is to set the Rpc registry value EpmapSavedContextCap to 65536 and reboot (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).
Improvement16 Oct 2026 04:10 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelsummaryevidencebody

Microsoft's Exchange Team added a banner to its release post on 2026-10-15 saying that the October 2026 Windows Server updates might create issues on Exchange servers and that installing the October 2026 Exchange updates is not required for them (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13).

Update17 Oct 2026 03:36 UTCrun 2026-10-17T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidenceactionsbody

Microsoft's Exchange Team has published guidance for Exchange servers that become unstable after the October 2026 Windows Server updates. Since 2026-10-13 it has seen reports of OWA failing with MapiExceptionMdbOffline (hr=0x80004005, ec=1142; event ID 1006 in the Application log), mail queues growing during the day, DAG members unable to reach quorum and a reboot helping only temporarily; Exchange 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition can all be affected (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17). It says the issues are not related to installing the October 2026 Exchange security updates and that any Exchange version running on an affected Windows build can be hit; KB5126646 (Windows Server 2025), KB5126655 (2022), KB5126651 (2019) and KB5126868 (2016) can cause the failures after some time, and the impact varies with Exchange load, so some servers may never see a problem (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Microsoft's recommendation is not to uninstall the October 2026 Windows Server updates and, from an elevated command prompt on the Exchange server, to set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc to 65536, reboot, monitor, and raise the limit if the problem recurs; it says this has solved the customer cases it has assisted (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Improvement21 Oct 2026 08:21 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-auditbody

On 2026-10-16 Microsoft replaced the release post's 2026-10-15 banner with a link to its dedicated post on Exchange servers that become unstable after the October 2026 Windows Server updates (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-13). That post names the Windows updates, KB5126646 (Windows Server 2025), KB5126655 (Windows Server 2022), KB5126651 (Windows Server 2019) and KB5126868 (Windows Server 2016), gives among the symptoms Exchange OWA failing with the error MapiExceptionMdbOffline (event ID 1006 in the Application log) and mail queues growing, and carries Microsoft's registry workaround (Microsoft Exchange Team, 2026-10-17).

Microsoft's Exchange Team says the October Windows Server updates (KB5126646, KB5126655, KB5126651, KB5126868) can make Exchange servers unstable, with OWA failures, growing mail queues and lost DAG quorum, whether or not the Exchange update is installed; it advises against uninstalling them and on 2026-10-17 gave a registry workaround.

It adds that DAG members losing quorum are among the reported symptoms and that the Exchange security updates are not the cause.

The account of Microsoft's 2026-10-15 notice now cites what each page carries: the release post records the banner and its replacement on 2026-10-16 by a link to a dedicated post, which names the Windows updates and the OWA and mail-queue symptoms. entries.headline: Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 record, rejected on 16 October, reads as restored in ENISA's database; the flaw and its exploitation stand
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-21589exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-21589, Atlassian Data Center: unauthenticated arbitrary file access in every version of eight self-managed products, patch or take them off the internet (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 says every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, and of Crucible and Fisheye, is affected by CVE-2026-21589, an arbitrary file access flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker access specific files within the web application root directory (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). The attacker needs the target file's exact name and path and cannot enumerate or list directory contents, and Atlassian adds that in some configurations sensitive files are present that increase the risk (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). Atlassian's public ticket for Confluence Data Center labels the weakness "Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write)" (Atlassian, 2026-10-02), while the advisory's CVSS 4.0 vector (9.3, Critical: network, low complexity, no privileges, no user interaction) rates the confidentiality impact high and the integrity and availability impact none on the vulnerable system, with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact on subsequent systems (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). Atlassian Cloud is already patched (Atlassian, 2026-10-05), and exploitation attempts have been recorded on honeypot sensors since 2026-10-06 (Previdian, 2026-10-16); CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 "based on evidence of active exploitation" (CISA, 2026-10-15). The Register reports that Atlassian emailed customers on Monday pointing to the advisory (The Register, 2026-10-06). The CVE record for this ID was marked rejected on 2026-10-16 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-16), while Atlassian's advisory still uses the ID and lists the same fixed versions (Atlassian, 2026-10-05).

The fixed versions are Bitbucket Data Center 9.4.26, 10.2.8 and 10.5.1; Confluence Data Center 9.2.26 and 10.2.19; Jira Service Management Data Center 5.12.40, 10.3.26 and 11.3.12; Jira Software Data Center 9.12.40, 10.3.26 and 11.3.12; Bamboo Data Center 10.2.24 and 12.1.12; Crowd Data Center 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7 and 7.2.4; and Crucible and Fisheye 4.9.15 (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). Atlassian's Confluence ticket adds that versions past end of life may also be affected (Atlassian, 2026-10-02), and its Crowd ticket lists the same fixed Crowd builds (Atlassian, 2026-10-02). Until a patch is applied, Atlassian says to remove the instance from the internet where possible, including instances that require user authentication, or to block at a web application firewall or proxy any URL that carries '..' directly next to a slash, backslash or '::' in plain or percent-encoded form; it also gives a Tomcat RewriteValve rule for Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd and a urlrewrite.xml rule for Bitbucket (Atlassian, 2026-10-05).

Exposure
Every self-managed Data Center installation of the eight products on a version below the fixed ones, internet-facing instances first, because Atlassian asks that even instances requiring user authentication be taken off the internet until patched; Atlassian Cloud customers need do nothing (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). Jira instances integrated with Crowd carry a plaintext application password in a configuration file under the readable web root, so a file read can end in administrator access there; watchTowr demonstrated this on Jira only (watchTowr Labs, 2026-10-06).
Detection
Web server and reverse-proxy access logs. Atlassian says to URL-decode each request line (up to two decoding passes) and look for '..' directly next to '/', '\' or '::', or to search the raw lines with its regular expression; it cannot confirm whether any instance was affected and asks customers to check every affected instance for evidence of compromise (Atlassian, 2026-10-05). The public attempts use the paths from watchTowr's write-up: resource-download URLs under the Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket plugin paths with '..::' sequences ahead of a WEB-INF file such as web.xml or urlrewrite.xml, and SANS ISC notes the target file must exist, which is why web.xml, present in every Tomcat application, is the probe of choice (SANS ISC, 2026-10-07). Upgrading does not undo a read of the Crowd credential, so Crowd's own audit records of new users and changed group memberships are the post-patch check for Jira instances integrated with Crowd.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade each affected installation to a fixed version of its line now, internet-reachable ones first, and until each is upgraded keep it off the internet or behind Atlassian's rule; then search the access logs for the exposure period for traversal sequences, rotate the Crowd application password on every Jira instance integrated with Crowd and review Crowd for accounts created since the exposure began, because the flaw's mechanics are public, exploitation attempts have been observed since 2026-10-06, CISA lists the flaw as actively exploited and Atlassian cannot confirm that any instance is unaffected. The CVE record was rejected on 2026-10-16 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-16) and ENISA's database shows it restored on 2026-10-19 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-19), so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets keyed on the ID or on a feed that drops rejected IDs may have stopped reporting the flaw in between: re-run them.
Update07 Oct 2026 04:50 UTCrun 2026-10-07T0404Z-intelheadlinesummarytagstechniquescvessourcesevidenceverificationsourcing_noteclassificationactionsbody

watchTowr Labs published the root cause on 2026-10-06 after comparing a vulnerable and a fixed build of the web-resource library that Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket share: its router converts a double colon in a request path into a slash before it resolves a plugin resource, so a traversal written with double colons leaves the resource directory through a deprecated relative-path resolver that is still reachable (watchTowr Labs, 2026-10-06). watchTowr says it cannot leave the Tomcat context but can read any file within the application server, and it shows working requests against Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket, with Bitbucket blocking one configuration file but not another under WEB-INF (watchTowr Labs, 2026-10-06).

The impact it demonstrates depends on the configuration: where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the crowd.properties file under WEB-INF stores the application name and its password in plaintext, and with those watchTowr reached Crowd's REST interface in its lab, created a user and added it to the Jira administrators group; it adds that a Crowd IP allow-list would make this harder (watchTowr Labs, 2026-10-06). watchTowr also published a Detection Artifact Generator on GitHub that sends the traversal to Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket hosts to test whether they are vulnerable (watchTowr Labs on GitHub, 2026-10-06). Neither watchTowr's post nor Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 reports exploitation in the wild. Atlassian's Crowd ticket lists the same fixed builds as the advisory, 7.1.7 for the 7.1 line (Atlassian, 2026-10-02).

Update08 Oct 2026 04:56 UTCrun 2026-10-08T0404Z-intelheadlinesummarytagstechniquescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Exploitation attempts began on 2026-10-06, the day watchTowr published. Previdian, which runs a honeypot network, told BleepingComputer that its sensors began recording attempts within two hours of that publication, and that a Nuclei template has since been released that makes scanning for vulnerable systems easier; it expects exploitation to rise significantly over the coming days and weeks (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-07). As recorded on 2026-10-08, Previdian's telemetry page showed at least 129 attempts from at least 22 source addresses in eight countries across three sensors, from 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-08, and listed the flaw as not in CISA's KEV catalog (Previdian, 2026-10-08). Its timeline still lists the first sensor observation at 21:55 UTC on 2026-10-06, about five hours after watchTowr's post of 17:01 UTC, which is later than the two-hours figure (Previdian, 2026-10-16; watchTowr Labs, 2026-10-06). The SANS Internet Storm Center says its own honeypots began receiving attempts on 2026-10-06 with the URLs from watchTowr's write-up against Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket resource paths, that every source address belongs to one cloud hosting provider, and that it believes a single actor is behind them (SANS ISC, 2026-10-07).

Neither honeypot operator reports a successful compromise. The Canadian Cyber Centre updated its bulletin on 2026-10-07 to say that open-source reporting indicates the flaw is being exploited in the wild (Canadian Cyber Centre, 2026-10-07), while NCSC Switzerland's advisory, edited on 2026-10-07 to add the public proof of concept, then listed the status as proof of concept available without reporting exploitation (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-07).

Update16 Oct 2026 04:11 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

entries.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's honeypot sensors recorded attempts from dozens of addresses in about twenty countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, without saying what the evidence is. Where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives access to Crowd as an administrator of that application. The record for this ID was marked rejected on 2026-10-16 with only a generic reason and ENISA's database shows it restored with its full description on 2026-10-19, while Atlassian's advisory and fixed versions read unchanged, so tooling keyed on the ID may have dropped the flaw in between.

The flaw moves from a patch-now issue with unpublished mechanics to one with public mechanics and a Crowd credential to rotate; no exploitation is reported. Exploitation attempts began on 2026-10-06, the day watchTowr published its write-up and proof of concept: Previdian's sensors have recorded at least 129 attempts from at least 22 addresses in eight countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts against Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket on its own honeypots, all from one cloud provider, and a Nuclei template exists; the Canadian Cyber Centre's bulletin now cites open-source reporting of in-the-wild exploitation. CISA added CVE-2026-21589 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, which moves the flaw from honeypot-observed attempts to government-confirmed exploitation; CISA names neither the evidence, the actor nor any victim, and neither CISA nor the honeypot operators report a compromise; Previdian's honeypot count has grown to 607 attempts from 65 addresses in 20 countries, and NCSC Switzerland has listed the flaw as actively exploited since 2026-10-12.

entries.classification_html: NATOB1
entries.headline: GTIG: AOMEI update files were altered for minutes at a time to push a backdoor; Switzerland among victim countries
entries.html:
HIGHNATOB1

AOMEI Backupper and AnyViewer update files tampered with for five to ten minutes at a time between April and July 2026 to push the CROSSROAD downloader and the SHINYROAD backdoor, with Switzerland among 11 countries GTIG names

GTIG and Mandiant report that a cluster they track as UNC7017 repeatedly altered two configuration files on AOMEI Technology's update servers between April and July 2026, each time for five to ten minutes before restoring the genuine content; GTIG confirmed three windows and says more probably went unseen (GTIG, 2026-10-16). ManageEngine's Threat Analysis Lab (METAL) writes "There was no CVE, no memory corruption, and no unpatched component." (METAL, 2026-10-16).

The client polls down_html.ini (update archive address and MD5 checksum) and Notifycfg.ini (what to display and run); during a window the actor pointed the first at an attacker-controlled ZIP with a matching checksum and padded the second with more than 35,000 lines of dummy sections, so the client started the unpacked downloader from its html directory, and GTIG describes the same flow for AnyViewer (GTIG, 2026-10-16). METAL's EDR recorded the chain on Backupper 8.3.0 (METAL, 2026-10-16).

The downloader, CROSSROAD, stops in some branches when the host geolocates to China (GTIG, 2026-10-16) and, METAL adds, when specific endpoint security agents are present (METAL, 2026-10-16). It registers a scheduled task that runs a signed Radmin binary every three hours; that binary loads an attacker-built DLL by search-order hijacking, which registers an in-process COM server running the SHINYROAD backdoor as encrypted PocketPy bytecode (GTIG, 2026-10-16). On some hosts GTIG later saw the Adaptix C2 agent, disguised as Nitro PDF tooling and started by hidden PowerShell through a second scheduled task (GTIG, 2026-10-16). The 20 July window also pointed a popup at a remote WebDAV path through an invisible window, which can leak the user's NetNTLMv2 response (GTIG, 2026-10-16).

GTIG's telemetry shows affected IT-services, telecommunications and higher-education organizations in 11 countries including Switzerland and calls the targeting opportunistic; AOMEI told Mandiant on 2026-07-29 that it had taken corrective action (GTIG, 2026-10-16). AOMEI's Backupper release notes through 8.5.0 list no change to update verification as of 2026-10-17 (AOMEI Technology, 2026-10-09).

Exposure
Windows hosts running AOMEI Backupper or AnyViewer that polled for updates during an unseen window between April and July 2026; server-side repair does not clean a host that already ran the downloader (GTIG, 2026-10-16).
Detection
In process telemetry, an executable written into the Tmphtml or html folders and started by the notification process, and a signed Radmin binary loading an unexpected DLL (GTIG, 2026-10-16); METAL adds dllhost.exe hosting a COM component registered from a non-standard path (METAL, 2026-10-16). Also scheduled tasks named RadminComponentRuntime or NitroRuntime, and outbound SMB (TCP 445) and WebDAV to external addresses; hunt the whole April to July span and preserve the cached update files in the Tmphtml folder (GTIG, 2026-10-16).

Triage: do not validate an alert by fetching AOMEI's update address now: the files revert within minutes and the genuine content served then has led analysts to dismiss real detections; the Nitro PDF camouflage can make alerts read as isolated user downloads, so trace each one's parent process back to the updater (GTIG, 2026-10-16). Radmin is legitimate software, so provenance discriminates: METAL's EDR recorded the updater's unsigned child process installing it (METAL, 2026-10-16).

Defender takeaway
Hunt every Windows host that runs AOMEI Backupper or AnyViewer for these artifacts even though AOMEI says its servers are repaired, treat a match as a compromised host, and block outbound SMB and WebDAV to external addresses, which GTIG advises against NTLM credential coercion (GTIG, 2026-10-16).

No software flaw is involved, GTIG names Switzerland among 11 victim countries, and the vendor's server-side repair does not clean a host that already ran the downloader, so installations need an endpoint hunt covering April to July 2026.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Unit 42: a memory-resident FortiGate implant rides an exploited FortiOS flaw that has no fix on 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2025-61624exploitedNATOB2

PEERSTITCH: a memory-resident FortiGate implant installed through the FortiOS CLI path traversal CVE-2025-61624, which Fortinet lists as exploited and leaves unfixed on FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, after a FortiManager compromise exposed the configurations of 500+ firewalls

Unit 42 investigated a September 2024 intrusion at a telecommunications organization, tracked as cluster CL-STA-0954, that began with CVE-2024-47575 against a centralized FortiManager appliance: the attackers registered a rogue virtual FortiGate, then exfiltrated an archive with the running configurations, cryptographic material and database files of more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Unit 42 recovered the configurations' reversible-ciphertext credentials by brute force; the attackers later logged in over SSL VPN with legitimate credentials and pushed packet-capture settings to downstream firewalls (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

For root they used CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal in the FortiOS CLI system.auto-script engine that lets an authenticated administrative account read and write arbitrary files as root (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). That installed PEERSTITCH, an ARM64 injector that attaches with ptrace to the logging daemon miglogd and the IPsec daemon iked, allocates a 16 KB read-write-execute region, NOP-patches three fixed offsets and links the daemons through /proc memory so that tagged VPN sessions skip default FortiOS validation; it leaves no persistent binary on disk, opens no listening port and makes no outbound connection of its own (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Command and control ran through the firewall's own Apache mod_md ACME module, whose DNS-01 challenge handler executes Node.js with parameters from an attacker-run ACME server and so opens a reverse shell (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-122 of 2026-04-14 covers the CLI path traversal in FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager, lists it as known exploited, and for FortiOS gives fixes only in 7.6.5 and 7.4.10, telling users of 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4 to migrate to a fixed release (Fortinet, 2026-04-14).

Exposure
FortiOS on 7.2, 7.0 or 6.4, which have no fixed build, or on 7.6.0 to 7.6.4 and 7.4.0 to 7.4.9, with administrators who can reach the CLI (Fortinet, 2026-04-14); and a FortiManager below 7.6.1, 7.4.5, 7.2.8, 7.0.13, 6.4.15 or 6.2.13 that is reachable on TCP 541 from untrusted networks, where the intrusion began (Fortinet, 2024-10-23; Unit 42, 2026-10-14).
Detection
Management-plane audit records of the FortiManager (device registrations, archive creation, TCP 541 sessions from outside the management network); FortiGate administrator and VPN logs for SSL VPN logins with valid credentials from new external addresses and for administrator accounts that match nobody in the estate, such as an unexpected FortiGateCloud account; gaps in forwarded syslog, because the actors stop the logging daemons before running scripts; and unexplained packet-capture settings (Unit 42, 2026-10-14). Unit 42's hunting guidance adds the memory maps of miglogd and iked (anonymous 16,384-byte rwxp regions), text-segment integrity at three fixed offsets, cross-process open and write on /proc/<pid>/mem, signal-11 crashes of miglogd, iked or syslogd in the crash log, and configuration revisions holding auto-script objects with ../ in the name (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Triage: legitimate FortiManager work also creates and deletes auto-scripts and adds devices; the report's signals are ../ in an auto-script name, a device registered from outside the management network, and accounts that match no administrator or tenant the organization created.

Defender takeaway
Plan the move off FortiOS 7.2, 7.0 and 6.4, where Fortinet offers no fix for an exploited root escalation (Fortinet, 2026-04-14), and limit who can reach the administrative CLI meanwhile; after any suspected FortiManager compromise treat every managed device's credentials and certificates as compromised and rotate them, because the stolen trust material stays valid until it is rotated (Unit 42, 2026-10-14).

Builds on: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds…

entries.action_label: Unit 42: government Linux web and mail hosts hit…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Unit 42: government Linux web and mail hosts hit with PHP prepend persistence, a sudo password trap and mail searches
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

CL-UNK-1211: an AI-assisted intrusion set against government Linux web and mail servers persists through PHP auto_prepend_file, steals sudo passwords with a fake prompt and reads mail stores, and tries to pass as a red-team exercise

Unit 42 reports a campaign it tracks as CL-UNK-1211 (UNK: affiliation undetermined) against government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure between October 2025 and April 2026, concentrating on Linux servers for persistent access and intelligence collection (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). It names no victim or country and does not say how the web shells were first placed; the recovered tools include a custom Go scanner for CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell) (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). The scripts carry conversational, step-by-step comments in the style of an AI model, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work, an inference rather than a confirmed finding (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).

On the hosts, the attackers ran PHP web shells under the php-fpm parent process and rewrote auto_prepend_file in every PHP configuration under /etc/php/ and /opt/plesk/php/, so a planted file runs first (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). They replaced a .bashrc with a copy that, in one instance, aliases sudo to a fake password prompt that logs the input, searched configuration and history files for credentials, escalated with LinPEAS and the public PwnKit exploit (CVE-2021-4034), left root-SUID shells under hidden names and injected an SSH key into authorized_keys (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). They moved laterally with sshpass and hard-coded credentials and through an MSSQL double hop using xp_cmdshell, and kept access with SysGoRAT, a Go trojan that takes commands over WebSocket, plus the revsocks and pysoxy proxies and GSocket's gs-netcat, which ran from /dev/shm under a fake kernel-thread process name (Unit 42, 2026-10-15). On government mail servers they enumerated /var/qmail/mailnames/, counted mails in Maildir folders to pick targets and searched mail headers for social-media messages; they tried to exfiltrate database dumps over netcat and to public file-hosting platforms, to delete authentication, history, mail and system logs and to kill endpoint security processes, timestomped scripts with touch -t, and planted a red-team marker string and a pentest-style password to pass as an authorised exercise (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Linux web and mail hosting estates of government or state-affiliated bodies, in particular Plesk-managed PHP stacks and their /var/qmail/mailnames/ mail directories, which the attackers enumerated and searched; the report does not say how the attackers got in (Unit 42, 2026-10-15).
Detection
From the described behaviour: file-integrity monitoring on PHP configuration directories for any auto_prepend_file that points outside the application tree; shells or interpreters spawned by php-fpm or web server workers; writes to shell startup files, authorized_keys and any new sudo alias; PHP or web-server access to the mail store; new systemd units, five-minute cron entries and hidden-name SUID-root binaries; outbound WebSocket, GSocket or file-hosting connections from servers; touch -t changes, bursts of deleted history and mail logs, and pkill sequences that name EDR agents.

Triage: Plesk or PHP hardening can legitimately set auto_prepend_file and administrators do define sudo aliases; the report supports these discriminators: a prepended file with a vendor-like name outside the application tree, an alias that prompts for and logs the password, a log file named after another product, and red-team marker strings that no change record explains.

Defender takeaway
Audit every PHP configuration for auto_prepend_file, privileged accounts' startup files for a sudo alias and authorized_keys for unknown keys, and the file system for root-SUID binaries under hidden names; ship authentication, mail and web logs off-host so local log cleanup cannot erase them; patch PwnKit and keep Linux EDR self-protection alerting.

Sources: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42
entries.summary: Unit 42 reports CL-UNK-1211, a cluster of unknown nation-state or criminal affiliation that between October 2025 and April 2026 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure, focusing on Linux servers to run reconnaissance and keep persistent access for intelligence collection. Its scripts carry AI-style reasoning comments, which Unit 42 reads as LLM-generated code or an AI agent's work; the intrusions used PHP web shells with auto_prepend_file persistence on Plesk hosts, a replaced .bashrc that traps sudo passwords, SUID root shells, searches of mail directories and log cleanup. Unit 42 names no victim or country, does not say how the web shells were first placed, and is the only source.

entries.action_label: Citizen Lab: spyware delivery through targeted ads…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Citizen Lab: spyware delivery through targeted ads, with defence and government networks among the impressions
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

AdFection: Citizen Lab and Confiant document zero-click Candiru spyware delivered through targeted online ads from the ad-tech firm Discover-Tech, with ad impressions on defence-ministry, armed-forces and NATO networks

Citizen Lab reports that in 2024 and 2025 at least 45 devices at the news network Al Jazeera were targeted in zero-click attacks that it links with high confidence to Candiru spyware delivered through ads bought by Discover-Tech, an Israeli firm that presents itself as an ad company (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). An ad carries a script tag that calls Discover-Tech's ad-decision server with the user's cookie or mobile advertising identifier; the server decides, apparently from the source address and the identifiers, whether the device is eligible, and returns JavaScript only if so and a zero-byte response otherwise, which keeps malicious code and pointers to it out of what ad vendors can inspect (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). In Al Jazeera's network logs an infected device first contacted Discover-Tech infrastructure, which indicates an ad impression, then a Candiru validator server that checks the device, and finally a Candiru command-and-control server; a Windows implant that Al Jazeera isolated from a compromised device and Citizen Lab analysed persists through COM hijacking (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Confiant, working from ad-delivery telemetry from April to September 2026, describes a cloaked payload that fingerprints the device and opens an encrypted channel, and found a hand-off to Candiru-attributed infrastructure, with Belgium by far the most targeted country at 56 percent of the global hits in the period; it has not captured a full exploit chain (Confiant, 2026-10-15).

Citizen Lab's analysis of four billion Discover-Tech bidding records shows ads on almost 200,000 websites and apps in four months, including on devices in networks of defence ministries, armed forces, national cyber agencies and intergovernmental organizations such as NATO; an impression alone does not prove targeting or infection (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle (Liftoff) and Eskimi disconnected Discover-Tech after the disclosure (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Any device that renders third-party ads in a browser or an app, on staff whose phones or workstations an espionage buyer would want, such as defence, security and diplomatic staff; no source reports an infection in Switzerland, and neither report mentions it (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).
Detection
In per-device web-proxy, DNS and egress logs the reported signature is contact with Discover-Tech infrastructure, which marks an ad impression, followed by a connection to a validator server and finally to a command-and-control server, the sequence seen in Al Jazeera's network logs (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15). Confiant adds that the ad-delivered SDK resolves an operator-chosen domain over DNS-over-HTTPS and reaches it by raw IP, so it never appears as a plaintext DNS query or connection hostname and stays invisible to DNS-based monitoring and blocklists (Confiant, 2026-10-15). On a Windows endpoint, the implant Citizen Lab analysed persists through COM hijacking, so a new COM registration that points at an unfamiliar DLL is the artifact to look for.

Triage: ordinary ad tags also call identifier-bearing endpoints and sync user IDs; the reported discriminators are the eligibility gating, with an empty reply for ineligible devices and code only for chosen ones, and the validator-then-command-and-control sequence (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Defender takeaway
The delivery is zero-click and needs no user action, and Citizen Lab says there is currently no consistently safe way to expose users and networks to targeted ads; its control is to block online advertising at the organization's gateway and on work-issued and edge devices (Citizen Lab, 2026-10-15).

Sources: Citizen Lab · Confiant

Citizen Lab's bidding data shows Discover-Tech ads on networks of defence ministries, armed forces, national cyber agencies and NATO, though an impression alone does not prove infection, and neither report mentions Switzerland.

entries.headline: Drupal patches a critical Field UI RCE reachable through contributed modules; uninstall field_ui if you cannot update
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-108097 +1NATOA2

CVE-2026-108097, Drupal core (SA-CORE-2026-014): a critical Field UI code-execution flaw reachable through contributed modules, at least one without login; fixed in 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19, with no fix for end-of-life branches (Drupal risk 19/25)

The Drupal Security Team's advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 of 2026-10-14 rates CVE-2026-108097 Critical, 19 out of 25 on Drupal's own scale, a remote code execution flaw in the core Field UI module: the vulnerability is not directly exploitable with core alone, but multiple serious exploit paths exist with contributed modules and at least one known path needs no authentication (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-14). The advisory names no module that opens a path; The Hacker News reads the mechanism from the fix, where Field UI's table element ran whatever PHP callable each row carried in its #region_callback property through call_user_func_array with no check, bypassing the renderer's rule against untrusted callbacks, and 11.4.10 no longer calls it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Fixed releases are Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and below, 10.5.x and below, and Drupal 8 and 9 are end of life and get no fix, which The Hacker News counts at 28.5 percent of the sites reporting a core version in the week of 2026-10-04 (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). The advisory records no public exploit at publication, but the Security Team's pre-announcement of 2026-10-12 told sites to reserve time "because exploits might be developed within hours or days", and in May Drupal reported exploit attempts within two days of a core SQL injection advisory that CISA then added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). The contributed Entity List module has its own critical code-execution advisory, SA-CONTRIB-2026-218, under the same conditions, at least one known path needing no authentication, and 3.0.10 fixes it (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-14); the flaw is CVE-2026-108099, and updating core does not update the module (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Drupal core on 10.6.x below 10.6.19, 11.3.x below 11.3.19 or 11.4.x below 11.4.10, or on an end-of-life branch from 8.9 to 11.2, with the Field UI module installed (the Standard install profile installs it) and a contributed module or custom code that exposes the vulnerable functionality, which the advisory does not name; Drupal Steward, a web application firewall service run by Acquia, Pantheon, Ironstar and Skpr, blocks some known vectors but not every one (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).
Detection
The advisory publishes no exploit artifact. The result of the flaw is PHP code running as the web server's user, so as an inference from that, watch web access logs for unusual requests to routes that contributed modules provide, PHP worker process lineage for shells, curl or interpreters spawned by the web server, and new or modified PHP files under the web root and the Drupal files directory. An exposed site updated only after the fix was public needs that file-integrity review in addition to the update.
Defender takeaway
Update core to the fixed release of its branch now, internet-facing sites first, because the flaw's mechanism is readable from the public fix and Drupal itself warned that exploits could follow within hours or days; where a site cannot be updated at once, uninstall Field UI, which removes the field management and display admin pages until the update (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15). Custom code that set #region_callback on a field_ui_table row stops working after the update, so test the manage fields and manage display pages (The Hacker News, 2026-10-15).

entries.headline: BeyondTrust patches an exploited Remote Support zero-day; the actor's persistence survives reboot and reset
entries.html:
CRITICALCVE-2026-102764exploitedNATOB1

CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

BeyondTrust's advisory BT26-05 of 2026-10-15 fixes CVE-2026-102764, an improper origin validation (CWE-290) in an internal messaging component of Remote Support that lets a remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance without authenticating; every version up to 26.2.3 is affected (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). Google's Threat Intelligence Group found in an incident response that ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploited the flaw as a zero-day in late August 2026 (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust dates the exploitation of one hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance to 2026-08-29 (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15). GTIG warns that ARMORY CASTLE and others have historically exploited broadly once a flaw is public (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust lists government among the actor's documented targets (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

After the exploit GTIG saw SAWFLY, a lightweight PHP web shell that evaluates attacker-supplied code as the appliance's unprivileged site account; the actor then made a root-owned SUID copy of the system shell, tried to dump the appliance's native secrets vault, and persisted through a boot-time script that adds a passwordless-sudo line to the sudoers template, so the escalation survives reboot and configuration reset (GTIG, 2026-10-15). It deleted appliance logs throughout, raised an account's Jump Item and Team permissions from No Access to Administrator, pulled software inventories from users' desktops through the built-in file transfer, and exposed BARECLAW, a custom SOCKS5-over-WebSocket tunneler, by editing the HAProxy configuration (GTIG, 2026-10-15).

Exposure
Self-hosted Remote Support appliances on any version up to 26.2.3 without the BT26-05-RS patch; the advisory says to apply the patch manually unless the instance is subscribed to automatic updates in its /appliance interface, and a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15), which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure (GTIG, 2026-10-15). SaaS tenants were patched by 2026-10-09 (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust patched Privileged Remote Access too, which shares the code, though it found no way to exploit it (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).
Detection
The actor deletes on-appliance logs, so use other copies: forwarded syslog for user changes that raise a Jump Item or Team role to Administrator and for account or API-account changes without a change ticket; authentication logs for administrative /login success from residential-broadband or commercial-VPN address space; reverse-proxy or WAF logs for unknown .php paths and WebSocket upgrades from non-support addresses; file transfers by accounts whose roles changed (GTIG, 2026-10-15). Patching does not evict the actor, so GTIG advises redeploying any appliance of confirmed or unknown status from a clean, fully patched image and then rotating credentials in dependency order, from the appliance administrators to anything typed into a support session (GTIG, 2026-10-15).

Triage: a known administrator changing Jump Item roles or signing in from a new network under a change ticket is routine; BeyondTrust's signals are privileged sessions from residential or VPN addresses tied to no administrator or ticket (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Defender takeaway
Patch every self-hosted appliance now, then treat each one that was internet-reachable on an affected build since late August as potentially compromised until reviewed, and redeploy from a clean image any whose status is confirmed or unknown (GTIG, 2026-10-15); BeyondTrust adds that the built-in triage tool of its third-party detection platform closed the sensors' privilege-escalation alerts as false positives, and that it is working with the vendor so that automated triage cannot close high-severity signals on its own (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

entries.headline: Adobe fixes unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce; no exploitation known
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-105899 +9updatedNATOA2

Adobe October 2026 bulletins: unauthenticated CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 flaws, most leading to code execution, in ColdFusion (APSB26-144), Experience Manager (APSB26-152) and Commerce and Magento (APSB26-153), none reported exploited

Adobe's 2026-10-13 bulletins put critical fixes into three server products: ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce. Adobe says it is not aware of any exploits in the wild for the ColdFusion issues (Adobe ColdFusion APSB26-144, 2026-10-13). ColdFusion 2025 up to 2025.0.13 and 2023 up to 2023.0.25 are affected and 2025.0.14 and 2023.0.26 fix them; the bulletin lists five network flaws that need no privileges at CVSS 9.0 or above: an unrestricted file upload leading to arbitrary code execution (CVE-2026-105899, 10.0), a server-side request forgery rated privilege escalation (CVE-2026-106622, 10.0), an input-validation flaw leading to code execution (CVE-2026-106624, 9.8), a code injection rated privilege escalation (CVE-2026-106621, 9.1) and a further input-validation code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-106619, 9.0, high complexity), besides code-execution flaws that need a low-privileged account at 9.9 (Adobe ColdFusion APSB26-144, 2026-10-13).

Experience Manager APSB26-152 covers Cloud Service 2026.9.28187 and earlier, 6.5 up to Service Pack 25 and 6.5 LTS up to Service Pack 3: three incorrect-authorization flaws that lead to arbitrary code execution are scored 10.0 with no privileges required (CVE-2026-90532, CVE-2026-48383, CVE-2026-48382), fixed by Cloud Service 2026.9.28386 and, on 6.5 and 6.5 LTS, by per-issue hotfixes, and Adobe is not aware of exploits of these either (Adobe Experience Manager APSB26-152, 2026-10-13). Commerce and Magento APSB26-153 fixes a template-engine injection leading to code execution (CVE-2026-103849, 10.0, which Adobe marks as needing no authentication) and an incorrect-authorization code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-92909, 9.8, which Adobe's note tags B2B) in builds up to the 2026-sep release; the fixes are the 2026-oct builds, Adobe Commerce B2B has its own 2026-oct builds, Magento Open Source gets them for 2.4.9, 2.4.8 and 2.4.7, and Adobe asks customers to apply the CVE-2026-75650 hotfix from its September APSB26-146 update as well, and Adobe is likewise not aware of exploits (Adobe Commerce APSB26-153, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
ColdFusion 2025 and 2023, Experience Manager Cloud Service, 6.5 and 6.5 LTS, and Adobe Commerce or Magento Open Source 2.4.x that untrusted networks can reach; none of the flaws named by CVE id above needs an account.
Detection
Adobe publishes no exploit behavior. As an inference from the flaw classes: after unexpected requests to upload or administrative endpoints, look for new script files in web-accessible directories (the upload flaw), and for outbound requests from the application server to internal addresses (the request forgery).
Defender takeaway
Update internet-facing ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce or Magento instances first, because the flaws need no login and the order is set by exposure; Adobe reports no exploitation as of 2026-10-13. A Composer-installed Commerce or Magento store needs the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch applied explicitly (Sansec, 2026-10-15).
Update16 Oct 2026 04:13 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidenceverificationsourcing_noteactionsbody

Sansec reports that it reproduced four different attack routes to code execution for the Commerce and Magento template-engine flaw CVE-2026-103849 within 24 hours of Adobe's fix and expects threat actors to do the same, and that it has not seen attacks on live stores (Sansec, 2026-10-15). It describes the flaw as a second-pass directive injection like September's StyleSmuggler, where attacker-controlled data in a child template can still be signed and re-scanned at the root level so that a smuggled block directive runs inside Magento's rendering, and says Adobe's October patch replaces that generic re-scan with registered placeholders (Sansec, 2026-10-15). Sansec questions Adobe's priority 2 rating for the Commerce bulletin, a 30-day patch window, because StyleSmuggler went from a priority 1 hotfix to mass exploitation in three days and it judges BlockStrap to be of similar complexity (Sansec, 2026-10-15).

Two cautions for the patch: a plain Composer install still has the vulnerable base version, so the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch must be applied, and BlockStrap and StyleSmuggler are separate fixes, so the September hotfix for CVE-2026-75650 has to stay in place as well (Sansec, 2026-10-15). Sansec lists Adobe Commerce up to 2.4.9, Adobe Commerce B2B up to 1.5.3 and Magento Open Source up to 2.4.9 as affected (Sansec, 2026-10-15).

entries.headline: IDCF Cloud outage: backups now retrievable for 194 of 495 customers; provider finds no trace of server data taken
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA1

IDC Frontier: ransomware stops four zones of IDCF Cloud for 495 companies and local governments; the provider now says its backups are safe and retrievable for 194 customers and that it found no trace of data taken from customers' virtual servers

IDC Frontier says a ransomware attack that began around 3:40 a.m. on 2026-10-07 stopped four zones of IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1, affecting 495 companies and local governments, among them the websites of Ibaraki Prefecture and the city of Kodaira, and has suspended customer management consoles in every region; no source names the actor, the ransomware family or the intrusion route (IDC Frontier, 2026-10-07; IDC Frontier, 2026-10-08; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-08; Jiji Press via nippon.com, 2026-10-07). The lesson is supplier concentration: local governments sat behind one provider whose recovery first depended on copies the customers held, until the fifth report made the provider's own snapshot backups retrievable for 194 of the 495.

Exposure
Customers of IDCF Cloud; IDC Frontier lists IDCF Cloud TypeS and its private-cloud offering as outside the incident (translated from Japanese) (IDC Frontier, 2026-10-08). For any other body, the condition is a website, mail or form service whose hosting and recovery copies depend on one provider.
Defender takeaway
Check where the recovery copies of hosted websites, mail, forms and line-of-business systems live: IDC Frontier first expected restoration only from copies customers hold themselves (IDC Frontier, 2026-10-08), and its own snapshot backups became retrievable for 194 of the 495 customers only a week into the outage (IDC Frontier, 2026-10-14); the attacker's console message claims it wiped 554,153 snapshots, which the provider's report does not confirm (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-08). A copy in the provider's own environment is not one to count on for the recovery window.
Update16 Oct 2026 04:12 UTCrun 2026-10-16T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

IDC Frontier's fifth report of 2026-10-14 says that, with an external security firm, it confirmed the backup data is safe, so the 194 of the 495 affected customers that used its snapshot function can retrieve it, and that it found no trace of customer data in the affected zones being queried or carried out, so it judges that none left those servers, while confirming improper queries of the registration data of 48 customers in its cloud portal with no trace of it being taken (translated from Japanese; IDC Frontier, 2026-10-14). This replaces the third report's expectation that data could be restored only from customers' own backups; the report does not state the intrusion route.
