entries.headline: An unauthenticated SSRF in Cisco Unified CM's WebDialer leads to root; Cisco and CISA confirm exploitation
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-20230exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-20230: Cisco Unified CM WebDialer SSRF to root file write, exploited and KEV-listed; WebDialer is off by default

CVE-2026-20230 (CVSS 8.6) is a server-side request forgery in Cisco Unified Communications Manager and Unified CM Session Management Edition that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker write files and, Cisco says, elevate privileges to root, which is why it rates the advisory Critical (Cisco PSIRT). Only systems with the WebDialer service enabled are affected, and WebDialer is disabled by default; there is no workaround, but disabling WebDialer mitigates until a fix is applied (Cisco PSIRT). Fixed releases are 14SU6 and, for Release 15, 15SU5 (September 2026) or a version-specific COP patch (Cisco PSIRT).

Defused reported exploitation over the weekend before 2026-06-23 from a single IP address, using file:// payloads to create files on the device in what appears to be a check for vulnerable systems; after that disclosure SSD Secure Disclosure, which reported the flaw to Cisco, published a technical write-up and proof-of-concept exploit (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-23). SSD's chain reads the node's true hostname from an unauthenticated WebDialer page, then abuses an unauthenticated cluster-install status endpoint as the SSRF, passing a full path in place of a node hostname to write a file that registers a new web service, and uses that service to write a JSP web shell (SSD Secure Disclosure, 2026-06-23). CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-06-25 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-25), and Cisco updated its advisory on 2026-07-01 to say it became aware of active exploitation in June and that proof-of-concept code is available (Cisco PSIRT).

Exposure
Unified CM or Unified CM SME with the Cisco WebDialer Web Service shown as Started under Control Center Feature Services, on Release 14 before 14SU6 or Release 15 without 15SU5 or the COP (Cisco PSIRT).
Detection
In the Unified CM web tier's access logs, the request sequence of SSD's chain: an unauthenticated GET of /webdialer/Version.jws?wsdl, then /cmplatform/installClusterStatusExecute with action=clusterNodeInstallStatus and a hostname parameter carrying a percent-encoded full path with XML markup instead of a bare node name, then calls to a new service under /webdialer/services/ and to new JSP files under /platform-services/axis2-web/ (SSD Secure Disclosure, 2026-06-23). Also look for requests to the WebDialer service whose parameters carry file:// URLs, the payload form Defused saw in the exploitation, and files created on the appliance that no administrative change accounts for (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-23).
Defender takeaway
Where WebDialer is not needed, disable it now; where it is, apply 14SU6 or the Release 15 COP, and check the appliance for files written outside normal administration since June (Cisco PSIRT) (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-23).

CISA added CVE-2026-20230 to its KEV catalog on 2026-06-25 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-25), and Cisco's advisory revision of 2026-07-01 confirms active exploitation in June and the availability of proof-of-concept code (Cisco PSIRT). Defused's observation came over the weekend before BleepingComputer's report of 2026-06-23 (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-23).

updates.summary: The entry said the flaw was not KEV-listed; CISA added it on 2026-06-25 and Cisco confirmed active exploitation on 2026-07-01. The weekend of Defused's observation preceded 2026-06-23, not 21 and 22 June; the claim that such scanning historically precedes a targeted wave and the Sysmon and auditd guidance for an appliance had no source; and a test file name served as an indicator. entries.headline: An unauthenticated Splunk Enterprise flaw lets attackers write files through the database sidecar, enabled by default on AWS
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-20253exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-20253: Splunk Enterprise unauthenticated file write through the PostgreSQL sidecar chains to RCE, exploited and KEV-listed

CVE-2026-20253 (CVSS 9.8, CWE-306) lets an unauthenticated user create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint in Splunk Enterprise 10.0.0 to 10.0.6 and 10.2.0 to 10.2.3; Splunk fixed it in 10.0.7, 10.2.4 and 10.4.0, and 9.4 and earlier are not affected (Splunk SVD-2026-0603). watchTowr showed how the web tier proxies requests to the sidecar's backup and restore API, listening on 127.0.0.1:5435, and chained the file write into code execution (watchTowr Labs, 2026-06-12). The sidecar is installed and enabled by default on Splunk Enterprise on AWS, and not by default on manually installed Windows systems (watchTowr Labs, 2026-06-12). Splunk's workaround is setting disabled = true in the [postgres] stanza of server.conf and restarting, except on instances using Edge Processor, OpAmp or SPL2 data pipelines, which it would break (Splunk SVD-2026-0603).

Exposure
Splunk Enterprise 10.0.x or 10.2.x below the fixed release with the PostgreSQL sidecar enabled, as on AWS deployments by default (Splunk SVD-2026-0603) (watchTowr Labs, 2026-06-12).
Detection
Web-tier requests to /en-US/splunkd/__raw/v1/postgres/recovery/backup or /restore from clients that have no reason to manage the sidecar, and files written or overwritten by the Splunk service account outside normal upgrades, are the behaviours the chain produces (watchTowr Labs, 2026-06-12).
Defender takeaway
A SIEM host compromised through this flaw loses its value as an evidence source, so a host that ran an affected version with the sidecar enabled since the 2026-06-10 advisory needs a compromise check alongside the upgrade.
Update20 Jun 2026 05:12 UTCrun 2026-06-20-4cfd00efactionscvesevidenceregionssectorssourcestagsbody

Splunk updated its advisory to say its PSIRT became aware of limited exploitation in June 2026 (Splunk SVD-2026-0603), and CISA added CVE-2026-20253 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-06-18 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-18). SecurityWeek reported the exploitation days after disclosure (SecurityWeek, 2026-06-19). The fixes have been available since the advisory of 2026-06-10 (Splunk SVD-2026-0603).

Correction11 Oct 2026 14:51 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarysectorstechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceclassificationactionsbody

The fixes date from 2026-06-10, and Splunk's interim measure is disabling the PostgreSQL sidecar in server.conf, not restricting search-job submission (Splunk SVD-2026-0603). entries.headline: Cisco fixes an admin-to-root command flaw across ISE releases up to 3.5 and an unauthenticated credential-hash leak in 3.4 and 3.5; no exploitation known
entries.html:
ROUTINECVE-2026-20181 +1updatedNATOA2

Cisco ISE CVE-2026-20181 / CVE-2026-20190: administrator-level command execution to root and an unauthenticated disclosure of hashed credentials, two independent flaws

Cisco's advisory of 2026-06-17 covers two independent flaws in Identity Services Engine and ISE-PIC; Cisco states that exploiting one is not required to exploit the other (Cisco PSIRT). CVE-2026-20181 (CVSS 9.1, SIR Critical) lets an attacker with valid administrative credentials send a crafted HTTP request that gives user-level access to the underlying operating system and then root; on a single-node deployment it can also take the node down (Cisco PSIRT). It affects releases 3.1 to 3.5, and Cisco tells releases earlier than 3.1 to migrate to a fixed release; it is fixed in 3.3 Patch 11, 3.4 Patch 6, 3.5 Patch 4 or a hot patch for 3.5 Patch 3, with 3.1 Patch 12 and 3.2 Patch 11 scheduled for September 2026 (Cisco PSIRT). CVE-2026-20190 (CVSS 7.5, SIR High) lets an unauthenticated attacker read sensitive information, including hashed credentials, through improper authorization checks; it affects only 3.4 and 3.5, fixed in 3.4 Patch 6 and 3.5 Patch 3 (Cisco PSIRT). Cisco knows of no public announcements or malicious use, and lists no workarounds (Cisco PSIRT). SecurityWeek and CERT-Bund relayed the advisory (SecurityWeek, 2026-06-18) (CERT-Bund WID-SEC-2026-1989).

Exposure
ISE or ISE-PIC 3.4 or 3.5 below the fixed patch is exposed to the unauthenticated disclosure; every release is exposed to the administrator-level command execution until its patch, releases earlier than 3.1 until they migrate to a fixed release (Cisco PSIRT).
Defender takeaway
The unauthenticated flaw leaks hashed credentials on 3.4 and 3.5, so patch those trains first and treat ISE administrator credentials as the control that keeps CVE-2026-20181 out of reach (Cisco PSIRT).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:53 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarytechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesclassificationdeep_divedeep_dive_categorybodypriorityregionssectorsevent_date

Cisco states that the two vulnerabilities are not dependent on one another (Cisco PSIRT); the earlier chain of a credential leak feeding root execution was not in any source. CVE-2026-20181 requires valid administrative credentials and affects releases 3.1 to 3.5, with releases earlier than 3.1 told to migrate to a fixed release, with a hot patch available for 3.5 Patch 3, and CVE-2026-20190 discloses information including hashed credentials (Cisco PSIRT). The priority moves from notable to routine: Cisco reports no public announcements or malicious use, and the update is a patch-cycle item.

entries.headline: Check Point IKEv1 VPN auth bypass exploited since 7 May, actor assessed with medium confidence to use Qilin. CISA KEV, public PoC, apply sk185033
entries.html:
CRITICALCVE-2026-50751 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-50751: Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 VPN authentication bypass, actively exploited, actor assessed with medium confidence to use Qilin ransomware

Check Point disclosed and patched CVE-2026-50751 (CVSS 9.3) on 8 June 2026. It is a logic-flow weakness in certificate validation in the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange affecting Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access deployments. An unauthenticated remote attacker can establish a VPN session without a valid user password; post-authentication activity is still required to reach internal resources (Check Point, 2026-06-08). Check Point has observed exploitation since 7 May against a few dozen targeted organizations, with one case showing confirmed post-compromise activity associated with a Qilin ransomware affiliate. Based on the post-exploitation activity it observed, Check Point assesses with medium confidence that the actor behind the exploitation is financially motivated and uses Qilin ransomware (Check Point, 2026-06-08). NCSC-CH issued an advisory the same day flagging the CVE as actively exploited and linking observed exploitation to a Qilin ransomware affiliate (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-08); CISA added the CVE to its KEV catalog on 8 June (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-08). The companion CVE-2026-50752 (CVSS 7.4, site-to-site IKEv1 MitM under specific conditions, no observed exploitation) should be patched in the same window.

Exposure
Remote Access VPN, Mobile Access / SSL VPN and Spark Firewall on R80.20.X through R82.10, of which R80.20.X, R80.40, R81 and R81.10 are end of support and need migration (Rapid7, 2026-06-08) (Check Point, 2026-06-08), where the deployment uses the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange, accepts legacy Remote Access clients and does not require a machine certificate for connections (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-08).
Detection
In the gateway's VPN logs, Check Point's hunt is a completed IKEv1 Quick Mode exchange (a "Key Install" event marked Quick Mode completion) recorded before the hotfix or mitigation went in, searched over at least 7 May to 5 June 2026 (Check Point, sk185033); Check Point dates the earliest observed exploitation to 7 May and advises forensic log audits and configuration reviews from then (Check Point, 2026-06-08). After access it saw attempts to download Linux ELF files from actor-controlled infrastructure, so outbound fetches of executables from a gateway or from hosts behind a newly established remote-access session are the post-exploitation signal (Check Point, 2026-06-08). Its IPS protection for the public proof-of-concept adds visibility into attack attempts and scanning, but it is not a remediation (Check Point, sk185033).

Triage: Check Point says to treat every completed Quick Mode exchange recorded before the fix as suspicious, and the discriminator it gives is a user or source IP address the organisation does not recognise (Check Point, sk185033).

Defender takeaway
Apply hotfix sk185033 (Check Point, 2026-06-08). Until it is in, NCSC-CH lists temporary mitigations: remove support for the legacy remote access client, set Remote Access VPN authentication to IKEv2 only, enforce mandatory machine certificate authentication, and enable IPS with updated signatures (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-08).
Update17 Jun 2026 05:14 UTCrun 2026-06-17-e102009cactionscvesregionssectorssourcestagsbody

entries.headline: Defused reports exploitation of three pre-auth FortiSandbox flaws and CISA lists two in KEV; upgrading to 5.0.6 or 4.4.9 fixes all three
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-25089 +2exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-25089, Fortinet FortiSandbox: unauthenticated OS command injection in the web UI's VNC-launch handler (CVSS 9.8 base)

Fortinet patched CVE-2026-25089 (CWE-78) on 2026-06-09: the FortiSandbox web interface's "start vnc" feature passes attacker-controlled JSON input to an OS command, a second-order injection that "may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests" (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09). Affected are FortiSandbox 5.0.0 through 5.0.5 and 4.4.0 through 4.4.8 plus FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS 5.0.4 through 5.0.5; the fix is 5.0.6 or 4.4.9, and the 5.2 branch is not affected (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09). CCB Belgium urged immediate patching and warned that a public proof-of-concept raises the likelihood of exploitation (CCB Belgium, 2026-06-11).

The same upgrade closes two April flaws that Defused reported under attack alongside it. CVE-2026-39813 is a path traversal in the JRPC API that lets an unauthenticated attacker bypass authentication on 5.0.0 through 5.0.5 and 4.4.0 through 4.4.8 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-112, 2026-04-14). CVE-2026-39808 is an OS command injection through an API endpoint that gives an unauthenticated attacker command execution on 4.4.0 through 4.4.8, with 5.0 not affected (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-100, 2026-04-14). Fortinet's three advisories give all three flaws the same CVSS 3.1 vector, which scores 9.8 before the temporal adjustment behind the 9.1 they display (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-112, 2026-04-14) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-100, 2026-04-14). No exploitation was reported as of the 2026-06-09 disclosure. Defused then reported attacks on all three, and Help Net Security noted Fortinet had not yet confirmed them (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16). CISA added CVE-2026-25089 and CVE-2026-39808 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-07-16 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-07-16), while Fortinet's three advisories list none of the flaws as known exploited (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-112, 2026-04-14) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-100, 2026-04-14).

Help Net Security describes FortiSandbox as a platform that other Fortinet security products depend on for threat verdicts to enforce blocking decisions and trigger automated responses (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16).

Contradiction: CCB Belgium says a publicly available proof-of-concept exploit raises the likelihood of exploitation (CCB Belgium, 2026-06-11), while Security Affairs reports that a working exploit for CVE-2026-25089 has not been publicly disclosed and that the exploit seen in attacks appears AI-assisted and bugged (Security Affairs, 2026-06-16).

Exposure
FortiSandbox 4.4.0 through 4.4.8 carries all three flaws, 5.0.0 through 5.0.5 carries CVE-2026-25089 and CVE-2026-39813, and FortiSandbox Cloud or PaaS 5.0.4 through 5.0.5 carries CVE-2026-25089. NCSC-NL's advisory on CVE-2026-25089 covers FortiSandbox versions 4.2 through 5.0.5 (NCSC-NL, 2026-06-11), which Fortinet's advisory table does not (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09), so a 4.2 installation should be treated as exposed. Any affected build whose web UI or JRPC API is reachable beyond the management network is exposed.
Detection
Review FortiSandbox web UI and JRPC API access logs for unauthenticated HTTP requests from outside the management network, especially to the VNC-launch function. After patching, check for administrator accounts, configuration changes and verdict settings nobody can account for, since the upgrade does not remove access gained before it.
Defender takeaway
Two of the three flaws are in CISA KEV and one upgrade fixes all of them, so an unpatched FortiSandbox is an exploited hole in the security stack itself and belongs in an emergency change, not the next maintenance window.
Update17 Jun 2026 05:14 UTCrun 2026-06-17-e102009cactionscvesevidenceprioritysectorssourcestagsbody

Threat-intelligence firm Defused Cyber reported active exploitation of three FortiSandbox flaws within a 24-hour window: CVE-2026-39813 (CVSS 9.1), a JRPC API path traversal that allows authentication bypass, and CVE-2026-39808 (CVSS 9.8), an OS command injection, both patched in April 2026, and CVE-2026-25089, the web UI command injection patched on 2026-06-09 (Security Affairs, 2026-06-16). Defused researchers speculate that the CVE-2026-25089 exploit was built with AI assistance and is bugged, yet attackers are still using it against unpatched systems (Security Affairs, 2026-06-16).

Help Net Security describes FortiSandbox as a platform that other Fortinet security products depend on for threat verdicts to enforce blocking decisions and trigger automated responses, and notes that Fortinet had not yet confirmed in-the-wild exploitation (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16).

Correction30 Sep 2026 06:49 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-auditheadlinesummarytechniquesaffected_productscvesevidenceactionssourcesbodyclassificationentitiestags

The earlier main text said no in-the-wild exploitation was reported, treated a public proof-of-concept as established and carried a table of unrelated CVEs. Defused reported exploitation of all three flaws, which Fortinet had not confirmed (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16), and Fortinet's advisories list them as not known exploited (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-112, 2026-04-14) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-100, 2026-04-14). CISA added CVE-2026-25089 and CVE-2026-39808 to its KEV catalog on 2026-07-16 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-07-16). Fortinet's advisories give the affected and fixed versions. For CVE-2026-25089 and CVE-2026-39813, 5.0.0 through 5.0.5 and 4.4.0 through 4.4.8 are affected, 5.0.6 or 4.4.9 fixes them and 5.2 is not affected (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09) (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-112, 2026-04-14). For CVE-2026-39808, 4.4.0 through 4.4.8 is affected, 4.4.9 fixes it and 5.0 is not affected (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-100, 2026-04-14). Sources disagree on whether a public proof-of-concept exists (CCB Belgium, 2026-06-11) (Security Affairs, 2026-06-16). The 2026-06-17 text said FortiSandbox feeds verdicts to FortiGate, FortiMail, FortiProxy and FortiClient and that a compromised sandbox can suppress detection across that stack, while the cited report says only that other Fortinet security products depend on its verdicts (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16). CVE-2026-39813 was listed at CVSS 9.1 next to 9.8 for the other two. Fortinet gives all three the same vector, which scores 9.8 before the temporal adjustment behind the 9.1 on its advisories (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-112, 2026-04-14).

Correction11 Oct 2026 14:01 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitlesourcesactionsbody

Contradiction: NCSC-NL says Fortinet fixed the flaw in FortiSandbox versions 4.2 through 5.0.5 (NCSC-NL, 2026-06-11), while Fortinet's advisory lists 4.4.0 through 4.4.8 and 5.0.0 through 5.0.5 as affected and does not mention 4.2 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09). Operators still on 4.2 should assume exposure and move to 4.4.9 or later.

entries.headline: An SD-WAN Manager user with write access can overwrite any file; Cisco confirms limited exploitation
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-20262exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-20262: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authenticated arbitrary file write, exploited and KEV-listed; Cisco says a written file could later be used to gain root

CVE-2026-20262 (CVSS 6.5) is an arbitrary file write in the web UI of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager: the software does not properly validate user-supplied input during a file upload, so an authenticated attacker with at least write access can create or overwrite any file on the system, which Cisco says can later be used to gain root; it affects all deployment types and has no workaround (Cisco PSIRT). Cisco found it in internal testing and became aware of limited exploitation in June 2026 (Cisco PSIRT); CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-06-15 as a path traversal (CWE-22) (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-15). BleepingComputer reports that Cisco shared no details of the attacks (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-15). First fixed releases are 20.9.9.2, 20.12.7.2, 20.15.4.5, 20.15.5.3, 20.18.3.1 and 26.1.1.2 (Cisco PSIRT), the same first fixed releases Cisco lists for CVE-2026-20245, the netadmin-to-root command injection it disclosed on 2026-06-04 (Cisco PSIRT, CVE-2026-20245 advisory).

Exposure
SD-WAN Manager below the first fixed release for its train, where an attacker holds or can obtain an account with write access; Cisco says Managers exposed to the internet, with ports exposed to the internet, are at risk (Cisco PSIRT).
Detection
In /var/log/nms/vmanage-server.log, a SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler entry for an uploaded Remote Access AnyConnect profile file whose path climbs with ../ into the WildFly deployments directory /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/ and names a .war archive, which Cisco treats as a possible initial compromise vector; as follow-on activity that is not always logged, a WFLYSRV0010 deployment line for that archive in /var/log/nms/vmanage-appserver.log and POST requests to a JSP page of the new application in /var/log/nms/containers/service-proxy/serviceproxy-access.log (Cisco PSIRT). Cisco notes these entries can occur in standard operations and must be assessed against normal posture; run request admin-tech on each control component before opening a TAC case (Cisco PSIRT).
Defender takeaway
With exploitation confirmed for an authenticated flaw, accounts with write access to SD-WAN Manager are the attack surface: upgrade, then review who holds such accounts and check for unexpected web application deployments (Cisco PSIRT).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:52 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarysourcing_noteentitiestechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceclassificationdeep_divedeep_dive_categorybody

Cisco's indicators place the planted web application in the application server's deployments directory and record it as a .war deployment (Cisco PSIRT); the earlier text named Tomcat. No cited source attributes exploitation of CVE-2026-20262 to UAT-8616, and Cisco shared no details of the attacks (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-15).

Improvement21 Oct 2026 12:09 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1149Z-auditsourcesreferencesbody

Cisco's indicators name the exact log entries: in /var/log/nms/vmanage-server.log, a SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler upload whose path climbs into the WildFly deployments directory /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/ with a .war archive, followed, though not always, by a WFLYSRV0010 deployment line in vmanage-appserver.log and POST requests to the new application's JSP page in the service-proxy access log; Cisco also says Managers with ports exposed to the internet are at risk (Cisco PSIRT). CISA lists the flaw as a path traversal (CWE-22) (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-15). Its first fixed releases are the same as for CVE-2026-20245, disclosed on 2026-06-04 (Cisco PSIRT, CVE-2026-20245 advisory).

entries.headline: One unauthenticated request yields a session as any phpBB user on default boards, and only an upgrade fixes it
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-48611 +1updatedNATOB2

CVE-2026-48611 / CVE-2026-48612: phpBB authentication bypass gives a session as any user from one unauthenticated request, plus an OAuth account-link CSRF

phpBB 3.3.17, released on 2026-06-06, fixes two authentication flaws disclosed by Pentest-Tools.com (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). CVE-2026-48611 (CVSS 9.4 per Pentest-Tools) lets a single unauthenticated POST to the user control panel's login-link handler with auth_provider=apache route the login through phpBB's Apache provider, which checks only that the HTTP Basic username matches and that the password is non-empty, never comparing the password with the stored hash, and returns a valid session as any active user on default installations (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). The CVE record, assigned by HackerOne as numbering authority, scores it CVSS 3.0 9.8 and describes improper authentication checks in phpBB's OAuth implementation that allow account hijacking even when OAuth is not configured or enabled (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-12); heise reports the same 9.8 (heise online, 2026-06-15). A known username is enough, and a default board's public member list supplies it (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). Sources disagree on whether the session also reaches the Administration Control Panel. Pentest-Tools first wrote that the panel's separate password prompt stops the attacker, then added on 2026-06-15 that an attacker can in fact directly access the panel after impersonating an administrator (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). Aikido says a password check in front of the panel cannot be bypassed, which is why it rules out direct remote code execution even through the Extension Catalog (Aikido Security, 2026-06-10). Aikido reported the flaw to phpBB on 2026-06-02 and says it affects every version up to 3.3.16 and 4.0.0-a2 (Aikido Security, 2026-06-10), and heise reports that Aikido and Pentest-Tools' researcher found it independently (heise online, 2026-06-15).

CVE-2026-48612 (CVSS 8.3 per Pentest-Tools; 8.0 under CVSS 3.0 in its CVE record (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-12), the score heise reports (heise online, 2026-06-15)) affects only boards where an administrator has enabled OAuth login with a Google, Facebook or Bitly provider. Missing OAuth state validation and a missing CSRF check on the account-link endpoint let an attacker bind their own identity-provider account to a logged-in victim who opens a crafted link, which gives the attacker a permanent OAuth login to the victim's account (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). Pentest-Tools added proof-of-concept requests for both flaws to its write-up on 2026-07-04 (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog as of 2026-09-29 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-09-29).

Exposure
Every phpBB board before 3.3.17 that uses the default database authentication, and 4.0.0-a2, is exposed to CVE-2026-48611, public boards most directly because their member list names the targets. CVE-2026-48612 needs OAuth authentication enabled (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08).
Detection
Web access logs showing POST requests to the login-link mode of ucp.php with auth_provider=apache and an HTTP Basic Authorization header. After patching, audit the phpbb_oauth_accounts table for identity-provider links users did not create (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08).

Triage: the bypass works by forcing the Apache provider instead of the configured one (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08), so on a board that uses database authentication, a login request naming the Apache provider is the exploit path, not a misconfigured client.

Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 3.3.17, the only complete fix, since no configuration change closes CVE-2026-48611 (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). A board with OAuth enabled that cannot upgrade at once can disable OAuth and switch to database authentication to remove CVE-2026-48612 (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08).
Correction30 Sep 2026 07:18 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-auditcvesbodyclassificationtechniquestitleheadlinesummarytagsregionssectorssourcesactions

The main text above gave CVE-2026-48611 only the 9.8 score, said no public exploit code existed and advised disabling OAuth as a stop-gap, although the flaw is reachable even where OAuth is not configured or enabled (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-12). Pentest-Tools.com scores it 9.4 and shows a single unauthenticated request through phpBB's Apache authentication provider that yields a valid session as any active user, administrators included, on default installations of phpBB 3.3.16 and earlier, fixed in 3.3.17 with no configuration workaround. It published proof-of-concept requests on 2026-07-04 (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). Pentest-Tools is one of two independent discoverers, with Aikido (heise online, 2026-06-15). CVE-2026-48612 needs OAuth enabled and a victim who opens a crafted link, and it binds the attacker's OAuth identity to the victim's account rather than hijacking a session (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). Disabling OAuth helps only against CVE-2026-48612. No cited source says phpBB is common at European universities or municipalities.

The CVSS 9.8 for CVE-2026-48611 and 8.0 for CVE-2026-48612 that heise reports are the CVE records' own CVSS 3.0 scores, assigned by HackerOne as numbering authority (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-12; ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-12); Pentest-Tools.com, which found both flaws, scores them 9.4 and 8.3 (Pentest-Tools.com, 2026-06-08). entries.headline: CVE-2026-54420: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin root escalation on CloudLinux/CageFS shared hosting, exploited in the wild (CISA KEV)
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-54420exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-54420: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin root escalation on CloudLinux/CageFS shared hosting, exploited in the wild (CISA KEV)

The LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin before 2.4.8, bundled with the LiteSpeed WHM PlugIn and fixed in WHM PlugIn version 5.3.2.1, lets a user with FTP or web-shell access on a CloudLinux/CageFS shared-hosting server escalate to root. LiteSpeed says its WHM plugin itself was not affected, that the flaw "is being actively exploited", and that it was alerted on 2026-05-31 (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01). The CVE description attributes the flaw to mishandled symlinks (The Hacker News, 2026-06-16) and dates its exploitation in the wild to May 2026 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-14); LiteSpeed thanks cPanel, which pushed an uninstall command for the user-end plugin on 2026-05-31, for preventing further exploitation on additional servers (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01). The Hacker News lists a CVSS score of 8.5 (The Hacker News, 2026-06-16). The CVE description places the vulnerable plugin in WHM PlugIn releases before 5.3.2.0 (The Hacker News, 2026-06-16), while LiteSpeed names WHM PlugIn 5.3.2.1 as its fixed release; both put the user-end plugin fix at 2.4.8 (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01). CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-06-15 (CISA, 2026-06-15).

Exposure
Shared-hosting servers running CloudLinux/CageFS with any LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin version before 2.4.8, where a user with FTP or web-shell access can escalate to root (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01).
Detection
LiteSpeed's check searches the cPanel logs for generateEcCert and packageUserSize API calls, and where it matches, LiteSpeed advises examining the system logs for actions taken by the detected source IPs (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01). With exploitation dated to May 2026 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-14), the check belongs on every server that ran a user-end plugin before 2.4.8, upgraded ones included, since the upgrade does not undo a root escalation that already happened.

Triage: a match can be a false positive. LiteSpeed's discriminators are generateEcCert immediately followed by packageUserSize for the same user, which legitimate UI flows do not chain, 7 to 10 concurrent calls per attempt where the legitimate UI makes one at a time, and the same source IP hammering both endpoints (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01).

Defender takeaway
Upgrade to LiteSpeed WHM Plugin 5.3.2.1 (bundled with cPanel plugin 2.4.8) or later, or remove the user-end plugin until the upgrade is possible (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01), then run the log check on every server that ran an earlier version.

It says only its user-end cPanel plugin is affected, not its WHM plugin, and gives 2026-05-31 as the date it was alerted; the CVE record dates the exploitation itself to May 2026 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-14). The 8.5 score is now cited to The Hacker News (The Hacker News, 2026-06-16).

The CVE record for CVE-2026-54420 says the flaw was exploited in the wild in May 2026 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-06-14). entries.headline: Year-old WinRAR flaw (CVE-2025-8088) still fuels Ukraine intrusions: GIFTEDCROOK via UAC-0226 and an Earth Dahu chain
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2025-8088exploitedupdatedNATOB2

Year-old WinRAR flaw (CVE-2025-8088) still fuels Ukraine intrusions: GIFTEDCROOK via UAC-0226 and an Earth Dahu chain

Trend Micro documents two Russia-aligned campaigns still exploiting CVE-2025-8088, a path traversal via NTFS Alternate Data Streams in WinRAR patched in July 2025, nearly a year after the fix (Trend Micro, 2026-06-08). SHADOW-EARTH-066 (UAC-0226) delivers GIFTEDCROOK via crafted RAR archives with decoy PDFs and hidden ADS payloads that extract to the Startup folder and run in-memory PowerShell DLL loaders to steal passwords, cookies and documents from Chrome, Edge, Opera and Firefox; a separate Earth Dahu chain uses an HTA-to-VBScript dropper (The Hacker News, 2026-06-09). SHADOW-EARTH-066 moved exfiltration from Telegram to dedicated command-and-control servers, a change The Hacker News says likely aligns with Russia's blocking of the platform (The Hacker News, 2026-06-09).

Exposure
WinRAR installations before 7.13, the July 2025 release that fixed CVE-2025-8088 (CVSS 8.4); Trend Micro notes that WinRAR is not covered by Group Policy or centralized update mechanisms (Trend Micro, 2026-06-08).
Detection
Trend Micro's monitoring list: cmd.exe launching hidden PowerShell with an execution-policy bypass that reads from C:\ProgramData, PowerShell allocating executable memory (kernel-level telemetry), and mshta.exe running from the Startup folder (Trend Micro, 2026-06-08).
Defender takeaway
The exploited entry point persists in software outside central patching, so inventory applications that do not receive patches through standard update channels, WinRAR among them, and bring them to current versions (Trend Micro, 2026-06-08).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:55 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-auditreferencestechniquesclassificationevidenceverificationsourcing_notebodyentitiescves

Only SHADOW-EARTH-066 is reported to have moved exfiltration from Telegram to dedicated command-and-control servers, and The Hacker News says the change likely aligns with Russia's blocking of the platform rather than stating it as the cause (The Hacker News, 2026-06-09). The hunting guidance now follows Trend Micro's own monitoring list, and the entry states the fixed release, WinRAR 7.13 from July 2025 (Trend Micro, 2026-06-08).

entries.headline: NCSC-CH Week 23: three job-seeker scams, a fake interview login, reshipping identity theft and LinkedIn-to-GitHub infostealer delivery
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

NCSC-CH Week 23: three job-seeker scams, a fake interview login, reshipping identity theft and LinkedIn-to-GitHub infostealer delivery

NCSC Switzerland's Week 23 review (9 June) walks through three reported cases aimed at job seekers (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09). In the first, a job seeker was offered a phone-interview slot to confirm through a Google Calendar entry, and the confirmation opened a counterfeit Google login that sent the entered credentials to the scammers. In the second, an ad for a "Swiss social welfare" work-from-home packing job moved to WhatsApp and asked for photos of the passport, identity card, driving licence and home address. Such documents are used to order high-value goods in the victim's name, and the job itself is parcel reshipping that hides criminal proceeds. In the third, a recruiter on LinkedIn, in one case writing from a compromised but genuine-looking profile, offered a technical position and, as part of a technical interview, asked the candidate to download a private GitHub repository and complete a small programming task in it. Running the commands installed an infostealer that reads crypto wallets, stored login credentials and browser cookies. NCSC notes that attackers systematically exploit applicants' willingness to react quickly and engage with unfamiliar procedures.

Exposure
Job seekers, and in the third case an IT professional approached on LinkedIn about a technical position, in a similar case from a compromised but genuine-looking profile (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09). In analyst judgement an employee in job-search mode who runs such a task on a work device brings the infostealer into the corporate estate, and NCSC notes that the incident becomes particularly serious where sensitive documents are stored on the device (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09).
Detection
By inference from the mechanism, process-creation telemetry with parent lineage showing a freshly downloaded or cloned repository followed within minutes by script or interpreter execution from that path (for example Sysmon event 1 with git or an interpreter as the parent), then a non-browser process reading browser credential and cookie stores or crypto-wallet files, the data NCSC says the infostealer took (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09).

Triage: downloading a repository and running its commands is common in IT work, which is why the step raised no suspicion (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09); by inference from the mechanism, the discriminators are the repository's origin, a private repository handed over by an external recruiter during an interview, and what follows execution, reads of credential, cookie or wallet stores by a process that is not the browser.

Defender takeaway
Treat a device on which the interview task ran as having lost its stored login credentials, browser cookies and crypto wallets, the data the infostealer reads (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09): revoke the sessions and rotate every credential stored on it, not only the password the user typed, since a stolen cookie carries a live session.
Correction30 Sep 2026 06:43 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0634Z-auditsourcestechniquesclassificationtitleheadlinesummarysectorsbody

NCSC Switzerland's Week 23 review presents three reported cases, not a coordinated campaign (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09). The fake interview was a phone-interview slot confirmed through a Google Calendar entry, which opened a counterfeit Google login. The recruiter case was a technical interview in which the candidate downloaded a private GitHub repository and ran a small programming task, and running its commands installed the infostealer. The analysis had described interview-confirmation emails from Swiss employers, an onboarding or technical-assessment repository and PowerShell, which the page does not say, and it now follows the page. The citation now points at the page's new address on bacs.admin.ch, after the old ncsc.admin.ch page went dead.

Improvement21 Oct 2026 08:21 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-auditbodytechniques

Downloading a repository and running its commands is common in IT work, which is why the interview task raised no suspicion; once run, the infostealer secretly reads crypto wallets, stored login credentials and browser cookies, and NCSC notes the incident becomes particularly serious where sensitive documents are stored on the device (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-09). A device where the task ran should therefore be treated as having lost its stored credentials and live sessions, and the sessions need revoking along with the passwords.

entries.headline: CVE-2026-42271, BerriAI LiteLLM: low-privilege command injection to host RCE, added to CISA KEV
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-42271 +1exploitedupdatedNATOB1

CVE-2026-42271, BerriAI LiteLLM: low-privilege command injection to host RCE, added to CISA KEV

CISA added CVE-2026-42271 to its KEV catalog on 8 June 2026, confirming active exploitation of a command-injection flaw in LiteLLM, the open-source AI gateway/proxy (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-08) (GitHub Advisory GHSA-v4p8-mg3p-g94g). Two preview endpoints, POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list, accept a full MCP server configuration (command, args, env) in the request body; with stdio transport, the proxy spawns the supplied command on the host under the proxy's privileges. The endpoints were gated only by a valid API key with no role check, so any authenticated user (including low-privilege internal keys) could execute arbitrary commands. Horizon3.ai documents that chaining with CVE-2026-48710 (a Starlette Host-header validation bypass) makes the path unauthenticated (Horizon3.ai, 2026-06-01). Affected: LiteLLM 1.74.2 to < 1.83.7; fixed in 1.83.7, which adds role-based authorization on the MCP test endpoints.

Exposure
LiteLLM 1.74.2 through 1.83.6, fixed in 1.83.7; deployments whose dependency tree includes Starlette 1.0.0 or earlier are reachable without authentication through the CVE-2026-48710 Host-header bypass (Horizon3.ai, 2026-06-01).
Detection
In process telemetry on the proxy host, subprocesses spawned by LiteLLM; in HTTP logs, requests to /mcp-rest/test/connection and /mcp-rest/test/tools/list and unusual Host header values (Horizon3.ai, 2026-06-01).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade LiteLLM to 1.83.7 or later and Starlette to 1.0.1 or later (Horizon3.ai, 2026-06-01); where that cannot happen at once, block the two test endpoints at the reverse proxy or API gateway (GitHub Advisory GHSA-v4p8-mg3p-g94g) and rotate the credentials the proxy stores (Horizon3.ai, 2026-06-01).

entries.headline: Attackers turned an Everest Forms Pro code-injection flaw, patched in March, into rogue admin accounts on WordPress sites
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-3300exploitedupdatedNATOB2

CVE-2026-3300: unauthenticated code execution in Everest Forms Pro exploited since April to create rogue WordPress administrators, fixed in March

CVE-2026-3300 (CVSS 9.8) is an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Everest Forms Pro, a commercial WordPress plugin with about 4,000 active installations, which Wordfence disclosed on 2026-03-30 after the vendor shipped the fix on 2026-03-18 (Wordfence, 2026-06-03). Attacker input reaches PHP evaluation through the plugin's calculation feature; the most common payload Wordfence sees closes a string literal and calls wp_insert_user() to create an administrator account (Wordfence, 2026-06-03). Attacks began on 2026-04-13 and peaked on 2026-05-16, when Wordfence blocked more than 17,900 attempts (Wordfence, 2026-06-03); The Hacker News and BleepingComputer reported the campaign in early June (The Hacker News, 2026-06-05) (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-06).

Exposure
WordPress sites running Everest Forms Pro 1.9.12 or earlier with a form that uses complex calculations (Wordfence, 2026-06-03).
Detection
Unauthenticated POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php submitting Everest Forms data that contains PHP code, followed by a new administrator account the site owner did not create (Wordfence, 2026-06-03).
Defender takeaway
Updating to 1.9.13 closes the flaw but does not remove an administrator account an attacker already added; review administrator users on every site that ran an affected version since 2026-04-13 (Wordfence, 2026-06-03).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:49 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarysectorstechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceclassificationactionsdeep_divedeep_dive_categorybodyevent_datesourcing_note

Wordfence published its exploitation report on 2026-06-03 and dates the peak to 2026-05-16, with more than 17,900 attempts blocked that day (Wordfence, 2026-06-03). The plugin has about 4,000 active installations, and no source names public-sector victims.

NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

The hijacked Polyfill CDN domain came back online answering HTTP 401, so leftover script tags raised browser sign-in prompts on Toshiba, Muji and other sites

Starting in late May 2026, the Polyfill CDN domain that was bought and used to serve malicious scripts in 2024 became active again and answered requests with HTTP 401 authentication challenges, which a browser shows as its own username and password dialog (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-05). Pages that still loaded the Polyfill script two years after the service was abandoned therefore raised a sign-in prompt that looked as if it came from the site itself. Toshiba warned on 2026-06-02 that parts of its website showed such a screen, asked users to choose Cancel without typing anything, told anyone who had entered a username and password to change it at every service that uses it, and added on 2026-06-04 that the screen no longer appears (Toshiba, 2026-06-02). Muji published a similar warning, and Japanese media reported Zojirushi, FiNC Technologies, Ishiyaku Publishers and Hobonichi affected, while a researcher saw the prompt on Samsung Smart TVs and websites on 2026-06-01; there is no indication the sites were hacked or that typed credentials were stolen (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-05).

Exposure
Any web page, CMS template or embedded web view that still references the original Polyfill CDN domain; the site has to load nothing new for its visitors to be prompted (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-05).
Detection
In web proxy or secure web gateway logs, browser requests to the original Polyfill CDN domain answered with HTTP 401 identify the pages that still embed it, through their referrer; a source-code or rendered-HTML search across the organization's web properties finds the same references before a visitor does.
Defender takeaway
Remove the Polyfill reference outright rather than switching it to another host, as the project's creator recommended in 2024, and treat any credentials users report typing into the prompt as exposed (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-05).
Correction11 Oct 2026 15:08 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummaryprioritytagsentitiestechniquesaffected_productssourcesevidenceclassificationupdate_ofbody

The earlier text advised moving the script to two other domains. BleepingComputer describes those domains as the service's relaunch after the 2024 incident, not as vetted mirrors, and the project's creator recommended removing the service (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-05). The earlier text also recommended Subresource Integrity, which does not stop a browser from showing the sign-in prompt for an HTTP 401 answer. Toshiba reported on 2026-06-04 that the prompt no longer appears on its site (Toshiba, 2026-06-02). The priority moves from high to notable: the prompts collected nothing that is known to have been stolen, and the fix is a cleanup.

entries.headline: NCSC Switzerland: WhatsApp hotel-booking phishing in two variants, one fed by the April Booking.com data leak
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

NCSC Switzerland: WhatsApp hotel-booking phishing in two variants, one fed by the April Booking.com data leak

NCSC Switzerland's Week 22 report notes an uptick in fraudulent WhatsApp messages about hotel bookings, in two variants (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02). Variant 1 draws on real booking data (dates of stay, hotel names, guest names) from the April 2026 Booking.com data leak and sends a fake refund lure on WhatsApp that leads to a phishing page imitating TWINT and then to a second one posing as a bank, where the victim enters card data. Variant 2, which NCSC calls long-known, uses hotel booking-system credentials stolen by phishing or malware to message guests through the platform's official messaging, or by email or WhatsApp, demanding urgent card verification or an advance payment. In analyst judgement the second is the harder one to spot, since the message carries the trust of the real platform and defeats the usual "is this sender legitimate?" check. NCSC speaks of victims generally and names no sector.

Exposure
Guests whose bookings were in the April 2026 Booking.com data leak, who receive the refund lure, and hotels whose booking-system logins are phished or stolen by malware, whose existing and future guests are then contacted through the platform's own messaging (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02). Staff who book travel through these platforms fall in the same exposed population (analyst inference).
Detection
For a hotel, booking-system login records and the messages its account sends to guests, since the takeover variant logs in with stolen credentials and messages guests with urgent card-verification or advance-payment demands; for any organisation, web-proxy or DNS records of visits to pages imitating TWINT or a bank, the path the refund variant uses to collect card data (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02).

Triage: correct booking details and a seemingly authentic sender do not make a message genuine; NCSC's tell is the request, an unsolicited refund or an urgent card verification to be completed through a link, and a refund never asks for login details or a QR-code scan (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02).

Defender takeaway
Because the takeover lure comes from the hotel's real booking account, a sender check does not catch it (analyst judgement); NCSC's lever is out-of-band verification, opening the booking through the official app or website or calling the hotel on a number looked up independently, never through the message's link, and having the card blocked at once if its details were entered (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02).
Correction30 Sep 2026 06:43 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0634Z-auditsourcestechniquesclassificationtitleheadlinesummaryprioritysectorsbody

NCSC Switzerland ties only the first variant, the WhatsApp refund scam, to the April 2026 Booking.com data leak. It calls the second, the takeover of hotel booking-system accounts, long-known, and it does not rank the two (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02). The title, summary and analysis now say so, and the view that the second is the harder one to spot is marked as analyst judgement. The phishing pages imitate TWINT and a bank, and NCSC speaks of victims generally without narrowing them to Switzerland or to a sector, so the entry's priority is notable rather than high. The citation now points at the page's new address on bacs.admin.ch, after the old ncsc.admin.ch page went dead.

Improvement21 Oct 2026 08:21 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-auditbodytechniques

Correct booking details and a seemingly authentic sender do not make a message genuine: the tell is an unsolicited refund or urgent card verification to be completed through a link, and a refund never asks for login details or a QR-code scan. Verification belongs out of band, through the official app or website or a call to the hotel on an independently looked-up number, and a card whose details were entered should be blocked at once (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-02).

entries.headline: NCSC Switzerland warns of cyber operations around the G7 Évian summit (15–17 June)
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA3

NCSC Switzerland warns of cyber operations around the G7 Évian summit (15–17 June)

On 2026-06-01 Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre published a pre-event advisory warning that large events and international conferences are "often used as an opportunity to stage a cyberattack" and that it "expects disruptive maneuvers in cyberspace again" around the G7 summit in Évian (France, 15–17 June) (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-06-01). Although the summit sits on French soil, most delegations land at Geneva airport and stay on the Swiss side (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03). An independently published threat map for the event frames the expected activity against the template of the 2024 Bürgenstock summit, when the pro-Russia hacktivist collective NoName057(16) ran DDoS waves against Swiss federal sites and conference-linked organisations on each summit day; the same map additionally flags state intelligence collection against hotel and telecom infrastructure, rogue-base-station cellular interception, and social engineering of hotel help desks as plausible vectors (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03). The NCSC advisory itself recommends generic protective measures and DDoS preparedness for organisations linked to the event.

Exposure
The websites and online services of Swiss organisations, which the DDoS attacks NCSC anticipated during the summit were expected to target, and the participants of such events and their organisations, which NCSC rates as likely targets (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-06-01). In analyst judgement that put Swiss federal and cantonal administrations, conference-linked suppliers and Swiss telecom operators in the blast radius; ZENDATA adds that state services target the providers around a summit, such as hotels, transport and telecom operators, and asks organisations around Lake Geneva whether they sit in a target's supply chain (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03).
Detection
Inbound traffic volume and the availability of websites and online services, which a DDoS floods until they are partially or completely inaccessible (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-06-01); ZENDATA notes that most network-layer attacks now end in under ten minutes, faster than any human can authorise mitigation (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03). After an event, ZENDATA's hunt looks for in-memory implants, suspicious driver signatures, anomalous OAuth grants, persistence in supplier networks and login-page anomalies on exposed platforms (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03).
Defender takeaway
The warning's lasting lesson is NCSC's baseline for organisations around large international events, which it recommends regardless of the current threat situation: a second factor or passkey on every remote-access channel, prompt patching, offline backups, an anti-DDoS solution for essential web services, EDR or XDR on clients and servers, and restricted access to exposed systems (NCSC Switzerland, measures for major events). ZENDATA's map adds event-specific steps, such as rotating administrative credentials before and after the event and reviewing MFA on customer-facing identity providers (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03).
Correction30 Sep 2026 06:43 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0634Z-auditsourcestechniquesclassificationsummaryentitiesbody

ZENDATA's risk map for the summit names social engineering of hotel help desks among the plausible vectors, not social engineering of event staff, and the analysis now says so (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03). The observation that most delegations arrive through Geneva and stay on the Swiss side comes from the same map and now cites it. NCSC Switzerland's advisory warns that large events and conferences are "often used as an opportunity to stage a cyberattack", not that the summit is a high-value target, and the analysis now quotes it. Neither source says that the Swiss administrations, suppliers and telecom operators the analysis places in the blast radius will be targeted at Évian, so that exposure is now marked as analyst judgement. The advisory is cited at its new address on bacs.admin.ch (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-06-01).

Correction11 Oct 2026 14:02 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-auditbodyprioritysummarysources

The G7 summit in Évian was scheduled for 15 to 17 June 2026 (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-06-01), so the warning's event window has passed; the entry stays as a record of the warning, at routine priority instead of high. The summary records the warning in the past tense, and the takeaway separates NCSC's baseline measures, which it recommends regardless of the current threat situation (NCSC Switzerland, measures for major events), from the event-specific steps in ZENDATA's map (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03).

Improvement21 Oct 2026 08:21 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-auditbody

NCSC expected the DDoS attacks around the summit to target the websites and online services of Swiss organisations, and it rated the participants of such events and their organisations as likely targets (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-06-01). ZENDATA notes that most network-layer attacks now end in under ten minutes, faster than any human can authorise mitigation, and its post-event hunt looks for in-memory implants, suspicious driver signatures, anomalous OAuth grants, persistence in supplier networks and login-page anomalies on exposed platforms (ZENDATA Cybersecurity, 2026-05-03).

entries.headline: A Netlogon overflow gives unauthenticated attackers SYSTEM on domain controllers; Belgium's CCB reports exploitation that Microsoft has not confirmed
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-41089 +3exploitedupdatedNATOA3

Microsoft May 2026 Patch Tuesday: Netlogon pre-auth RCE on domain controllers (CVE-2026-41089), later reported exploited by Belgium's CCB, leads four critical fixes

Microsoft's May 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed 118 vulnerabilities by Tenable's count, 16 rated critical, with none exploited or publicly disclosed at release (Tenable, 2026-05-12) (Krebs on Security, 2026-05-12); Help Net Security counts more than 120 (Help Net Security, 2026-05-12) and ZDI 138 (ZDI, 2026-05-12). The one that matters most is CVE-2026-41089 (CVSS 9.8), a stack-based buffer overflow in Windows Netlogon that lets an unauthenticated attacker execute code over the network (Microsoft MSRC); on a domain controller that means code execution as SYSTEM (CERT-EU, 2026-06-10). CVE-2026-41096 (CVSS 9.8) is a heap-based buffer overflow in the Windows DNS Client reachable through a malicious DNS response from an attacker able to influence replies (ZDI, 2026-05-12), which Microsoft assesses as less likely to be exploited (Krebs on Security, 2026-05-12). CVE-2026-41103 (CVSS 9.1) is an elevation of privilege in the Microsoft SSO Plugin for Jira and Confluence rated "Exploitation More Likely" (Tenable, 2026-05-12), and CVE-2026-42898 (CVSS 9.9) is a code-injection flaw in on-premises Dynamics 365 that requires an authenticated attacker (ZDI, 2026-05-12).

Exposure
CVE-2026-41089 affects Windows Server 2012 through 2025 acting as a domain controller; the fixed builds are 10.0.14393.9140 (2016), 10.0.17763.8755 (2019), 10.0.20348.5074 (2022), 10.0.25398.2330 (2022 23H2) and 10.0.26100.32772 (2025) (CERT-EU, 2026-06-10); Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 are also affected (CERT-EU, 2026-06-10), and Krebs reports patches for every Windows Server version from 2012 onwards (Krebs on Security, 2026-05-12).
Detection
The indicators Automox lists for the Netlogon flaw are unexpected Netlogon service crashes or restarts, anomalous Netlogon traffic patterns from source addresses that are not domain controllers, and authentication failures or domain trust errors right after suspicious traffic reaches a domain controller (Help Net Security, 2026-06-01).

Contradiction: Belgium's CCB states that CVE-2026-41089 is exploited, on information from "trusted partners", while Microsoft told BleepingComputer it had no evidence to support the claim (CCB, 2026-05-29) (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-01).

Defender takeaway
Patch every domain controller to the fixed build (CERT-EU, 2026-06-10); because CCB reports exploitation and notes that patching does not remediate historic compromise (CCB, 2026-05-29), check domain controllers that were unpatched after the May update for the Netlogon indicators above.
Update02 Jun 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-06-02-8af85d01actionscvesevidenceimmediate_actionpriorityregionssectorssourcestagsbody

Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity updated its May Patch Tuesday advisory on 2026-05-29 to say that CVE-2026-41089 is now actively exploited in the wild (CCB, 2026-05-29), and BleepingComputer and Help Net Security reported it on 2026-06-01 (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-01) (Help Net Security, 2026-06-01). CCB attributes the information to trusted partners, and Microsoft said it had no evidence to support the claim while recommending the security updates (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-01). CERT-EU relayed CCB's statement in its advisory of 2026-06-10 (CERT-EU, 2026-06-10).

Correction11 Oct 2026 14:42 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummaryimmediate_actionsectorstechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceclassificationactionsbodypriority

CCB's exploitation statement dates from 2026-05-29 and rests on information from trusted partners; Microsoft told BleepingComputer it had no evidence to support it (CCB, 2026-05-29) (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-01). Microsoft says 16 of the May CVEs, CVE-2026-41089 and CVE-2026-41096 among them, were found with its MDASH agentic system, and places the DNS Client flaw in dnsapi.dll (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-12); no source says that flaw runs code as NetworkService. CVE-2026-41103 is an elevation of privilege, and CVE-2026-42898 requires an authenticated attacker (Tenable, 2026-05-12) (ZDI, 2026-05-12). The priority moves from critical to high: the exploitation claim rests on one national CERT's partner information, Microsoft said in a statement BleepingComputer added on 2026-06-02 that it had no evidence, and its advisory lists the flaw as not exploited (Microsoft MSRC); patching domain controllers remains the action.

entries.headline: Attackers abused a FortiClient EMS auth bypass to add VPN connect scripts that installed a credential stealer posing as a Fortinet patch
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-35616exploitedupdatedNATOA1

FortiClient EMS CVE-2026-35616: exploited API authentication bypass used to push VPN on-connect scripts that drop EKZ Infostealer on managed endpoints

CVE-2026-35616 is an API authentication bypass in FortiClient EMS 7.4.5 and 7.4.6 that Fortinet has observed exploited in the wild; a hotfix exists for both versions and 7.4.7 includes the fix (Fortinet PSIRT, FG-IR-26-099). CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-04-06 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-04-06). Bishop Fox traced the bypass to EMS's Django middleware trusting client-supplied X-SSL-CLIENT-VERIFY and certificate headers as if Apache had set them, combined with chain validation that matches only subject and issuer names without checking signatures, so a forged certificate chain passes (Bishop Fox, 2026-04-07).

Arctic Wolf documented a campaign that used the flaw to reach managed endpoints (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27). After authenticating as a Fabric device, the actor deferred upgrade reminders and edited the Remote Access Profile and endpoint policy to add scripts that run when FortiClient establishes a VPN tunnel; within seconds of an IPsec tunnel coming up, fortitray.exe launched GUID-named .cmd files through cmd.exe, which ran base64-encoded PowerShell that downloaded and ran a payload, slept 90 seconds and sent the script output out (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27). The payload, disguised as a Fortinet patch executable, is EKZ Infostealer, which exports credentials, cookies and autofill data from Chromium and Firefox browsers to a log file; for Chromium it copies itself into the browser's Application directory and relaunches from there to pass Chromium Elevation Service path validation before decrypting the browser's master key, and stolen cookies can let attackers reuse sessions without triggering MFA (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27).

Exposure
FortiClient EMS 7.4.5 or 7.4.6 without the hotfix; every endpoint the EMS manages is reachable through its policies (Fortinet PSIRT, FG-IR-26-099) (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27).
Detection
In EMS logs, a request rejected with "Certificate not found in request header" followed by a Fabric-device certificate update, and unexpected edits to the Remote Access Profile or endpoint policy; on endpoints, fortitray.exe or ipsec.exe starting cmd.exe with a GUID-named script from the FortiClient trace folder, then encoded PowerShell; in file and process telemetry, the fake patch executable running from the shared ProgramData folder, a copy of it written into a browser's Application directory, and a log file in that folder that PowerShell reads, sends out by HTTP POST and then deletes along with the payload (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27).
Defender takeaway
A compromised EMS turns a trusted management channel into a fleet-wide execution path, so after patching review every Remote Access Profile and policy for added scripts and treat browser sessions on affected endpoints as stolen (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:47 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummaryevent_datetagsregionssectorstechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceclassificationdeep_divedeep_dive_categorybody

Bishop Fox attributes the bypass to EMS's Django middleware accepting client-supplied certificate headers and to chain validation that checks names without signatures (Bishop Fox, 2026-04-07); the earlier comparison with a SharePoint flaw was wrong. In Arctic Wolf's campaign the endpoints ran attacker scripts through VPN on-connect settings that fortitray.exe or ipsec.exe launched, and EKZ copies itself into the browser's Application directory (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27); the earlier detection guidance on update tasks and profile writes did not match the observed behaviour.

Improvement21 Oct 2026 12:07 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1149Z-auditcvesbody

Fortinet scores CVE-2026-35616 at CVSSv3 9.8, with 9.1 as the temporal score (Fortinet PSIRT, FG-IR-26-099). On Chromium browsers EKZ copies itself into the browser's Application directory and relaunches from there to pass Chromium Elevation Service path validation; Arctic Wolf's hunts also cover the payload running from the shared ProgramData folder and a log file there that PowerShell reads, posts out over HTTP and deletes together with the payload (Arctic Wolf, 2026-05-27).

Arctic Wolf traced the chain to EKZ Infostealer, a browser credential and cookie stealer disguised as a Fortinet patch.

updates.summary: The mechanism was wrong: the bypass rests on EMS's Django middleware trusting client-supplied certificate headers plus name-only chain validation, not a reverse proxy stamping a header, and it bears no relation to the SharePoint CVE-2026-45659. The CVSS 9.1 is the temporal score of a vector with availability impact; the EPSS figure and the push of a signed update task had no source. The campaign ran through VPN on-connect scripts launched by fortitray.exe or ipsec.exe, and EKZ copies itself into the browser's Application directory, not into profile folders. The evidence quotes were not on the Arctic Wolf page and the region and sector tags had no source. The entry is rewritten from Fortinet, Bishop Fox and Arctic Wolf with exposure, detection and takeaway lines, verbatim evidence, a rating and an ATT&CK mapping.

Fortinet's base score is CVSSv3 9.8, with 9.1 its temporal score. The Chromium step now reads as Arctic Wolf states it, a self-copy into the browser's Application directory to pass Elevation Service path validation, and the detection guidance adds Arctic Wolf's ProgramData staging and log-file exfiltration hunts. The payload and log file names are replaced by descriptions of the behaviour.

entries.headline: IBM HTTP Server's CVSS 9.8 flaw CVE-2026-9170 is fixed in Fix Packs 9.0.5.29 and 8.5.5.30, both now released
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-9170updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-9170: IBM HTTP Server improper input validation allows denial of service and potential remote code execution without authentication (CVSS 9.8)

IBM's bulletin of 2026-05-26 fixes nine vulnerabilities in IBM HTTP Server (IHS), the Apache-based component shipped with all editions of WebSphere Application Server and bundling products. The most severe, CVE-2026-9170, is improper input validation (CWE-94) that IBM says makes IHS "vulnerable to denial of service and a potential remote code execution", scored CVSS 9.8 by IBM with a network attack vector and no privileges or user interaction required (IBM, 2026-05-26). The other flaws include CVE-2026-8855 (CVSS 8.1), remote code execution in configurations with TLS client authentication, and CVE-2026-8834 (CVSS 8.0), a heap overflow reachable by a privileged user authenticated to the Administration Server (IBM, 2026-05-26). NCSC-CH flagged the advisory on 2026-05-28 and gives the exploitation status as unknown (NCSC-CH Cyber Security Hub, 2026-05-28). CVE-2026-9170 is not in CISA's KEV catalog as of 2026-09-29 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-09-29).

Exposure
IBM HTTP Server 9.0.0.0 through 9.0.5.28 and 8.5.0.0 through 8.5.5.29 (IBM, 2026-05-26). IBM lists the affected configuration as servers using the SSLEnable directive and rates it common (IBM, 2026-10-13).
Defender takeaway
Apply Fix Pack 9.0.5.29 or 8.5.5.30 or later, which IBM's bulletin names as the fix (IBM, 2026-05-26) and which IBM released on 2026-09-08 and 2026-07-27 (IBM, 2026-09-08). Where a fix pack cannot go in yet, IBM's current cumulative interim fix is IFDT503301 of 13 October 2026, which supersedes IFPH71594 and still includes the PH71265 fix; it is published for 9.0.5.27 through 9.0.5.29 and for 8.5.5.30 and 8.5.5.31, and its prerequisite fix pack must be applied first (IBM, 2026-10-13). IBM lists no workaround (IBM, 2026-05-26). NCSC-CH suggests disabling unneeded optional modules such as mod_ibm_upload or mod_mem_cache as a temporary step against certain denial-of-service vectors only (NCSC-CH Cyber Security Hub, 2026-05-28).
Correction30 Sep 2026 07:16 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-auditbodyclassificationtechniquestitleheadlinesummaryprioritysectorscvesevidencesources

The earlier text placed the flaw in the HTTP request-parsing layer behind the default web listener, which IBM's bulletin does not say, said fix packs were already out when only an interim fix existed, and attributed module-disabling advice to IBM. IBM describes CVE-2026-9170 as improper input validation that can cause denial of service and potential remote code execution, scores it CVSS 9.8 itself with a network attack vector and no privileges or user interaction, offered an interim fix for APAR PH71265 with fix packs targeted for 3Q2026, and lists no workaround (IBM, 2026-05-26). Fix Pack 8.5.5.30 was released on 2026-07-27 and 9.0.5.29 on 2026-09-08 (IBM, 2026-09-08). The module advice comes from NCSC-CH and covers certain denial-of-service vectors only, and NCSC-CH gives the exploitation status as unknown rather than none observed (NCSC-CH Cyber Security Hub, 2026-05-28). No cited source describes where the product is deployed, so an earlier claim about Swiss banking, insurance and federal estates is withdrawn.

Correction21 Oct 2026 08:20 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-auditsummarycvessourcesbody

IBM's cumulative security interim fix page, modified on 13 October 2026, now offers IFDT503301 (13 October 2026), which supersedes IFPH71594 and still includes the PH71265 fix for CVE-2026-9170; IFPH71594 had itself replaced IFPH71265 only on 16 July 2026 (IBM, 2026-10-13). IBM removes a superseded interim fix from Fix Central, so the interim route is now IFDT503301, published for 9.0.5.27 through 9.0.5.29 and for 8.5.5.30 and 8.5.5.31, on top of its prerequisite fix pack (IBM, 2026-10-13).
