entries.classification_html: NATOB1
entries.headline: Nx Console / TanStack / DAEMON Tools supply-chain cascade lands three CISA KEV entries
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-48027 +2exploitedupdatedNATOB1

Nx Console / TanStack / DAEMON Tools supply-chain cascade lands three CISA KEV entries

Background. The CISA KEV adds on 2026-05-27 close a chain of disclosures across the preceding three weeks that share a single operational pattern: trusted developer-tooling-publishing pipelines (a maintainer's machine, a vendor build server, a popular VS Code marketplace listing) used to push malicious code to downstream consumers at scale (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-27; Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21; GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w, 2026-05-18; GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx, 2026-05-11; Disc Soft Limited, 2026-05-06; Kaspersky, 2026-05-05; Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). The TanStack compromise was carried out via Mini Shai-Hulud, TeamPCP's self-replicating worm that steals CI/CD credentials and uses them to publish infected versions of more packages (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). Three of the chain's CVEs were added to CISA KEV on the same day (2026-05-27), confirming in-the-wild exploitation (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-27), and GitHub's CISO Alexis Wales named the malicious Nx Console extension as the vector for the theft of about 3,800 of GitHub's internal repositories (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21).

The TanStack → Nx Console pivot: CVE-2026-45321 and CVE-2026-48027.

The chain begins on 2026-05-11 with GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx (CVE-2026-45321): 84 malicious versions across 42 @tanstack/* npm packages were published with a credential-stealing payload (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). On a Nx contributor's machine the payload read locally stored credentials and exfiltrated them, including the contributor's GitHub CLI OAuth token. The Nx postmortem names @tanstack/zod-adapter@1.166.15 as the malicious dependency resolved on that machine (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). Seven days later, the attacker published Nx Console v18.95.0 as a legitimate Nx core contributor (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21), tracked as CVE-2026-48027 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-27). The malicious version was live on the Visual Studio Marketplace from 12:30 to 12:48 UTC on 2026-05-18 and on Open VSX from 12:33 to 13:09 UTC (GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w, 2026-05-18). Nx Console is a VS Code extension with 2.2 million installs (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). The payload ran on extension activation in VS Code or a fork such as Cursor and harvested Vault tokens, npm tokens, AWS metadata-service, Secrets Manager, SSM and Web Identity credentials, GitHub tokens, the contents of an active 1Password op CLI session, SSH private keys, .env files and GCP and Docker credentials (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). The advisory describes it as an obfuscated payload that the extension fetched, and says the harvested data was exfiltrated over HTTPS, the GitHub API and DNS (GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w, 2026-05-18).

The advisory says the leaked credentials "allowed the attacker to run workflows on our GitHub repository as a contributor" (GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w, 2026-05-18). The postmortem names the gap that let this become a release: until the incident any core contributor could publish a new Nx Console version without a second human's approval, with no required-reviewer rule and no environment gate (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). A stolen developer credential therefore turned into a downstream publish without secondary review.

CVE-2026-8398: DAEMON Tools Lite signed-build trojanisation.

CVE-2026-8398 covers a separate but parallel compromise of Disc Soft Limited's build environment. DAEMON Tools Lite versions 12.5.0.2421 through 12.5.0.2434, circulating since 2026-04-08, contained trojanised DTHelper.exe, DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe, and DTShellHlp.exe binaries signed with a valid AVB Disc Soft digital signature, which contact a command-and-control server at every system start (Kaspersky, 2026-05-05). Disc Soft says it found "unauthorized interference within our infrastructure" and that certain installation packages "were impacted within our build environment and were released in a compromised state". It released the clean version 12.6 on 2026-05-05 (Disc Soft Limited, 2026-05-06). Kaspersky detected several thousand attempts to install additional payloads through infected installations during the roughly four-week distribution window (Kaspersky, 2026-05-05). Safe version: 12.6 or later. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 2026-05-27 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-27).

Downstream impact: what GitHub and Grafana Labs publicly confirmed.

GitHub CISO Alexis Wales named the malicious Nx Console v18.95.0 extension, installed by a GitHub employee, as the vector for GitHub's breach in which about 3,800 private repositories were exfiltrated (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). Grafana Labs' CISO Joe McManus traced Grafana's separate GitHub breach to "a TanStack npm supply chain attack via the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign", not to Nx Console, so both breaches trace back to the TanStack compromise by different routes (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). The malicious version was live for less than an hour (about 18 minutes on the Visual Studio Marketplace and 36 on Open VSX) (GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w, 2026-05-18); the postmortem's summary gives about 11 minutes for the Marketplace, counted from the maintainers' first alert (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21), and one install by a GitHub employee was enough for the attackers to reach GitHub's private repositories (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21).

Detection and hardening: what to push to operators today.

Exposure
For Nx Console, only 18.95.0 is affected, in VS Code and forks such as Cursor. Earlier and later versions are not, and 18.100.0 is the fixed release (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). The Visual Studio Marketplace reports 28 installs of 18.95.0 and Open VSX 41 downloads from 21 unique IPs, while Nx's own analytics count about 6,000 activations of that version, so Nx says anyone who had the extension with auto-update enabled between 12:30 and 13:09 UTC on 2026-05-18 should assume compromise (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). The 2.2 million installs are the extension's overall count, not those of the malicious version (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). For DAEMON Tools Lite, the trojanised builds are 12.5.0.2421 to 12.5.0.2434, in circulation from 2026-04-08 (Kaspersky, 2026-05-05). Disc Soft says only the free 12.5.1 release was affected, not the paid Lite, Ultra or Pro products, and that 12.6 is clean (Disc Soft Limited, 2026-05-06). For the upstream TanStack compromise (CVE-2026-45321), TanStack says any developer or CI environment that ran an npm, pnpm or yarn install against an affected @tanstack/* version on 2026-05-11 should be considered compromised, with every credential the install process could reach rotated and cloud audit logs reviewed for activity from those hosts (GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx, 2026-05-11).
Detection
Inventory installed editor extensions on developer hosts for Nx Console at exactly version 18.95.0 (the postmortem's check lists extensions with their versions and filters on angular-console) (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). On hosts that ran it, look for the payload's persistence: a Python backdoor under the user profile with staging and state files in temporary directories, a LaunchAgent on macOS, attempted /etc/sudoers changes on Linux, and a Bun runtime installed under the user profile on Windows (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). Updating to 18.100.0 is only the first remediation step: the advisory also says to kill the backdoor processes, which actively try to exfiltrate credentials, and to delete the persistence artifacts, so check patched hosts as well (GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w, 2026-05-18). For DAEMON Tools Lite: hunt for DTHelper.exe or DTShellHlp.exe invocations with parent-process or file-modify timestamps inside the 2026-04-08 → 2026-05-05 window and a hash that does not match the post-12.6 reference set (compare against the indicators Kaspersky links from its write-up (Kaspersky, 2026-05-05)). For TanStack: a pinned @tanstack/* version is malicious if its published manifest carries an optionalDependencies entry for the fictitious @tanstack/setup package, with an undeclared obfuscated JavaScript payload of about 2.3 MB at the package root, and the CI pipelines to audit are those that ran an install against @tanstack/* between 19:20 and 19:30 UTC that day (GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx, 2026-05-11).

Hardening: enforce an organisational policy controls list for VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf extensions (the malicious upload passed the Visual Studio Marketplace's automated signing, manifest and malware checks (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21)); pin npm dependencies with lockfile + --ignore-scripts for CI/CD builds; require human approval for any package that adds or modifies postinstall / preinstall / install scripts; rotate every CI/CD secret, npm token, GitHub PAT, and AWS access key accessible from any host that ran an affected Nx Console version between 2026-05-18 12:30 and 13:09 UTC. Treat any host that installed Nx Console 18.95.0, or had Nx Console installed with auto-update enabled in VS Code or a fork such as Cursor during that window, as potentially compromised (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21).

Defender takeaway
One stolen developer credential became a public release because any core contributor could publish Nx Console without a second human's approval (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). For a host that installed 18.95.0, the postmortem says to treat anything reachable from it as exposed and to rotate every credential that was on disk or could have been minted during the exposure window. Its lesson for any pipeline that can publish to a public registry is to require approval gating (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21).
Correction30 Sep 2026 07:16 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-auditsourcesbodyevidencesourcing_noteclassificationtechniquestagssummaryentitiesaffected_products

CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog marks both CVE-2026-48027 (Nx Console) and CVE-2026-45321 (TanStack) as used in known ransomware campaigns (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-27). The attackers who stole Grafana Labs' codebase through the TanStack compromise demanded payment not to release or sell it, and Grafana did not pay (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). Credentials exposed through either compromise are best handled on the assumption that an extortion group holds them.

The Nx postmortem does not describe token scopes, a tag push or hosted-runner publish secrets. It says any core contributor could publish without a second approval (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). The harvested credentials are Vault, npm, AWS service, GitHub, 1Password op session, SSH, .env, GCP and Docker secrets (Nx postmortem, 2026-05-21). GitHub named Nx Console only for its own breach, while Grafana Labs traced its breach to the TanStack npm attack (Help Net Security, 2026-05-21). The DAEMON Tools trojanised builds circulated for about four weeks, from 2026-04-08 until the clean 12.6 release on 2026-05-05 (Kaspersky, 2026-05-05; Disc Soft Limited, 2026-05-06).

entries.summary: CISA added three supply-chain CVEs to KEV on 2026-05-27, the Nx Console / TanStack / DAEMON Tools cascade. The Nx Console v18.95.0 VS Code extension compromise (CVE-2026-48027) traces to the TanStack npm supply-chain compromise (CVE-2026-45321), whose payload exfiltrated a contributor's GitHub CLI OAuth token. GitHub's CISO named the extension as the vector for the theft of about 3,800 GitHub internal repositories, and Grafana Labs traced its own breach to the upstream TanStack compromise. Separately, CVE-2026-8398 covers a roughly four-week trojanisation of signed DAEMON Tools Lite builds 12.5.0.2421 to 12.5.0.2434 from the vendor's build environment.
entries.title: Nx Console / TanStack / DAEMON Tools supply-chain cascade lands three CISA KEV entries

updates.summary: CISA's catalog is now cited for the 2026-05-27 KEV additions, and CISA marks the Nx Console and TanStack compromises as used in known ransomware campaigns. Claims no source carries are removed: token scopes, a tag push, hosted-runner publish secrets, Claude Code or AWS credential-file harvesting, GitHub confirming Grafana's breach, Kaspersky supplying KEV evidence, a vendor statement about the signing path, a six-week window, unsigned marketplace extensions and an uncited Laravel-Lang comparison. The payload and GitHub-breach sentences cite the pages that carry them, and the detection guidance follows the postmortem's version check and persistence artifacts. An exposure line gives the affected versions and the reach of the malicious Nx Console release, Grafana's extortion is noted, and a cited takeaway closes the analysis. The Mini Shai-Hulud campaign and the Nx Console and DAEMON Tools incidents are linked. The exposure and detection lines now also cover the upstream TanStack compromise as TanStack's advisory describes it.

entries.headline: Attackers used a Ghost CMS SQL injection to poison 700+ sites with fake verification pages that push stealers to users
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-26980exploitedupdatedNATOB2

Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980: Content API SQL injection mass-exploited to steal Admin API keys and turn 700+ sites into ClickFix lures

CVE-2026-26980 is an unauthenticated SQL injection in the Ghost CMS Content API, present from 3.24.0 to 6.19.0, fixed in 6.19.1 and rated CVSS 9.4 on Ghost's advisory; because it gives access to a site's API keys, Ghost recommends reviewing staff users and rotating keys after upgrading (Ghost, GHSA-w52v-v783-gw97). There is no application-level workaround, since the Content API key is public by design; a reverse proxy or WAF rule blocking Content API requests whose filter contains slug:[ (or slug%3A%5B) is the temporary mitigation (Ghost, GHSA-w52v-v783-gw97). The fix shipped in February, but many sites did not install it (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-24).

XLab detected the campaign on 2026-05-07, confirmed 156 victim domains by 2026-05-10 and more than 700 in its enumeration of 2026-05-17, when it also found a second attack group; the two groups sometimes replace each other's code on the same site (XLab, 2026-05-21). XLab names Harvard University, Oxford University and Auburn University among the well-known sites affected, and its victim table is 48.1% personal blogs or independent sites (XLab, 2026-05-21); BleepingComputer adds DuckDuckGo and describes the mix as university portals, AI/SaaS companies, media outlets, fintech firms, security sites and personal blogs (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-24).

The attackers used the SQL injection to read each site's Admin API key, which has management permissions over articles, themes and users, then called the Admin API (PUT /ghost/api/admin/posts/:id/) to append a JavaScript loader to articles in bulk (XLab, 2026-05-21). The loader fetches a cloaking script, which XLab traces to the commercial Adspect service, that fingerprints each browser and shows only visitors it judges to be real victims a forged Cloudflare "Verify you are human" page in an iframe (XLab, 2026-05-21). While the page silently downloads an archive, it tells the visitor to press WIN+R and paste a command that moves the archive to %TEMP%, extracts it with tar and starts the batch file inside it minimized; the batch file runs hidden PowerShell that downloads a DLL and starts one of its exported functions through rundll32 (XLab, 2026-05-21). From 2026-05-16 the DLL fetched a stealer, an Electron application that persists through Electron's login-item API and polls its server every 30 seconds for JavaScript or executables to run (XLab, 2026-05-21). BleepingComputer also lists DLL loaders and JavaScript droppers among the payloads (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-24).

Exposure
Any Ghost site running 3.24.0 to 6.19.0; the running Ghost version is the test (Ghost, GHSA-w52v-v783-gw97).
Detection
On the site, PUT /ghost/api/admin/posts/:id/ requests from unfamiliar sources or in bulk within a short period, Admin API keys nobody created, and extra <script> tags in post bodies, Code Injection settings or theme files (XLab, 2026-05-21). On endpoints, a Run-dialog command that moves an archive out of the Downloads folder, extracts it with tar and starts a batch file, followed by hidden PowerShell and rundll32 loading a freshly downloaded DLL (XLab, 2026-05-21).
Defender takeaway
An upgrade does not undo the compromise: after moving to 6.19.1 or later, rotate the Admin API key, Content API key, administrator password and sessions, review staff accounts, and remove injected scripts at the database level, not just in the editor (Ghost, GHSA-w52v-v783-gw97) (XLab, 2026-05-21). XLab advises keeping at least 30 days of Admin API call logs so a compromise can be traced back (XLab, 2026-05-21).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:46 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarytagsregionssectorstechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceclassificationbodydeep_divedeep_dive_categorysourcing_note

Ghost's advisory says there is no application-level workaround and that restricting the Content API key does not mitigate the flaw, because the key is public by design; the temporary control is a reverse-proxy or WAF rule blocking slug:[ filters (Ghost, GHSA-w52v-v783-gw97). The earlier advice to restrict the Content API to trusted origins would not have protected a site.

Improvement21 Oct 2026 15:43 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1149Z-auditbodyevidenceheadlinesummarytechniques

Ghost's advisory gives the affected range, 3.24.0 to 6.19.0, without distinguishing hosted from self-hosted sites (Ghost, GHSA-w52v-v783-gw97). XLab's figure of more than 700 counts poisoned domains, confirmed in its enumeration of 2026-05-17, and XLab names Harvard University, Oxford University and Auburn University among them (XLab, 2026-05-21); BleepingComputer adds DuckDuckGo (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-24). In the chain XLab traced, a cloaking script it attributes to the commercial Adspect service shows only visitors it judges to be real victims a forged Cloudflare "Verify you are human" page in an iframe; that page itself downloads the archive in the background, and the command the visitor pastes only moves, extracts and starts it (XLab, 2026-05-21). XLab's site-side checks are PUT /ghost/api/admin/posts/:id/ requests in the Ghost logs, unknown Admin API keys and <script> tags added to posts, Code Injection settings or themes; after upgrading it advises rotating the Admin and Content API keys, the administrator password and sessions, and keeping at least 30 days of Admin API call logs (XLab, 2026-05-21).

entries.summary: CVE-2026-26980, an unauthenticated SQL injection in the Ghost CMS Content API (3.24.0 to 6.19.0, fixed in 6.19.1), is exploited at scale: XLab confirmed more than 700 poisoned domains by 2026-05-17. In the chain it traced, attackers stole each site's Admin API key and injected a loader that shows selected visitors a fake Cloudflare check and talks them into running a command that installs a stealer. Upgrading does not remove injected content or revoke stolen keys.
entries.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980: Content API SQL injection mass-exploited to steal Admin API keys and turn 700+ sites into ClickFix lures

updates.summary: Restricting the public Content API is not a mitigation, according to Ghost's own advisory; the WAF rule on slug filters is. Ghost's advisory is dated 2026-02-16, while BleepingComputer dates the fix's release to 19 February and XLab dates public disclosure to the same day; the sources describe an unauthenticated arbitrary database read rather than a boolean-blind injection with time-delay artefacts, and the file name, the 2024 ClickFix history, the region and sector, the Ghost(Pro) statement and the self-quoted evidence had no source. The entry is rewritten from Ghost's advisory, XLab's report and BleepingComputer with the affected range, the WAF mitigation, the campaign timeline, detection and takeaway lines, verbatim evidence, a rating and an ATT&CK mapping.

Ghost's advisory does not limit the flaw to self-hosted sites, and XLab's figure of more than 700 counts poisoned domains as of its 2026-05-17 enumeration, not sites whose keys were confirmed stolen. Added from the campaign reports: the named victims (Harvard, Oxford and Auburn per XLab, DuckDuckGo per BleepingComputer), the Adspect-derived cloaking and fake Cloudflare iframe, the background download that the pasted Run-dialog command unpacks, XLab's site-side log and key checks with its credential-rotation list, and a fuller ATT&CK mapping.

entries.headline: 7-Eleven confirms a breach of franchisee documents after ShinyHunters claims 600,000+ Salesforce records
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOB2

7-Eleven confirms breach of franchisee documents after ShinyHunters claims 600,000+ Salesforce records

7-Eleven's notification letters went out on 2026-05-01 (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-20) and say an unauthorized third party gained access on 2026-04-08 to systems used to store franchisee documents (Security Affairs, 2026-05-18), which held personal information from the franchise application process, including names and addresses; the Vermont filing adds Social Security numbers and the Massachusetts filing Social Security numbers and driver's license data (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-20). Filings in Massachusetts, Maine and Vermont count 47, 2 and 1 affected people, the letters offer up to 24 months of IDX identity-theft protection, and 7-Eleven says it has no reason to believe customer data was affected (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-20); the notices became public on 2026-05-18 (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-18). ShinyHunters had listed 7-Eleven on its leak site on 2026-04-17 claiming more than 600,000 Salesforce records with personal and corporate data, demanded a ransom by 2026-04-21 and then offered the data for $250,000 on a hacker forum (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-18); 7-Eleven did not respond when asked about that claim (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-20). Its relevance lies in the actor: SecurityWeek says ShinyHunters has targeted organizations' Salesforce instances since mid-2025 through phishing, abuse of third-party integrations or misconfigurations rather than Salesforce vulnerabilities, and that the group and affiliated actors recently claimed Instructure, Vimeo, Wynn Resorts, Vercel and Medtronic (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-18), while Security Affairs lists the European Commission among its earlier claims (Security Affairs, 2026-05-18). No source says how the 7-Eleven systems were accessed.

Exposure
Organizations whose Salesforce tenants can be reached through phished accounts, third-party integrations or misconfigurations, the paths SecurityWeek gives for the group's campaign (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-18); CyberInsider describes recent victims whose environments allegedly held exposed credentials, authentication tokens or improperly secured integrations (CyberInsider, 2026-05-23).
Defender takeaway
The 7-Eleven breach itself, about 50 franchise applicants, asks nothing of other organizations (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-20); for Salesforce tenants, review which third-party integrations hold access and which credentials and tokens they keep, the weaknesses ShinyHunters' recent victims allegedly had (CyberInsider, 2026-05-23).
Update25 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-25-d675ef38sectorssourcesbody

ShinyHunters added Charter Communications, which operates the Spectrum brand, to its leak site in the week of 2026-05-23, claiming over 42 million records containing personal information and threatening to leak them unless negotiations opened before 2026-05-27; the nature of the data had not been independently verified (CyberInsider, 2026-05-23). Charter confirmed a cybersecurity incident and told CyberInsider it was "following our security protocols" and alerting authorities, adding: "No sensitive personal information (PI) or customer proprietary network information (CPNI) data was exfiltrated by the threat actor." (CyberInsider, 2026-05-23). Charter did not disclose how the attackers gained access, and CyberInsider links the claim to the ongoing campaign against Salesforce environments (CyberInsider, 2026-05-23). entries.headline: Drupal core CVE-2026-9082: anonymous SQL injection on PostgreSQL sites, exploited in the wild from 2026-05-22
entries.html:
CRITICALCVE-2026-9082exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-9082: anonymous SQL injection in Drupal core on PostgreSQL, Highly critical, exploited and CISA KEV-listed

The Drupal Security Team pre-announced a Highly critical core release on 2026-05-18, scored 20 of 25 (AC:None, A:None, E:Theoretical, TD:Uncommon), and urged administrators to reserve the 2026-05-20 window from 17:00 to 21:00 UTC because "exploits might be developed within hours or days" (Drupal PSA-2026-05-18). SA-CORE-2026-004 followed on 2026-05-20 with CVE-2026-9082: a flaw in core's database abstraction API lets an anonymous attacker send specially crafted requests that result in arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL, which can lead to information disclosure and in some cases privilege escalation, remote code execution or other attacks (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004). Searchlight Cyber traced it to the PostgreSQL entity-query override of the case-insensitive IN operator, which builds SQL placeholder names from the keys of the submitted value array, so attacker-chosen JSON object keys reach the SQL text through two anonymous entry points, the JSON login endpoint and the JSON:API filter syntax (Searchlight Cyber, 2026-05-21). The fixed releases are 11.3.10, 11.2.12, 11.1.10, 10.6.9, 10.5.10 and 10.4.10, and Drupal 9 and 8.9 sites are told to try applying a best-effort patch file by hand (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004); Drupal 7 is not affected (Drupal PSA-2026-05-18). On 2026-05-22 Drupal raised the risk score to 23 of 25 because exploit attempts were being detected in the wild (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004), and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-22); the Drupal CNA scores it CVSS 9.8 (ENISA EUVD-2026-31153). By 2026-05-21 Imperva had observed over 15,000 attack attempts against almost 6,000 sites in 65 countries, most of it probing (Imperva, 2026-05-21).

Exposure
Drupal core sites on PostgreSQL running a version from 8.9.0 before 10.4.10, 10.5.0 before 10.5.10, 10.6.0 before 10.6.9, 11.0.0 before 11.1.10, 11.2.0 before 11.2.12 or 11.3.0 before 11.3.10 (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004); on MySQL and SQLite the IN compilation never enters the vulnerable loop (Searchlight Cyber, 2026-05-21). The releases for the supported branches (11.3, 11.2, 10.6 and 10.5) also carry Symfony and Twig security updates, which Drupal highly recommends whether or not the SQL injection affects a site, since exposure to those upstream issues depends on site configuration and contributed modules (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004).
Detection
Web access logs. The observed probes hit JSON:API routes, especially /jsonapi/node/article, with crafted filter parameters using the IN operator, crafted array keys, PostgreSQL pg_sleep timing checks and UNION-style probes, several of them carrying Nuclei-style markers, and Imperva also points to /user/login?_format=json requests (Imperva, 2026-05-21). A successful injection can make all non-public data accessible and let the attacker modify or delete any data (Drupal PSA-2026-05-18) and can escalate privileges (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004), so patching does not close a past compromise: on a PostgreSQL site that ran an affected version after 2026-05-20, review user accounts and role assignments for changes nobody made.

Triage: most of this traffic is automated probing that tests whether a site is vulnerable (Imperva, 2026-05-21); a probe against a MySQL or SQLite site, or one already on a fixed release, is noise, while the same request against an unpatched PostgreSQL site is an attempt that calls for the account review above (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004).

Defender takeaway
Every Drupal core site on PostgreSQL that was not on a fixed release by 2026-05-22 is in scope for that review; sites behind the Drupal Steward web application firewall were protected from known attack vectors but Drupal still told them to upgrade (CSO Online, 2026-05-20), and sites on other databases take the release for its Symfony and Twig fixes (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004).
Update21 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-21-77cdc4cdcvesprioritysectorssourcestagsbody

Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-004 on 2026-05-20 with CVE-2026-9082: a vulnerability in core's database abstraction API allows an attacker to send specially crafted requests resulting in arbitrary SQL injection for sites using PostgreSQL, it can be exploited by anonymous users, and it "can lead to information disclosure, and in some cases privilege escalation, remote code execution, or other attacks" (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004). The pre-announcement had scored it 20 of 25 and warned that "exploits might be developed within hours or days" (Drupal PSA-2026-05-18).

Affected versions run from 8.9.0 up to (not including) 10.4.10, 10.5.0 before 10.5.10, 10.6.0 before 10.6.9, 11.0.0 before 11.1.10, 11.2.0 before 11.2.12 and 11.3.0 before 11.3.10, and the fixed releases are 10.4.10, 10.5.10, 10.6.9, 11.1.10, 11.2.12 and 11.3.10; Drupal 9 and 8.9 sites get best-effort patch files to apply manually (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004), and Drupal 7 is not affected (Drupal PSA-2026-05-18). Sites using the Drupal Steward web application firewall are already protected from known attack vectors but should upgrade in the near future (CSO Online, 2026-05-20). NCSC.ch had carried the pre-announcement on 2026-05-19 (NCSC.ch Security Hub).

Update23 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-23-852c21c8actionscvesevidenceimmediate_actionprioritysourcestagsbody

On 2026-05-22 Drupal updated SA-CORE-2026-004, raising the risk score to 23 of 25 because exploit attempts are now being detected in the wild (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004); NCSC.ch marked Security Hub post 12584 as actively exploited the same day (NCSC.ch Security Hub), and CISA added CVE-2026-9082 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-05-22 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-22).

Imperva observed over 15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 sites across 65 countries, most of it probing of JSON:API routes, with Gaming and Financial Services sites drawing almost half the attacks (Imperva, 2026-05-21). Searchlight Cyber's analysis shows attacker-controlled array keys, sent as JSON object keys to the anonymous JSON login endpoint or through the JSON:API filter syntax, reaching the placeholder names that the PostgreSQL entity-query override builds for the case-insensitive IN operator (Searchlight Cyber, 2026-05-21).

Correction21 Oct 2026 16:06 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevidenceheadlineimmediate_actionkindregionssectorssourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitle

A score of 20 of 25 is Drupal's top tier, Highly critical, which covers 20 to 25, not the second-highest (Drupal security risk levels); it stayed below 25 because no exploit existed yet and only uncommon configurations were affected (The Register, 2026-05-19), and on 2026-05-22 it rose to 23 of 25 with exploitation detected (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004). A mitigation did exist before the patch: the PSA said the issue was protected by Drupal Steward (Drupal PSA-2026-05-18). Only Drupal 9 and 8.9 sites were left with patch files to apply by hand; the end-of-life 11.1.x and 10.4.x lines received full releases, 11.1.10 and 10.4.10 (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-004).

The Drupal CNA scores CVE-2026-9082 CVSS 9.8 (ENISA EUVD-2026-31153); 6.5 is NIST's score (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-22). Moving a site off PostgreSQL is not a control any source offers; the sourced interim measure is Drupal Steward. Imperva's figures count attack attempts, mostly probing, aimed chiefly at Gaming and Financial Services sites (Imperva, 2026-05-21). No source names Swiss, EU or university Drupal sites as targets or says Drupal dominates Swiss public portals; the Federal Administration's standard web platform is based on Livingdocs (Swiss Federal Chancellery).

entries.headline: Exploited Microsoft Defender flaws: CVE-2026-41091 gives a local attacker SYSTEM, CVE-2026-45498 denies service
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-41091 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-41091: exploited Microsoft Defender link-following privilege escalation to SYSTEM, with the CVE-2026-45498 Defender denial of service

Microsoft published CVE-2026-41091 on 2026-05-19 as exploited and publicly disclosed: improper link resolution before file access (CWE-59) in Microsoft Defender lets an authorized attacker elevate privileges locally and gain SYSTEM, scored CVSS 7.8 (MSRC, 2026-05-19). The flaw sits in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine (mpengine.dll); the last affected build is Engine version 1.1.26030.3008 and the first fixed build is Engine version 1.1.26040.8 (MSRC, 2026-05-19). Microsoft marked CVE-2026-45498, a Defender denial of service (CWE-400, CVSS 3.1 base score 4.0), as exploited the same day and fixed it separately in Antimalware Platform version 4.18.26040.7 (MSRC, 2026-05-19); CISA added both to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-05-20 based on evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-05-20). The researcher Nightmare Eclipse published the RedSun and UnDefend exploits on 2026-04-16 (Help Net Security, 2026-04-17) and has said that CVE-2026-41091 is RedSun and CVE-2026-45498 is UnDefend (The Hacker News, 2026-05-21); UnDefend lets a standard user block Defender from receiving signature updates (Help Net Security, 2026-04-17). RedSun baits Defender's real-time protection with an embedded EICAR test string and, using the Cloud Files API, oplocks and a directory junction, redirects the file rewrite of the resulting remediation into a protected system path, after which the Cloud Files infrastructure runs the attacker's binary as SYSTEM (Vectra AI, 2026-04-21).

Exposure
Defender runs on all supported versions of Windows, and System Center Endpoint Protection and Microsoft Security Essentials use the same engine; systems that have disabled Defender are not in an exploitable state, although scanners still flag their files on disk (MSRC, 2026-05-19). The running platform version shows as the Antimalware ClientVersion under Settings, About in the Windows Security program (MSRC, 2026-05-19).
Detection
Endpoint process and file telemetry. In the intrusion Huntress observed on 2026-04-16 the attacker dropped the exploit files into the user's Pictures and Downloads folders and renamed them, then ran commands that mapped user privileges, stored credentials and the Active Directory structure before launching the exploits (Help Net Security, 2026-04-17). RedSun then shows as a Defender remediation of an EICAR detection in a user-writable path followed by a SYSTEM process started from that path, and UnDefend was seen running as a child of cmd.exe under Explorer (Vectra AI, 2026-04-21). Patching does not undo a SYSTEM compromise: on hosts that ran an affected engine, look back to mid-April for SYSTEM processes launched from user profile folders.

Triage: an EICAR detection on its own is what an antivirus test produces; the RedSun pattern adds a directory junction that redirects the remediation's file rewrite into a protected system path and a SYSTEM-context process launched right after the remediation (Vectra AI, 2026-04-21).

Defender takeaway
Where Defender updates itself, the default configuration installs the fixed engine and platform with no action (MSRC, 2026-05-19); the decision is to verify, as Microsoft recommends, that engine and platform updates actually reach every host, offline and update-controlled machines first, and to hunt back on any host that ran Engine version 1.1.26030.3008 or earlier.
Update22 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-22-5b90d5a1actionscvesevidencesourcesbody

Microsoft also marks CVE-2026-45498 as exploited: a Microsoft Defender denial of service (CVSS 3.1 base score 4.0) fixed in Antimalware Platform version 4.18.26040.7 (MSRC, 2026-05-19), while CVE-2026-41091 is fixed in Malware Protection Engine version 1.1.26040.8 (MSRC, 2026-05-19). CISA added both to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-05-20 (CISA, 2026-05-20). The Hacker News notes that the two descriptions overlap with RedSun and UnDefend, the Defender zero-days Nightmare Eclipse disclosed in April, and that Huntress has observed exploitation of both (The Hacker News, 2026-05-21).

Correction21 Oct 2026 16:01 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitleverification

The two flaws are fixed by separate updates rather than one combined out-of-band release: Malware Protection Engine version 1.1.26040.8 fixes CVE-2026-41091, and Microsoft typically ships engine updates once a month or as needed (MSRC, 2026-05-19); Antimalware Platform version 4.18.26040.7 fixes CVE-2026-45498, which is a denial of service (CWE-400), not a privilege escalation (MSRC, 2026-05-19). The "Turn off routine remediation" policy named earlier only decides whether Defender remediates detected threats automatically or prompts the user (Microsoft Learn); it does not hold back engine updates, so the check is whether engine and platform updates reach each host.

The hunt signals given earlier, junction events on Defender paths and SYSTEM processes spawned by MsMpEng.exe, have no source. The behavior observed in the wild is renamed exploit binaries staged in the user's Pictures and Downloads folders (Help Net Security, 2026-04-17) and, for RedSun, a Defender remediation of an EICAR test string whose file rewrite is redirected so that the Cloud Files infrastructure runs the attacker's binary as SYSTEM (Vectra AI, 2026-04-21). The researcher has since said CVE-2026-41091 is RedSun and CVE-2026-45498 is UnDefend (The Hacker News, 2026-05-21).

entries.headline: Lumen and PwC detail Showboat, a Linux implant that hides and proxies inside telcos, and Red Lamassu's JFMBackdoor
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB1

Showboat Linux post-exploitation framework and JFMBackdoor for Windows used against telecom providers; PwC attributes the operation to Red Lamassu (Calypso)

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs published Showboat on 2026-05-20: a modular Linux post-exploitation framework, used since at least mid-2022, that spawns a remote shell, uploads and downloads files, acts as a SOCKS5 proxy and port mapper into internal hosts, can persist as a service and swap C2 nodes, and has a "hide" command that conceals its process with code fetched from Pastebin or online forums used as a dead drop (Lumen, 2026-05-20). It reports the host data it gathers in a PNG field as an encrypted, base64-encoded string, and Lumen found it on VirusTotal rather than on a live system, so the initial access vector is unknown (Lumen, 2026-05-20). PwC, publishing in tandem on 2026-05-21, found a Showboat sample, which it calls kworker, in an open directory active from July to October 2025 next to JFMBackdoor: a batch script downloads the files into the victim's temp directory and runs the legitimate fltMC.exe, which side-loads a malicious FLTLIB.dll that decrypts its configuration and loads the backdoor in memory through a shellcode stub; JFMBackdoor then offers a remote shell, full file operations including timestomping, TCP proxying and screenshots it base64-encodes and XOR-encrypts for exfiltration (PwC, 2026-05-21). Lumen's telemetry confirms two victims, an Afghanistan-based ISP whose Outlook server talked to a C2 node from 2025-12-01 to 2026-02-03 and an entity in Azerbaijan, finds two potential compromises in the United States, and links C2 traffic with the Donbas region, with moderate confidence, to a separate cluster sharing the tooling; the C2 nodes cluster on a shared self-signed certificate (Lumen, 2026-05-20). PwC ties the open directory to a telecommunications provider in Afghanistan and attributes it to Red Lamassu (also known as Calypso), a China-based actor likely operating from Sichuan Province that it has tracked since 2019 against telecom organizations in Asia (PwC, 2026-05-21), while Lumen attributes Showboat only to at least one and likely several PRC-aligned clusters (Lumen, 2026-05-20).

Exposure
Telecommunications providers, chiefly in Asia and the Middle East (PwC, 2026-05-21) (Lumen, 2026-05-20), and in particular their Linux servers and routers, which Lumen notes typically run no EDR (Lumen, 2026-05-20).
Detection
Network and host telemetry on Linux servers: east-west traffic from servers that does not map to a business process, which Lumen recommends monitoring, and, from Showboat's functions, a server process fetching Pastebin or forum content, a SOCKS5 listener or port mapper on a server, and a new service persisting an unfamiliar binary (Lumen, 2026-05-20). On Windows, a legitimate binary such as fltMC.exe launched from the temp directory next to a FLTLIB.dll is the side-loading pattern PwC describes (PwC, 2026-05-21).
Defender takeaway
Telecom operators hunt their Linux server and router estate for these behaviors rather than waiting for EDR alerts; Lumen calls the presence of such implants an early warning sign of broader compromise (Lumen, 2026-05-20).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:43 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditbodyclassificationevent_dateevidenceheadlineregionssourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitlepriority

The confirmed victims are an Afghanistan-based ISP and an entity in Azerbaijan; Lumen calls the US cases potential compromises, links the traffic from Ukraine's Donbas region with moderate confidence to a separate cluster sharing the tooling, and neither source places European telecoms in the targeting (Lumen, 2026-05-20). Showboat is not described as masquerading as a kernel worker thread: kworker is PwC's name for the malware and the sample PwC found was named systemd-ac-update (PwC, 2026-05-21), while Lumen documents process hiding and service persistence (Lumen, 2026-05-20).

The campaign dates from at least mid-2022 (Lumen, 2026-05-20), whereas PwC has tracked Red Lamassu since 2019; JFMBackdoor offers remote shell access, file system operations, network proxying, screenshot capture and self-removal (PwC, 2026-05-21); and the self-signed certificate clusters the C2 nodes rather than linking the victims (Lumen, 2026-05-20).

entries.headline: Verizon's 2026 DBIR puts exploitation at 31% of breaches; only 26% of KEV-listed flaws were fully remediated
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Verizon 2026 DBIR: vulnerability exploitation overtakes stolen credentials as the leading initial access vector for the first time in 19 years

Verizon published its 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report on 2026-05-19, built on more than 31,000 security incidents, over 22,000 of them confirmed breaches, at organizations in 145 countries (Verizon 2026 DBIR); the incidents date from November 2024 to October 2025 (Help Net Security, 2026-05-20). Exploitation of vulnerabilities is the most common initial access vector at 31% of breaches, up from 20%, and for the first time in the report's 19 years it has passed stolen credentials (Verizon 2026 DBIR) (Verizon, 2026-05-19); credential abuse fell from 22% to 13%, partly because Verizon now tracks pretexting as its own vector, and would have been 16% without that change (Verizon 2026 DBIR). Only 26% of KEV-listed vulnerabilities were fully remediated in 2025, against 38% the year before, and the median time to full patching grew from 32 to 43 days (Verizon 2026 DBIR) (Help Net Security, 2026-05-20). Breaches involving a third party rose 60% and now account for 48% of all breaches (Verizon, 2026-05-19), while only 23% of third-party organizations fully remediated their MFA issues; ransomware was present in 48% of breaches, up from 44%, and 69% of ransomware victims did not pay (Help Net Security, 2026-05-20).

Defender takeaway
The benchmark bears on patching more than on detection: Help Net Security notes that the analysed data predates the rise of AI-assisted vulnerability research and that the problem is organizations not patching known vulnerabilities quickly or thoroughly enough (Help Net Security, 2026-05-20), so KEV remediation completeness and time to full patch are the measures to compare against the 26% and 43-day figures.
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:39 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditbodyclassificationdeep_divedeep_dive_categoryentitiesevent_dateevidenceheadlinekindprioritysectorssourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

The report covers more than 31,000 incidents and 22,000 confirmed breaches in 145 countries (Verizon 2026 DBIR) that date from November 2024 to October 2025 (Help Net Security, 2026-05-20), so its third-party growth reflects 2025 data and says nothing about campaigns active in May 2026 such as TeamPCP or Mini Shai-Hulud. The 26% is the share of KEV-listed vulnerabilities fully remediated by the organizations polled, not a share of organizations bound by BOD 22-01 missing deadlines, and 23% is the share of third-party organizations that fully remediated their MFA issues (Help Net Security, 2026-05-20). Exploitation rose from 20% to 31% in one year rather than over three cycles, and credential abuse fell from 22% to 13%, a drop Verizon partly ascribes to tracking pretexting separately (Verizon 2026 DBIR).

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: PinTheft gives a local user root through an RDS zerocopy double-free, wherever the RDS kernel module is loaded
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-43494updatedNATOB2

PinTheft: Linux kernel RDS zerocopy double-free (CVE-2026-43494) turned into a root exploit through io_uring fixed buffers, public PoC; V12 found RDS loaded by default only on Arch Linux among the distributions it tested

V12 Security released PinTheft with a proof-of-concept exploit on 2026-05-19, and Gentoo's Sam James relayed it to the oss-security list the same day; Aaron Esau of the V12 team found the bug (oss-security, 2026-05-19). In the RDS zerocopy send path, rds_message_zcopy_from_user() pins user pages one at a time; when a later page faults, the error path drops the pages already pinned while the scatterlist entries stay live, so message cleanup drops them again and each failed send steals a reference from the first page (oss-security, 2026-05-19). The exploit registers an anonymous page as an io_uring fixed buffer, which gives it a FOLL_PIN bias of 1024 references, steals those references with failing RDS zerocopy sends, lets the page be reclaimed as page cache of a SUID-root binary and overwrites it through the stale fixed-buffer pointer with a small ELF payload, so running the binary drops into a root shell (oss-security, 2026-05-19). It needs the RDS modules, io_uring enabled, a readable SUID-root binary and x86_64 for the included payload (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20). The bug was patched upstream earlier in May (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20), and the kernel CNA published that fix, which resets op_nents in rds_message_zcopy_from_user(), as CVE-2026-43494 (CVSS 7.8) on 2026-05-21 (ENISA EUVD-2026-31267).

Exposure
Linux hosts that load the RDS modules (CONFIG_RDS with CONFIG_RDS_TCP), which V12 found enabled by default only on Arch Linux among the common distributions it tested (oss-security, 2026-05-19), and that have the io_uring I/O API enabled (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20).
Detection
Process and syscall telemetry: an unprivileged process that opens RDS sockets, registers an io_uring fixed buffer and issues a burst of failing RDS zerocopy sends, then executes a SUID-root binary that yields a root shell, is the exploit's sequence (oss-security, 2026-05-19).
Defender takeaway
Install the fixed kernel; where that cannot happen at once, unload rds_tcp and rds and block both from loading through modprobe configuration, the mitigation BleepingComputer gives (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20); hosts that never load RDS are not reachable by this exploit.
Improvement21 Oct 2026 20:35 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevent_dateevidenceheadlinekindsourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

V12 found the RDS module (CONFIG_RDS with CONFIG_RDS_TCP) enabled by default only on Arch Linux among the common distributions it tested; it did not establish that the module is off on every other distribution (oss-security, 2026-05-19). Aaron Esau of V12 found the bug and V12 released the exploit, which Gentoo's Sam James relayed to oss-security (oss-security, 2026-05-19). The kernel fix was published as CVE-2026-43494 (CVSS 7.8) on 2026-05-21 (ENISA EUVD-2026-31267), and the mitigation for hosts that cannot take the fixed kernel yet is to unload and block the rds_tcp and rds modules (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20).

The bug was patched upstream earlier in May and the kernel fix was published as CVE-2026-43494 (CVSS 7.8) on 2026-05-21; exploitation needs the RDS modules, which V12 found loaded by default only on Arch Linux among common distributions.

entries.headline: Keycloak 26.6.2: a crafted link can hand an attacker the victim's session, up to the master-realm admin account
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-7507 +5updatedNATOA2

Keycloak 26.6.2 fixes 16 security issues, among them an OIDC login session fixation (CVE-2026-7507) and a WebAuthn execute-actions token replay (CVE-2026-37982)

The Keycloak project released 26.6.2 on 2026-05-19 with fixes for 16 security issues carrying 18 CVE ids, several of them in bundled third-party components such as Bouncy Castle (Keycloak, 2026-05-19); BSI's WID-SEC-2026-1612, first released at 22:00 UTC that day, lists nine of the Keycloak CVEs and rates them high (BSI WID-SEC-2026-1612). CVE-2026-7507, which Red Hat calls a critical session fixation flaw although it scores CVSS 7.5, lets an unauthenticated attacker pre-create an authentication session and lure a victim to a crafted link: the /login-actions/restart endpoint lacks CSRF protection and cookie ownership checks, so single sign-on authenticates the victim and the attacker takes over the required-action form, which in default deployments reaches full takeover of the master-realm admin account (Red Hat CVE-2026-7507). CVE-2026-37982 (6.8) lets an attacker who intercepts an execute-actions e-mail link replay its token and register their own WebAuthn authenticator on the victim's account, where WebAuthn required actions are enabled (Red Hat CVE-2026-37982). CVE-2026-37979 (6.5) lets any confidential client with valid credentials read, through the token introspection endpoint, claims of lightweight access tokens meant for other resource servers (Red Hat CVE-2026-37979); CVE-2026-4630 (6.8) lets an authenticated client that knows the UUID of another resource server's resource in the same realm read, change or delete it through the Authorization Services Protection API (Red Hat CVE-2026-4630); CVE-2026-37978 (4.9) lets a low-privilege administrator with the view-clients role read other users' profile and role data through the evaluate-scopes Admin API (Red Hat CVE-2026-37978); and CVE-2026-6856 lets an authenticator that sends self-attestation bypass the acceptable-AAGUID allowlist during WebAuthn registration (Keycloak issue #48388). Red Hat fixed CVE-2026-7507 in Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.2.16 (RHSA-2026:19594) and it, CVE-2026-37982, CVE-2026-37979, CVE-2026-4630 and CVE-2026-37978 in 26.4.12 (RHSA-2026:19596).

Exposure
Keycloak before 26.6.2; CVE-2026-7507 needs only a victim who follows a link, while the others need a confidential or authenticated client, an intercepted execute-actions e-mail link or an administrator holding view-clients (Red Hat CVE-2026-7507) (Red Hat CVE-2026-37982) (Red Hat CVE-2026-37978).
Detection
Keycloak user and admin event logs: CVE-2026-37982 ends in an attacker's WebAuthn authenticator on the victim account, which Red Hat calls persistent account takeover (Red Hat CVE-2026-37982), so the upgrade does not remove it; review WebAuthn credentials registered through execute-actions links before the upgrade.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade Keycloak to 26.6.2 (Keycloak, 2026-05-19), or Red Hat build of Keycloak to 26.4.12 or 26.2.16 on those branches (RHSA-2026:19596) (RHSA-2026:19594); deployments whose users could be sent a crafted login link are the first in line because of CVE-2026-7507.
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:33 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesentitiesevent_dateevidenceheadlineregionssectorssourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitleverification

CVE-2026-4630 is not a cross-realm flaw: it lets an authenticated client reach another resource server's resources within the same realm (Red Hat CVE-2026-4630). CVE-2026-7507 works through the /login-actions/restart endpoint, with an attacker-created authentication session and a crafted link the victim follows, not through a crafted state parameter (Red Hat CVE-2026-7507), and CVE-2026-37982 needs an intercepted execute-actions e-mail link (Red Hat CVE-2026-37982). The highlighted CVEs carry Red Hat CVSS scores from 4.9 to 7.5 rather than none, CVE-2026-37979, CVE-2026-4630 and CVE-2026-37978 need an authenticated client or administrator, and the release fixes 16 issues with 18 CVE ids, nine of which BSI lists (Keycloak, 2026-05-19) (BSI WID-SEC-2026-1612). No source links the release to the Akira ransomware group.

entries.classification_html: NATOB1
entries.headline: ChromaDB CVE-2026-45829: one unauthenticated create-collection request runs attacker Python on the Python FastAPI server
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-45829updatedNATOB1

CVE-2026-45829: ChromaDB's Python FastAPI server runs an attacker's model code before checking authentication (CVSS 4.0 10.0), no fix in 1.5.9

HiddenLayer discovered CVE-2026-45829 in ChromaDB's Python FastAPI server and gave it the maximum severity score (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19); Hadrian, which published a technical analysis the same day, gives CVSS 4.0 10.0 and repeats HiddenLayer's name for it, "ChromaToast", (Hadrian, 2026-05-19). The create-collection handler loads the request's embedding-function configuration before it checks authentication: with trust_remote_code set to true and model_name pointed at a HuggingFace repository or local path the attacker controls, the server downloads and instantiates the model and runs the attacker's Python inside the uvicorn server process (Hadrian, 2026-05-19), and only then rejects the request, with a 500 in HiddenLayer's description (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19). Every Python FastAPI server from 1.0.0 is affected while the default Rust frontend does not use this code path, and there was no fixed version at the time of writing, 1.5.9 being the latest (Hadrian, 2026-05-19). HiddenLayer reports an initial acknowledgement on 2025-12-16 followed by silence across more than ten follow-ups (Hadrian, 2026-05-19), and its Shodan queries found roughly 73% of internet-exposed instances running a vulnerable version (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19); Hadrian dates the report to 2025-11-28 (Hadrian, 2026-05-19), BleepingComputer to February 17 (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19).

Exposure
Deployments that expose the Python FastAPI server, used by many self-hosters, development instances and the chromadb[server] distribution (Hadrian, 2026-05-19); local deployments without an exposed API server and the Rust frontend are not affected (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19).
Detection
Web access logs and egress: a POST /api/v2/tenants/.../collections that returns 500 with a body mentioning trust_remote_code, sentence_transformers, transformers, auto_map or model-loader errors, and outbound connections to HuggingFace from the Chroma server process (Hadrian, 2026-05-19). A server with such hits ran the payload with its own rights before the request was rejected, so mitigating afterwards does not clear it.

Triage: HuggingFace downloads started by your own ingestion code are normal; the same download from the Chroma server process that your ingestion code did not initiate is the signal (Hadrian, 2026-05-19).

Defender takeaway
Until a fix is confirmed, run the Rust frontend or keep the Python server off public networks and restrict network access to the ChromaDB API port (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19); Hadrian also describes a local hotfix for 1.5.9 that moves the authentication check ahead of the configuration loader and strips trust_remote_code from the embedding-function arguments (Hadrian, 2026-05-19).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:30 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevidenceheadlinesectorssourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitle

No server-wide setting turns trust_remote_code off: the flag travels in the attacker's own create-collection request, inside the embedding-function arguments (Hadrian, 2026-05-19), and the sourced mitigations are the Rust frontend, keeping the Python server off public networks and restricting access to the API port (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19). The rejection that follows the payload is a 500 in HiddenLayer's description (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19) and in Hadrian's own proof of concept, although Hadrian's summary says 403 (Hadrian, 2026-05-19). HiddenLayer discovered and scored the flaw (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-19), and Hadrian published the technical analysis (Hadrian, 2026-05-19).

vulnerability21 May 05:00Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Hadrian · BleepingComputer

Every Python server from 1.0.0 is affected, the default Rust frontend is not, and no fixed version existed as of 2026-05-19, 1.5.9 being the latest.

entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: Azure Local Disconnected Operations CVE-2026-42822 scores 10.0, but Microsoft's realistic attacker is an insider
entries.html:
ROUTINECVE-2026-42822updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-42822: improper authentication in Azure Local Disconnected Operations allows privilege escalation over the network (CVSS 10.0), fixed in ALDO 2604

Microsoft published CVE-2026-42822 on 2026-05-18: improper authentication (CWE-287) in Azure Local Disconnected Operations (ALDO) allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network, scored CVSS 10.0 with a scope change and rated Exploitation More Likely, though not exploited or publicly disclosed at release (MSRC, 2026-05-18). Microsoft says the most realistic scenario is a malicious or compromised insider who already has access to the internal environment and holds tenant or user identifiers, credentials or tokens; an external attacker would first need access to the internal network and valid identity context, and ALDO is designed to run disconnected and isolated (MSRC, 2026-05-18). The fix is ALDO version 2604 or later, delivered only as a full system update through the Azure portal, and ALDO is a restricted offering whose updates reach approved, allow-listed customers (MSRC, 2026-05-18).

Exposure
Only ALDO deployments, which Microsoft offers to approved customers; the attacker needs a foothold and identity context inside the disconnected environment (MSRC, 2026-05-18).
Defender takeaway
Approved ALDO customers schedule the full system update to version 2604 or later (MSRC, 2026-05-18); with an insider precondition and no exploitation known it is a planned update, not an emergency, and Azure customers without ALDO have no decision to make.
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:29 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitle

In practice the flaw is not a no-credentials, no-foothold remote bug: Microsoft's realistic scenario is a malicious or compromised insider with existing access and identity material, and an external attacker would first need access to the internal network and valid identity context (MSRC, 2026-05-18). The advisory does not say that cloud-managed Azure was already protected while manual stacks were not: the affected product is ALDO, and its fix is version 2604 or later, applied as a full system update through the Azure portal. No source says ALDO is common in German or Swiss federal administrations; Microsoft describes it as a restricted offering for approved customers (MSRC, 2026-05-18).

entries.headline: Carding shop B1ack's Stash dumps 4.6M stolen card records, about 70% US-issued, to punish its own sellers
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOB2

B1ack's Stash carding marketplace releases about 4.6 million stolen payment card records for free

SOCRadar reported on 2026-05-18 that B1ack's Stash, a dark-web carding marketplace operating since at least 2023, suspended about 8 million stolen CVV2 records from its inventory because sellers had resold its cards in competing shops, and released about 4.6 million of them as a free download (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18). Each record holds the full card number, expiry date, CVV2, cardholder name, billing address, e-mail, phone number and IP address; SOCRadar assesses that the data likely comes from e-commerce skimming or phishing operations, and about 70% of the records belong to US cardholders, followed by Canada, the United Kingdom, France and Malaysia (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18). After SOCRadar filtered out expired and duplicate records, roughly 4.3 million appear fresh and usable, and the marketplace has used free releases as marketing before, one million cards in April 2024 and over four million records in February 2025 (Security Affairs, 2026-05-20).

Exposure
Card issuers and merchants whose cardholders appear in the dump, overwhelmingly in the US; Europe appears mainly through UK and French cards (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18).
Detection
Payment fraud telemetry: SOCRadar expects card-not-present fraud to accelerate in the weeks after the release, and complete billing addresses make address verification easy to pass (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18).
Defender takeaway
For card-fraud teams the decision is SOCRadar's recommendation to review card-not-present fraud thresholds for transactions whose billing details match the dataset's patterns (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18); organizations without a card portfolio or merchant estate have no decision to make.
Improvement21 Oct 2026 20:28 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditbodyclassificationentitiesevent_dateevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitleverificationpriority

The release was reported on 2026-05-18 and is part of about 8 million CVV2 records the marketplace suspended (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18); the estimate of roughly 4.3 million fresh records is Security Affairs' account of SOCRadar's filtering (Security Affairs, 2026-05-20). SOCRadar assesses only that the data likely comes from e-commerce skimming or phishing (SOCRadar, 2026-05-18); no source names WooCommerce or Magento storefronts or a root cause shared across the marketplace's releases.

entries.headline: Patched SonicWall Gen6 SSL-VPNs still let brute-forced accounts skip MFA unless the LDAP fix is redone by hand
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2024-12802exploitedupdatedNATOB2

SonicWall Gen6 SSL-VPN: patched-firmware appliances still open to the CVE-2024-12802 MFA bypass without manual LDAP remediation, exploited February to March 2026 by a suspected access broker

SonicWall's SNWLID-2025-0001 describes CVE-2024-12802 (CWE-305, CVSS 6.5): when SSL-VPN authenticates against Microsoft Active Directory, UPN and SAM account names are handled separately, so MFA can be configured independently for each and an attacker can bypass it through the alternative account name (SonicWall SNWLID-2025-0001); in practice an attacker with valid credentials authenticates without the MFA step (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20). On Gen6 the fixed firmware does not remove the vulnerable LDAP configuration, so six manual steps are needed: delete the LDAP configuration that uses userPrincipalName, remove cached LDAP users, remove the SSL VPN user domain, reboot, recreate the LDAP configuration without userPrincipalName and take a fresh backup (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20); Gen7 firmware version 7.2.0-7015 and Gen8 firmware version 8.0.1-8017 build those steps in (SonicWall SNWLID-2025-0001). ReliaQuest responded to intrusions between February and March 2026 on Gen6 devices that looked patched and assesses with medium confidence that they are the first in-the-wild exploitation; the attacker brute-forced VPN accounts with an automated tool, in one case after only 13 attempts, and reached a file server within 30 minutes (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19), connected to it over RDP with a shared local administrator password, and tried to deploy a Cobalt Strike beacon and a vulnerable driver to disable endpoint protection, both blocked by EDR (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20). ReliaQuest describes the tools as consistent with actors in the ransomware ecosystem and the logouts and later re-entries with other accounts as initial access broker activity (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19); the researchers could not attribute the attacks, though the activity resembled the Akira ransomware group's (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-19).

Exposure
SonicWall Gen6 firewalls and NSv appliances running SSL-VPN with LDAP authentication against Active Directory where the LDAP configuration used userPrincipalName, even on the fixed firmware, until all six remediation steps are done; affected builds are firmware version 6.5.4.15-117n and older and NSv firmware version 6.5.4.4-44v-21-2457 and older (SonicWall SNWLID-2025-0001) (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20). The advisory also lists Gen7 builds up to 7.1.2-7019, the Gen8 TZ80 on 8.0.0-8035 and SMA100 10.2.1.13-72sv and older, fixed from 7.0.1-5169 or 7.2.0-7015, 8.0.1-8017 and 10.2.1.14-75sv (SonicWall SNWLID-2025-0001). Gen6 reached end-of-life on 2026-04-16 (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-19).
Detection
SonicWall authentication logs forwarded with the Authentication category: rapid logins with session type sess="CLI" from VPS and VPN hosting ranges, together with Event ID 238 (failed VPN login) or Event ID 1080 (successful SSL VPN zone login), and after a success a change of the session type from CLI to GMS, which marks hands-on access to internal resources (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19). Completing the LDAP remediation does not undo access already taken: the actor came back days later with other accounts, so the VPN accounts that authenticated through the bypass need new credentials and an audit of their privileges (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19).

Triage: where no CLI-based VPN client is authorized or typical, any sess="CLI" event is a high-fidelity indicator; where scripted VPN authentication is legitimate, ReliaQuest says to baseline it and tune on volume, source IP and timing (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19).

Defender takeaway
Treat a Gen6 SSL-VPN as exposed until all six remediation steps are confirmed, whatever its firmware version shows, because patch dashboards cannot tell patched from fully remediated (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19); with Gen6 out of support, the lasting fix is a move to supported hardware (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:37 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesentitiesevent_dateevidenceheadlineregionssectorssourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitle

SonicWall scores CVE-2024-12802 CVSS 6.5 with a vector that requires a low-privileged account (PR:L), not 9.1 for an unauthenticated attacker; 9.1 is the assessment of CISA's Authorized Data Publisher (SonicWall SNWLID-2025-0001) (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19), and the attacker needs valid credentials, which here were brute-forced. The attacks are not attributed: ReliaQuest describes a likely initial access broker using tools of the ransomware ecosystem, and the researchers could not attribute them, only compare them with Akira's 2025 activity (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19) (Cybersecurity Dive, 2026-05-19).

The six remediation steps come from SonicWall's advisory as BleepingComputer lists them (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-20). The detection signal ReliaQuest found is the sess="CLI" session type with Event IDs 238 and 1080 and a CLI-to-GMS transition, not UPN-format login names (ReliaQuest, 2026-05-19).

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: ESET: China-aligned Webworm targeted governments in Belgium, Italy, Serbia and Poland with Discord and OneDrive implants
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2017-7692updatedNATOB2

Webworm (China-aligned) turns to European government targets with the EchoCreep (Discord) and GraphWorm (Microsoft Graph and OneDrive) backdoors, ESET reports

ESET Research published its analysis of Webworm, a China-aligned group active since at least 2022 that it links to SixLittleMonkeys and FishMonger, on 2026-05-20: in 2025 the group moved from Asia to governmental organizations in Belgium, Italy, Serbia and Poland, compromised a South African university, and replaced its Trochilus and McRat backdoors with two new ones, EchoCreep and GraphWorm (ESET, 2026-05-20). ESET told The Hacker News that a link to Space Pirates is tenuous at best (The Hacker News, 2026-05-20). ESET could not find the entry point, but an operator server showed nuclei and dirsearch scans of 56 targets in countries including Spain, Hungary, Belgium, Nigeria, Czechia and Serbia, and a public exploit for the SquirrelMail post-authentication RCE CVE-2017-7692 run against a Serbian webmail target, which suggests the group held that victim's credentials (ESET, 2026-05-20).

EchoCreep and GraphWorm. EchoCreep, written in Go, sends all its traffic through Discord API endpoints, decodes commands with base64 and AES-CBC-128, runs them through cmd.exe and uploads files as attachments; it reports to per-victim channels, named after the victim's IP address or IP address and hostname, that the operators created before it first ran, and it runs under a custom scheduled task and carries a modified timestamp (ESET, 2026-05-20). ESET decrypted 433 messages going back to 2024-03-21 across four victim channels; the first real compromise came on 2025-04-09, followed by curl downloads (ESET, 2026-05-20). GraphWorm runs at every user logon through registry Run keys and talks only to OneDrive endpoints of Microsoft Graph, with a valid cloud account and API tokens, fetching jobs from and uploading results to a per-victim folder; it encrypts traffic with AES-256-CBC and base64, stages command output in a local file that it deletes after upload, and likely uses Graph's upload-session endpoint for large files (ESET, 2026-05-20).

Proxies, staging and stolen data. The proxy tools WormFrp, a modified frp that reads AES-encrypted configurations from a compromised third-party Amazon S3 bucket, ChainWorm, SmuxProxy and WormSocket build internal, external and multi-hop proxies through rented servers and VPS hosts, the group staged tools in a GitHub repository, and both the repository and the S3 bucket have been taken down (ESET, 2026-05-20). The S3 bucket held virtual-machine snapshots, one with the state of an Italian governmental machine, and from December 2025 to January 2026 an mRemoteNG connection-configuration file and a Visio infrastructure diagram taken from a Spanish governmental entity; in October 2025 the operators also uploaded SharpSecretsdump, a tool that mimics Impacket's secretsdump (ESET, 2026-05-20).

Exposure
Governmental organizations in Europe, Webworm's focus since 2025, and in particular internet-facing web servers and webmail, which the group scans and probes (ESET, 2026-05-20).
Detection
Egress and endpoint telemetry: Discord API traffic from hosts or processes with no business use of Discord, Microsoft Graph OneDrive calls from an unexpected process, new scheduled tasks and Run-key entries starting unfamiliar binaries, and frp-style reverse and SOCKS5 proxies opening outbound connections (ESET, 2026-05-20). Because ESET reads the SquirrelMail exploit as run with the victim's own credentials, a webmail account it touched needs a new password after clean-up.
Defender takeaway
European government networks hunt for the Discord and OneDrive command channels and the proxy tooling described above, and review webmail and web servers for the scanning and the SquirrelMail exploitation ESET found (ESET, 2026-05-20).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:41 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditbodyclassificationcvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

FishMonger (which The Hacker News also calls Aquatic Panda (The Hacker News, 2026-05-20)), SixLittleMonkeys and Space Pirates are not other names for Webworm: ESET links Webworm to SixLittleMonkeys and FishMonger as related China-aligned groups (ESET, 2026-05-20) and calls the Space Pirates link tenuous at best (The Hacker News, 2026-05-20). EchoCreep does not create its Discord channels: it reports to channels the operators made before it first ran, which suggests they knew their targets or had gathered the details after initial access (ESET, 2026-05-20). The S3 bucket was a compromised third-party bucket that has since been taken down, and SharpSecretsdump, which mimics Impacket's secretsdump rather than dumping LSASS memory, was only seen uploaded to it (ESET, 2026-05-20).

A compromised third-party Amazon S3 bucket held its proxy configurations and files taken from Italian and Spanish governmental entities; ESET could not find the entry point, but the group scanned victims' web servers and ran a public SquirrelMail exploit (CVE-2017-7692) against a Serbian webmail target.
