The March wave was GitHub Actions and Open VSX extensions and the KICS Docker image came in April; the PCPJack worm, LLM API key targeting and Checkmarx One API tokens are not part of this incident. Exposure covers any instance that installed build 2026.5.09 between 2026-05-09 01:25 and 2026-05-10 08:47 UTC, and TeamPCP's role rests on its own claim.

entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: Attackers exploited Škoda's German accessories-shop software; logs cannot show which customer data was copied
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

Škoda Auto Deutschland accessories-shop breach: attackers exploited the shop software, customer data and password hashes were accessible, logs cannot show what was copied

Škoda Auto Deutschland's security monitoring found that unauthorised parties had exploited a vulnerability in the standard shop software of its online accessories shop and gained temporary access to the shop system; the shop was taken offline, the vulnerability fixed, an external IT forensics firm engaged and the incident reported to the competent data-protection authority (Škoda Auto Deutschland). The shop stores names and addresses, email addresses and sometimes telephone numbers, order information and customer-account credentials made up of the email address and a password kept as a cryptographic hash; full credit card data is processed only by the payment providers (Škoda Auto Deutschland). Škoda's analysis found that access to the stored data was possible in principle, but the nature of its logs does not allow it to reconstruct whether and to what extent data was actually copied or retrieved, and it has no concrete indication of misuse (Škoda Auto Deutschland). Only the accessories shop run by Škoda Auto Deutschland GmbH for customers in Germany was affected, not other Škoda online shops, the systems of the manufacturer Škoda Auto a.s. or the Škoda Connect portal (Škoda Auto Deutschland). SecurityWeek reported the disclosure on 2026-05-11 and noted that the number of affected customers had not been disclosed (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-11).

Exposure
Customers of the German Škoda accessories shop, above all those who reuse its password elsewhere: Škoda expects phishing that refers to earlier orders and login attempts with the known credentials, especially where the same password serves several services (Škoda Auto Deutschland).
Defender takeaway
Affected customers change any password they reused from the shop and treat messages about Škoda orders with suspicion, as Škoda advises (Škoda Auto Deutschland); for other organisations the case changes no decision, since neither the shop software nor the vulnerability is named (Škoda Auto Deutschland).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:44 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationconfidenceentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

Škoda Auto Deutschland reported the incident to the competent data-protection authority but does not say when, so no 72-hour timing can be stated (Škoda Auto Deutschland). Its own words on the data are that access to the stored data was possible in principle and that, because of the nature of the available logs, it cannot reconstruct in every detail whether and to what extent data was actually copied or retrieved (translated from German); the shop concerned is only the German accessories shop, while other Škoda shops, the manufacturer's systems and Škoda Connect are unaffected and full card data is not stored there (Škoda Auto Deutschland). The step Škoda gives customers is to change passwords reused from the shop and to watch for messages that refer to their Škoda orders (Škoda Auto Deutschland).

entries.action_label: West Pharmaceutical discloses data theft and…

entries.headline: West Pharmaceutical discloses data theft and encryption in an 8-K; core systems restored, sites restarting
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

West Pharmaceutical Services 8-K Item 1.05: data exfiltrated and systems encrypted, global operations partly restarted

West Pharmaceutical Services determined on 2026-05-07 that it had suffered a material cybersecurity attack in which an unauthorized party exfiltrated data and encrypted some systems; after detecting the intrusion on 2026-05-04 it took systems offline globally, notified law enforcement and engaged external forensic experts, and the 8-K filed on 2026-05-11 says the business was disrupted globally, core enterprise systems were restored and shipping, receiving and manufacturing had restarted at some sites, with no timeline yet for complete restoration and no access vector or exfiltration method stated (SEC 8-K, 2026-05-11). The company, which specialises in injectable drug packaging, syringe and vial components, containment systems and drug delivery devices, engaged Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 for incident response, and no ransomware group had taken credit as of 2026-05-13 (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-13).

Defender takeaway
No detection or patching decision follows, since the filing gives no access vector; for West's customers the question was supply continuity while its sites were being restored (SEC 8-K, 2026-05-11).
Improvement21 Oct 2026 20:45 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationconfidenceentitiesevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

The 8-K says that data was exfiltrated and some systems encrypted, but not how the data left or how the attacker got in, and that the investigation into the scope and the data affected was ongoing (SEC 8-K, 2026-05-11). No ransomware group had taken credit as of 2026-05-13, and West specialises in injectable drug packaging, syringe and vial components, containment systems and drug delivery devices (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-13); no cited source describes which European supply lines depend on it or what detection preceded the encryption.

entries.action_label: German police shut down the relaunched Crimenetwork…
entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: German police shut down the relaunched Crimenetwork marketplace; suspected operator arrested in Mallorca
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

BKA and ZIT shut down the relaunched Crimenetwork darknet marketplace; suspected German operator arrested in Mallorca on a European Arrest Warrant

A special unit of the Spanish National Police arrested the suspected 35-year-old German operator of the relaunched Crimenetwork marketplace at his residence in Mallorca under a European Arrest Warrant, in an operation with Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) and the Frankfurt am Main Public Prosecutor's Office's Central Office for Combating Internet Crime (ZIT); he is accused under Section 127 of the German Criminal Code of operating criminal trading platforms, and of narcotics trafficking (Help Net Security, 2026-05-11). Authorities say he built new infrastructure for Crimenetwork a few days after the previous version was shut down and its administrator arrested in December 2024; the BKA calls the marketplace one of the central marketplaces of the German-speaking underground economy for many years (Help Net Security, 2026-05-11). The relaunched platform offered stolen data, drugs, forged documents and other illegal services to more than 22,000 users and over 100 vendors, took payment in Bitcoin, Litecoin and Monero and earned an estimated more than €3.6 million in commissions and vendor fees; about €194,000 in assets were preliminarily seized (Help Net Security, 2026-05-11).

Defender takeaway
No defender decision follows; the seized user and transaction data are expected to support further investigations into the platform's users and operators, who are believed to be mainly in German-speaking countries (Help Net Security, 2026-05-11).
Improvement21 Oct 2026 20:39 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditbodyclassificationconfidenceentitiesevent_dateevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytitletechniques

The arrest in Mallorca was made by a special unit of the Spanish National Police in the operation with the BKA and ZIT, and the BKA describes Crimenetwork as one of the central marketplaces of the German-speaking underground economy, relaunched a few days after its December 2024 takedown (Help Net Security, 2026-05-11). The seized user and transaction data are expected to support further investigations into the platform's users and operators, believed to be mainly in German-speaking countries (Help Net Security, 2026-05-11).

entries.headline: ICO fines South Staffordshire £963,900: a 20-month phishing foothold, ZeroLogon on two DCs and only 5% of IT monitored
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2020-1472exploitedupdatedNATOA2

ICO fines South Staffordshire Water £963,900 under UK GDPR for the 2020 to 2022 intrusion: phishing foothold, ZeroLogon on two unpatched domain controllers, 5% of IT monitored

The UK Information Commissioner's Office fined South Staffordshire Plc and South Staffordshire Water Plc £963,900 for infringing Articles 5(1)(f) and 32(1) of the UK GDPR (ICO enforcement action), after a 40% reduction for the company's early admission, which it accepted without appeal (ICO, 2026-05-11). The attack began in September 2020 with a phishing email whose attachment, once opened, let the attacker install malicious software that stayed undetected for 20 months; in May 2022 the attacker moved through the network and compromised domain administrator privileges, and the breach was found only when IT performance problems started an internal investigation on 15 July 2022, followed by a ransom note on 26 July (ICO, 2026-05-11). Two domain controllers were unpatched against ZeroLogon (CVE-2020-1472) in May 2022, and while the incident did not start through it, the attacker exploited it during the incident (ICO penalty notice). The company held data on about 1.85 million customers, around 750,000 current and 1.1 million former, and on its staff; the personal data of 633,887 people was published on the dark web, part of over 4.1 TB of data, including online-service usernames and passwords, bank account numbers and sort codes, employees' National Insurance numbers and information from which disabilities of Priority Services Register customers could be inferred (ICO, 2026-05-11). The ICO does not name the attacker; The Record and The Register attribute the attack to Cl0p, which claimed it, and the penalty notice makes no reference to any compromise of operational or water-treatment systems (The Record, 2026-05-11; The Register, 2026-05-11).

Exposure
The failures the ICO found: limited controls that let the attacker escalate to administrator after the first foothold, monitoring of only 5% of the IT environment, Windows Server 2003 still in use, unpatched critical systems and no regular internal or external security scans (ICO, 2026-05-11). ZeroLogon lets an unauthenticated attacker who connects to a domain controller over the Netlogon Remote Protocol obtain domain administrator access (Microsoft, CVE-2020-1472).
Detection
Coverage of endpoint telemetry in the SIEM is the gap the notice names: in December 2021 a third-party security operations centre monitored only 5% of the IT environment, and endpoint telemetry and logging were not integrated into the security monitoring platform (ICO penalty notice).
Defender takeaway
For UK data controllers, the ICO treats missing monitoring coverage, unsupported software and unpatched domain controllers as a breach of the UK GDPR security duty, and asks whether logging and monitoring cover the IT environment and alerts are acted on (ICO, 2026-05-11); domain controllers still without Microsoft's Netlogon updates of August 2020 remain exposed to the same escalation (Microsoft, CVE-2020-1472).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:43 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesentitiesevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitle

The ICO itself names the vulnerability: two domain controllers were unpatched against ZeroLogon (CVE-2020-1472) in May 2022, and the attacker exploited it during the incident, although the incident did not start through it (ICO penalty notice); it is the Cl0p attribution that comes from The Record and The Register (The Record, 2026-05-11). The sequence was a phishing attachment opened in September 2020, malicious software undetected for 20 months, then movement through the network and domain-admin compromise from May 2022, with the breach found on 15 July 2022 (ICO, 2026-05-11). The monitoring gap was concrete: a third-party security operations centre covered 5% of the IT environment and endpoint telemetry was not in the SIEM (ICO penalty notice). The fine is a UK GDPR penalty under Articles 5(1)(f) and 32(1) (ICO enforcement action); the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill was still expected to be introduced to Parliament (The Record, 2026-05-11).

entries.headline: A crafted SOAP envelope can make PHP reuse a freed object; PHP fixed it with two narrower SOAP flaws on 2026-05-07
entries.html:
ROUTINECVE-2026-6722 +2updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-6722: PHP SOAP extension use-after-free in the ref_map deduplication can lead to code execution, fixed in PHP 8.2.31 to 8.5.6

PHP 8.2.31, 8.3.31, 8.4.21 and 8.5.6, released on 2026-05-07, fix three flaws in the SOAP extension (php.watch, 2026-05-07) (PHP 8 ChangeLog). The serious one, CVE-2026-6722, is a use-after-free: ext-soap remembers decoded PHP objects in SOAP_GLOBAL(ref_map) for id/href deduplication without holding a reference, so an apache:Map with a duplicate key and an empty value frees an object while the map still points to it, and a later href reuses the freed memory, which PHP's advisory says can lead to remote code execution (PHP, GHSA-85c2-q967-79q5). The advisory includes a reproducer (PHP, GHSA-85c2-q967-79q5). PHP rates it High in that advisory, and the CVE record PHP published as the numbering authority scores it 9.5 under CVSS 4.0, with high attack complexity and attack requirements present (ENISA EUVD, EUVD-2026-28966).

The two companion flaws are narrower. CVE-2026-7261 is a use-after-free when a header handler returns false or throws while the server uses SOAP_PERSISTENCE_SESSION (PHP, GHSA-m33r-qmcv-p97q); CVE-2026-7262 is a NULL pointer dereference in the apache:Map decoder when the server has a typemap configured, a denial of service that PHP's advisory scores 6.3 under CVSS 4.0 (PHP, GHSA-hmxp-6pc4-f3vv); its CVE record scores 2.9, the same base vector with the threat metric for a public proof of concept added (ENISA EUVD, EUVD-2026-28971). No source reports exploitation.

Exposure
A SoapServer reachable by untrusted clients on PHP below 8.2.31, 8.3.31, 8.4.21 or 8.5.6 (PHP, GHSA-85c2-q967-79q5).
Defender takeaway
A patch-cycle upgrade for PHP hosts that expose SOAP endpoints; the use-after-free is triggered by a crafted envelope (PHP, GHSA-85c2-q967-79q5).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:44 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummaryevent_dateprioritytechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesclassificationdeep_divedeep_dive_categorybody

CVE-2026-7262 is a NULL pointer dereference that needs a typemap and causes a denial of service (PHP, GHSA-hmxp-6pc4-f3vv), and CVE-2026-7261 is a use-after-free that needs SOAP_PERSISTENCE_SESSION (PHP, GHSA-m33r-qmcv-p97q); neither was shown to give code execution. PHP's own advisory for CVE-2026-6722 includes a reproducer (PHP, GHSA-85c2-q967-79q5). The priority moves from notable to routine: no source reports exploitation, and the fix is a patch-cycle upgrade for PHP hosts.

Improvement21 Oct 2026 08:09 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-auditcvessourcesbody

The CVE record for CVE-2026-7262 scores it 2.9 under CVSS 4.0, against 6.3 in PHP's advisory: the base vector is the same, and the record adds the threat metric for a public proof of concept (ENISA EUVD, EUVD-2026-28971).

entries.headline: SMS blasters in Switzerland force nearby phones onto 2G to deliver spoofed phishing texts that bypass operator filters
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA1

SMS-blaster smishing in Switzerland: fake base stations push phones onto 2G and send spoofed texts past operator filters

BACS reported on 2025-09-09 that numerous fake parking-fine texts were reaching people in western Switzerland who had recently been in the places mentioned, and that one recipient's phone switched from 4G to 2G just before the message arrived, pointing to an SMS blaster (BACS, 2025-09-09). The device builds on IMSI-catcher technology: it poses as the best available mobile mast within a radius of 500 to 1,000 metres, forces connecting phones onto the outdated 2G standard and sends texts with forged sender information directly to the handset, bypassing the operator's SMS filters (BACS, 2025-09-09). In November 2025 Basel-Landschaft police arrested a suspect who had an SMS blaster in his car (SRF, 2025-11-13). On 2026-05-07 the awareness portal ebas.ch warned that the scam is establishing itself in Switzerland, with texts posing as authorities, banks or courier services that link to fake websites collecting credit card data or e-banking credentials and are adapted to the location, such as a parking fine where many cars are parked (ebas.ch, 2026-05-07).

Exposure
Any phone in range that still connects to 2G, which includes many modern smartphones; only SMS is affected, not services such as WhatsApp, Signal or Telegram (ebas.ch, 2026-05-07).
Detection
Handset network state as users report it: the phone drops from 4G to 2G shortly before the scam text arrives and returns to 4G immediately afterwards (BACS, 2025-09-09); the sender number is spoofed and cannot be verified or blocked (BACS, 2025-09-09).
Defender takeaway
On managed Android devices at API level 34 (Android 14) or later, a device owner or the owner of an organisation-owned managed profile can block 2G for the whole device with the DISALLOW_CELLULAR_2G restriction, and emergency calls still use 2G (Android Developers); iPhones cannot disable 2G directly, only through Lockdown Mode, which also limits other functions (ebas.ch, 2026-05-07).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:36 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

The Swiss signal predates the ebas.ch post: BACS reported in September 2025 that fake parking-fine texts in western Switzerland were being sent with SMS blasters (BACS, 2025-09-09), and Basel-Landschaft police arrested a suspect with such a device in his car in November 2025 (SRF, 2025-11-13). Blocking 2G on managed Android devices uses the DISALLOW_CELLULAR_2G user restriction, available from API level 34 and settable only by a device owner or the owner of an organisation-owned managed profile (Android Developers). The observable BACS describes is the handset itself switching from 4G to 2G just before the scam text and back to 4G afterwards (BACS, 2025-09-09); no cited source documents mobile-management products surfacing that switch.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: BSI rates two admin-authenticated pfSense CE code-execution flaws critical; Netgate disputes them and plans no patch
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2025-69690 +1updatedNATOB2

BSI lists two authenticated pfSense CE code-execution flaws as critical: CVE-2025-69690 (CE 2.7.2) and CVE-2025-69691 (CE 2.8.0), disputed by Netgate

BSI listed two Netgate pfSense Community Edition (CE) vulnerabilities in its advisory WID-SEC-2026-1435, released on 2026-05-08 (22:00 UTC on 2026-05-07), with severity critical: an attacker can exploit them to execute arbitrary code with administrator rights (BSI WID-SEC-W-2026-1435). Both come from a researcher's Full Disclosure post of 2026-02-16 (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16). CVE-2025-69690 affects pfSense CE 2.7.2: the configuration restore mechanism calls unserialize() on user-controlled data, so a crafted backup file carrying a serialized PHP object injects commands through its post_reboot_commands property, and they run through mwexec() as root (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16). CVE-2025-69691 affects pfSense CE 2.8.0: the XMLRPC API method pfsense.exec_php runs arbitrary PHP code as root (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16). The researcher scores them 8.8 and 9.9 under CVSS 3.1 (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16), and ENISA's EUVD records 9.1 and 9.9 (EUVD-2025-209738; EUVD-2025-209739).

According to the researcher, Netgate was notified on 2025-12-02, acknowledged the reports, classified both as expected behaviour for authenticated administrators and indicated that no patches would be issued (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16); the CVE records note that the supplier disputes them because the functions are only available to administrators, who are intentionally allowed to execute PHP code (EUVD-2025-209739). BSI's advisory names only pfSense CE 2.7.2 and CE 2.8.0 and references a public proof of concept (BSI WID-SEC-W-2026-1435).

Exposure
PfSense CE 2.7.2 (CVE-2025-69690) and CE 2.8.0 (CVE-2025-69691) (BSI WID-SEC-W-2026-1435), for anyone who can log in as administrator; the researcher notes the XMLRPC endpoint is enabled by default over HTTPS with Basic Authentication and that default administrator credentials are widely deployed (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16).
Detection
Firewall web and XMLRPC access logs: calls to the pfsense.exec_php method and configuration restores nobody scheduled, both made with administrator credentials (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16).
Defender takeaway
No patch is coming, so the decision is about the precondition: replace default administrator credentials and keep the management interface and XMLRPC off networks an attacker can reach; with that in place the flaws give nothing beyond what an administrator can already do, which is the supplier's position (EUVD-2025-209739).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:35 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationconfidencecvesevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitle

BSI's advisory states only that an attacker can exploit the flaws to run arbitrary code with administrator rights, rates them critical and names pfSense CE 2.7.2 and CE 2.8.0 (BSI WID-SEC-W-2026-1435); it carries no patch status and no mitigation, so it does not mark the CE build as unpatched or recommend a mitigation. Netgate disputes CVE-2025-69691 because the API call is only available to administrators, who are intentionally allowed to execute PHP code, while the CVE record's CVSS 3.1 vector scores it with low privileges (EUVD-2025-209739); the researcher adds that the endpoint is enabled by default and default administrator credentials are widely deployed (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16). ENISA's EUVD scores CVE-2025-69690 at 9.1, against the researcher's 8.8 (EUVD-2025-209738). Netgate's refusal to patch is reported by the researcher (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16), the CVE records mark both flaws as disputed by the supplier because the functions are admin-only (EUVD-2025-209739), and no cited source says whether pfSense Plus is affected. The researcher's post gives no file to audit for persistence, so the check is the firewall's own access logs for pfsense.exec_php calls and unplanned configuration restores (Full Disclosure, 2026-02-16).

entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: Microsoft shows how two Semantic Kernel flaws turned prompts into shells on the agent host; both were patched in February
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-26030 +1updatedNATOA2

Microsoft Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-26030 / CVE-2026-25592: prompt injection reaches eval() and the host Startup folder in an AI agent framework, fixed since February

Microsoft's Defender research team published on 2026-05-07 how two Semantic Kernel flaws turn a prompt injection into code execution on the host running an AI agent (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07). Both were fixed months earlier: CVE-2026-25592 in February (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-2ww3-72rp-wpp4, 2026-02-06) and CVE-2026-26030 later the same month (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-xjw9-4gw8-4rqx, 2026-02-19).

CVE-2026-26030 (Python semantic-kernel before 1.39.4) sits in the In-Memory Vector Store filter behind the Search Plugin: in the default configuration the filter is a Python lambda executed with eval(), and an AI-controlled value is interpolated into it (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07). Microsoft's exploit prompt escaped the template string, traversed Python's class hierarchy to BuiltinImporter, loaded os and called system(), bypassing the AST-based blocklist; the fix adds node-type and function-call allowlists and blocks class-hierarchy attributes (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07). The attack needs a prompt-injection vector and the Search Plugin backed by the In-Memory Vector Store in its default configuration (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07), and the advisory advises against using the In-Memory Vector Store in production (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-xjw9-4gw8-4rqx, 2026-02-19).

CVE-2026-25592 (.NET Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.Core before 1.71.0) exposed DownloadFileAsync to the model as a kernel function, so a prompt could have the agent write a script created inside the Azure Container Apps sandbox into the host's Windows Startup folder, where it runs at the next sign-in; upload_file in both SDKs similarly accepted any local path, allowing host files to be read out (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07). The advisory's workaround is a Function Invocation Filter that allow-lists localFilePath for the download and upload functions (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-2ww3-72rp-wpp4, 2026-02-06). No source reports exploitation.

Exposure
Agents built on Python semantic-kernel before 1.39.4 using the In-Memory Vector Store filter, or on the .NET Core plugins before 1.71.0 using the sessions Python plugin (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07).
Detection
In process telemetry, a Semantic Kernel host process (a Python interpreter or dotnet.exe) spawning a shell or download utility is what Microsoft's hunting queries look for, and Microsoft names an agent process dropping scripts into a Startup folder as behaviour endpoint defences should catch (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07).
Defender takeaway
The model is not a security boundary; any agent tool that reaches eval() or the host file system needs the same input validation as an internet-facing endpoint, and these two fixes have been available since February (GitHub, 2026-02-06) (GitHub, 2026-02-19).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:44 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-audittitleheadlinesummarytechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesclassificationbodydeep_divedeep_dive_category

In CVE-2026-25592, DownloadFileAsync is what writes attacker content to the host, including the Startup folder, and upload_file is what reads host files out (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07); the earlier text had the two reversed. CVE-2026-26030 passes an interpolated lambda to eval() behind an AST-based blocklist, which Microsoft bypassed through BuiltinImporter (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-07). The fixes were published in February (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-xjw9-4gw8-4rqx, 2026-02-19) (GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-2ww3-72rp-wpp4, 2026-02-06), three months before Microsoft's write-up.

Both score CVSS 9.9 and need a prompt-injection vector; no exploitation is reported.

CVE-2026-26030 is an eval() of a lambda with an AST-based blocklist bypassed through BuiltinImporter, not an f-string with a literal-text blocklist. The advisories date from February, not 2026-05-07; the product, EU-pilot and default-store claims, the Python-side blast-radius claim and the EDR category names had no source; and the CVEs need a low-privileged attacker with no user interaction. The entry is rewritten from Microsoft's post and the two advisories with exposure, detection and takeaway lines, a rating and an ATT&CK mapping.

entries.action_label: DENIC's new signing system made one key pair per…
entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: DENIC's new signing system made one key pair per HSM, so most .de signatures failed validation for over three hours
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

DENIC .de DNSSEC outage: a faulty key rollover made all .de domains unresolvable for validating resolvers for more than three hours on 5 May 2026

During a routine, scheduled DNSSEC key rollover on the evening of 2026-05-05, DENIC distributed signatures for the .de zone that validating resolvers could not verify, so they treated responses for all .de domains as bogus (DENIC, 2026-05-06). DENIC dates the incident from 21:57, began distributing a correct zone at 00:08 and had fully restored normal operation by 01:15 on 2026-05-06, giving no time zone; read as CEST, that is 19:57 to 23:15 UTC (DENIC, 2026-05-06); Cloudflare saw SERVFAILs from about 19:30 UTC and rolled out its own mitigation at 22:17 UTC through an existing override rule, having no native negative trust anchor mechanism (Cloudflare, 2026-05-06); heise gives 21:43 for the first disruption, which read as CEST is 19:43 UTC (heise online, 2026-05-08), so the three sources give three onsets. DENIC's analysis traces the fault to in-house code around its hardware security modules in the third-generation signing system it put into operation in April 2026: instead of one key pair stored on three HSMs, the software generated three different key pairs, one per HSM, and only one of them matched the pre-published DNSKEY (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08). Because signatures over NSEC3 records were also unverifiable, even second-level domains without DNSSEC failed to resolve, and DENIC's three permanent validation tools detected the anomaly but their alerts were not processed correctly (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08). DENIC's final report of 2026-06-11 confirms that initial analysis, rules out any compromise of the signing system and any malfunction of Knot or the HSMs, and explains that the test environment, a single HSM at one location, did not fully execute the rollover-agent code, which misbehaves only when several HSMs are connected (DENIC final report, 2026-06-11).

Defender takeaway
A TLD-side DNSSEC failure looks the same as an attack to a validating resolver; operators of validating resolvers should have a tested way to mark a broken TLD as insecure and should rely on serve-stale to absorb the first hours, as Cloudflare did (Cloudflare, 2026-05-06).
Update10 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-10-001sourcesbody

DENIC published its initial analysis on 2026-05-08 (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08) (heise online, 2026-05-08). A faulty piece of code in its in-house development generated three different key pairs instead of one for the same key tag, 33834, and only one of their public keys was in the DNSKEY record, so only about a third of the signatures could be validated (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08). Knot itself is standard software in the process; the defect was in DENIC's own code (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08). DENIC's validation tools detected the faulty signatures as designed, but their alerts were not processed correctly (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08).

Correction11 Oct 2026 14:30 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-auditkindtitleheadlinesummaryprioritytagstechniquessourcesclassificationbodysectors

DENIC gives 21:57 and 01:15 without a time zone; read as CEST, the incident ran from 19:57 UTC until normal operation returned at 23:15 UTC (DENIC, 2026-05-06), and Cloudflare dates the onset to about 19:30 UTC and its own mitigation, an override rule rather than a native negative trust anchor, to 22:17 UTC (Cloudflare, 2026-05-06). DENIC's addendum of 11 May 2026 says no key-tag collision occurred; the software generated one key pair per HSM, and only one matched the published DNSKEY (DENIC analysis, 2026-05-08). No source gives 18 million affected domains, singles out government domains, or mentions .ch.

Correction21 Oct 2026 12:11 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1149Z-auditevent_datesourcesbodyheadlinetitle

The outage began on the evening of 2026-05-05 (DENIC, 2026-05-06). DENIC's final report of 2026-06-11 confirms the findings of its initial analysis of 2026-05-08 and lists its short-term measures: additional alerts based on better visibility of errors, including those in the continuously running testing and validation tools; an accelerated procedure to provide a valid zone backup in an emergency; partial validation of the zone before deployment; no further ZSK rollover until further measures are complete, including a more secure software development process and a test environment with higher coverage; and an external security and process analysis (DENIC final report, 2026-06-11).

entries.summary: A routine DNSSEC key rollover on 2026-05-05 left the .de zone with signatures validating resolvers could not verify, from an onset the sources place between about 19:30 and 19:57 UTC until DENIC restored normal operation at 23:15 UTC. DENIC's new signing system generated one key pair per HSM instead of one shared pair, so only one matched the published DNSKEY; unverifiable NSEC3 signatures broke even unsigned .de domains.
entries.title: DENIC .de DNSSEC outage: a faulty key rollover made all .de domains unresolvable for validating resolvers for more than three hours on 5 May 2026

updates.summary: UPDATE (originally covered 2026-05-09): DENIC published its formal technical post-mortem on 2026-05-08 (DENIC analysis blog (German), 2026-05-08 · heise online, 2026-05-08).

The times were local time labelled UTC: the outage began between about 19:30 and 19:57 UTC, depending on the source, and ended at 23:15 UTC, about three and a half hours. Cloudflare's mitigation came about 2 hours 45 minutes after onset through an override rule, not an RFC 7646 negative trust anchor within 90 minutes; the 18 million domains, the government focus and the statement that .ch was unaffected had no source. DENIC's later addendum of 11 May replaces the key-tag collision account: one key pair per HSM instead of a shared pair. The signing system went live in April, not March. The entry is recorded as a non-adversarial resilience item with a rating and priority routine, and both sections are corrected in place.

The outage date is 5 May 2026; 8 May is the date of DENIC's initial analysis, and Cloudflare's account is dated 6 May. DENIC's final report of 11 June 2026 is added: it confirms the initial analysis, rules out compromise and Knot or HSM malfunctions, explains why the single-HSM test environment missed the defect, and lists DENIC's measures. The account dated 10 May now gives only what DENIC had published by then; the 11 May addendum stays in the later section. The title and headline now give the duration as more than three hours, matching the 19:57 to 23:15 UTC timeline.

entries.headline: cPanel patches authenticated Perl code injection (CVE-2026-29202) and two file-permission flaws across cPanel & WHM
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-29202 +2updatedNATOA2

cPanel & WHM security update of 2026-05-08: CVE-2026-29202 Perl code injection, CVE-2026-29203 symlink chmod and CVE-2026-29201 arbitrary file read

cPanel published patches and one advisory per CVE for three cPanel & WHM and WP Squared vulnerabilities on 2026-05-08 (cPanel, CVE-2026-29202). CVE-2026-29202 is a Perl code-injection flaw in the plugin parameter of the create_user API call (cPanel, CVE-2026-29202) that gives arbitrary Perl code execution as the already authenticated account's system user (The Hacker News, 2026-05-09). CVE-2026-29203 is an unsafe symlink handling error that lets a user chmod an arbitrary file, allowing denial of service and possible privilege escalation (cPanel, CVE-2026-29203). CVE-2026-29201 is an arbitrary file read in the feature::LOADFEATUREFILE adminbin call, where a relative path in the feature file name makes an arbitrary file world-readable (cPanel, CVE-2026-29201). The CVE records, as ENISA's EUVD carries them, score CVE-2026-29202 and CVE-2026-29203 at 5.3 under CVSS 4.0 (EUVD-2026-28811; EUVD-2026-28812) and CVE-2026-29201 at 8.6 under CVSS 3.1 with no privileges required (EUVD-2026-28810); The Hacker News reports 8.8, 8.8 and 4.3, and no evidence of exploitation in the wild as of 2026-05-09 (The Hacker News, 2026-05-09).

The fixed releases are cPanel & WHM version 11.136.0.9, 11.134.0.25, 11.132.0.31, 11.130.0.22, 11.126.0.58, 11.124.0.37, 11.118.0.66, 11.110.0.117, 11.102.0.41, 11.94.0.30 and 11.86.0.43 or higher, WP Squared version 11.136.1.11 or higher, and version 11.110.0.116 as a direct update for CentOS 6 and CloudLinux 6 (cPanel, CVE-2026-29202). The update followed by ten days cPanel's advisory for CVE-2026-41940, an authentication bypass (cPanel, CVE-2026-41940) that hosting provider KnownHost reported exploited in the wild since 2026-02-23 (SecurityWeek, 2026-04-30); Shadowserver counted at least 44,000 IP addresses likely compromised through it scanning its honeypots on 2026-04-30 (The Hacker News, 2026-05-04).

Exposure
Every cPanel & WHM and WP Squared server below the fixed release of its branch; CVE-2026-29202 needs an authenticated account (The Hacker News, 2026-05-09) and CVE-2026-29203 a user on the server (cPanel, CVE-2026-29203). The patch ships through the standard automatic update, so servers with automatic updates disabled or version-pinned in the update configuration are the ones left behind (NCSC-CH, 2026-05-08), and the running version is read with /usr/local/cpanel/cpanel -V (cPanel, CVE-2026-29202).
Detection
File-permission telemetry on the server: the two file flaws show as system files made world-readable through the adminbin call (cPanel, CVE-2026-29201) or chmod'ed through a symlink by a user account (cPanel, CVE-2026-29203).
Defender takeaway
No out-of-band action where automatic updates run; on pinned or manually updated servers run /scripts/upcp --force and confirm the version afterwards, as cPanel instructs (cPanel, CVE-2026-29202).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:29 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevent_dateevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitle

The CVE records, as ENISA's EUVD carries them, score 5.3 under CVSS 4.0 for CVE-2026-29202 and CVE-2026-29203 (EUVD-2026-28811; EUVD-2026-28812) and 8.6 under CVSS 3.1 for CVE-2026-29201 (EUVD-2026-28810); the 8.8, 8.8 and 4.3 figures are The Hacker News's (The Hacker News, 2026-05-09). Only CVE-2026-29202 yields code execution: CVE-2026-29203 lets a user chmod an arbitrary file (cPanel, CVE-2026-29203) and CVE-2026-29201 makes an arbitrary file world-readable (cPanel, CVE-2026-29201). The patch and the advisories were published together on 2026-05-08, and the fix covers eleven cPanel & WHM branches from 11.86 to 11.136 and WP Squared, not three (cPanel, CVE-2026-29202). For CVE-2026-41940, Shadowserver counted at least 44,000 likely compromised IP addresses scanning its honeypots on 2026-04-30 (The Hacker News, 2026-05-04), and KnownHost reported exploitation since 2026-02-23 (SecurityWeek, 2026-04-30); no source describes attackers chaining it with CVE-2026-29202.

entries.headline: Ivanti's exploited EPMM flaw needs an admin login, so admin passwords never rotated after January's EPMM zero-days are the real exposure
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-6973 +4exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-6973: Ivanti EPMM admin-authenticated RCE exploited in limited attacks, fixed with four further EPMM flaws including unauthenticated Sentry certificate issuance (CVE-2026-5787)

Ivanti's May 2026 update for on-premises Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) fixes five vulnerabilities. Ivanti states: "At the time of disclosure, we are aware of very limited exploitation of CVE-2026-6973, which requires admin authentication for successful exploitation", and "We are not aware of any customers being exploited by the other vulnerabilities disclosed today"; Ivanti Neurons for MDM, Ivanti EPM and Ivanti Sentry are not affected (Ivanti, 2026-05-07). CVE-2026-6973 (CVSS 7.2) is improper input validation that lets "a remotely authenticated user with administrative access to achieve remote code execution", fixed in 12.6.1.1, 12.7.0.1 and 12.8.0.1 (The Hacker News, 2026-05-07), and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-07).

The admin-login precondition is less reassuring than it looks. CERT-FR recalls that its guidance for January's exploited EPMM flaws CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340 was to reset every local EPMM account password, and warns that where this was not done, attackers can reuse administrator passwords obtained then to exploit CVE-2026-6973 (CERT-FR, 2026-05-07). Ivanti makes the same link, saying customers who rotated credentials after January face a significantly reduced risk (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-07).

The four companion flaws are not reported exploited: CVE-2026-5786 (CVSS 8.8) lets an authenticated attacker gain administrative access, CVE-2026-5787 (CVSS 8.9) lets an unauthenticated attacker impersonate registered Sentry hosts and obtain valid CA-signed client certificates, CVE-2026-5788 (CVSS 7.0) lets an unauthenticated attacker invoke arbitrary methods, and CVE-2026-7821 (CVSS 7.4) lets an unauthenticated attacker enroll a device from a restricted set, exposing information about the appliance (The Hacker News, 2026-05-07). Shadowserver counted over 850 exposed EPMM instances, 508 of them in Europe and 182 in North America (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-07). No one has attributed the exploitation; SecurityWeek notes only that Chinese actors are often believed to be behind Ivanti zero-days (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08).

Exposure
On-premises EPMM below 12.6.1.1, 12.7.0.1 or 12.8.0.1, most acutely appliances that were exploited in the January CVE-2026-1281/1340 wave and whose admin passwords were never reset. CVE-2026-7821 affects only deployments that use and have configured Apple Device Enrollment (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-07).
Detection
Administrative API sessions from sources outside the management network or at unusual hours, followed by the EPMM service spawning shells or making outbound connections, and for CVE-2026-5787, client certificates issued to Sentry hosts that do not exist in the deployment.
Defender takeaway
Patching closes all five flaws, but only a credential reset evicts an attacker who already holds a January-era admin password, so do both on any appliance that was internet-facing during January. Ivanti advises reviewing every account with admin rights and rotating those credentials where necessary (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-07). The May builds are not the end of the patch path: the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security reports that Ivanti's critical EPMM update of 2026-06-09 covers versions 12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1 and prior (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-06-09).
Update09 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-09-migratedregionssectorssourcestagsbody

CERT-FR (CERT-FR, 2026-05-07), Germany's BSI (BSI, 2026-05-07) and NCSC-CH (NCSC-CH Cyber Security Hub, 2026-05-08) published advisories on the May 2026 EPMM update. CERT-FR highlights the reuse of administrator passwords stolen in January as the way attackers reach CVE-2026-6973 (CERT-FR, 2026-05-07), and BSI notes that the required admin credentials may have leaked in the January attacks via CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340 (BSI, 2026-05-07).

Update10 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-10-001cvesevidencesourcestagsbody

Shadowserver counted over 850 internet-exposed EPMM instances, 508 of them in Europe and 182 in North America (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-07). Ivanti has confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-6973 against "a very limited number of customers" without naming them, and SecurityWeek notes that Chinese actors are often believed to be behind Ivanti zero-days, without attributing this wave (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08). The same May update fixes CVE-2026-5786, CVE-2026-5787, CVE-2026-5788 and CVE-2026-7821, none reported exploited (Ivanti, 2026-05-07).

Correction30 Sep 2026 07:22 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-audittitleheadlinesummaryevent_datetagstechniquesaffected_productscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteclassificationactionsbody

The earlier text described an exploited pre-authentication chain from CVE-2026-5787 into CVE-2026-6973, marked all five CVEs exploited and KEV-listed, and named four European public bodies as victims of this wave. Ivanti reports very limited exploitation of CVE-2026-6973 alone, which requires admin authentication, and no exploitation of the other four (Ivanti, 2026-05-07); only CVE-2026-6973 is in KEV (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-07); and no cited source names victims of the May wave. The path CERT-FR describes is reuse of administrator passwords stolen in January (CERT-FR, 2026-05-07). CVE-2026-7821 affects only deployments that use and have configured Apple Device Enrollment (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-07).

entries.headline: Microsoft: macOS infostealer campaign moves from disk images to ClickFix Terminal-paste lures for MacSync, SHub and AMOS
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

macOS infostealer campaign shifts to ClickFix Terminal commands to deliver MacSync, SHub Stealer and AMOS

Microsoft reported on 2026-05-06 that an infostealer campaign targeting macOS, whose earlier iterations delivered the stealers in disk-image (.dmg) files that users installed by hand, now instructs users to run Terminal commands that retrieve remote content with native utilities and then execute a script-based loader (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). The ClickFix-style instructions sit on standalone sites, on the note-taking platform Craft and in fake troubleshooting posts on Medium that promise to fix common macOS problems such as low disk space, and the pasted Base64 command decodes and runs an AppleScript or Bash loader (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). Scripts launched from Terminal do not undergo the code-signing and notarization evaluation Gatekeeper can apply to application bundles opened through Finder (Microsoft, 2026-05-06).

Microsoft tracks three execution paths. In the loader campaign, seen since February 2026, curl fetches a loader, a zsh script decodes a Base64 and Gzip payload and runs it with eval, fingerprints the host, stops on a Russian or CIS keyboard layout and runs a remote AppleScript stealer in memory through osascript; the stealer, which calls itself SHub Stealer, asks for the user's password as if installing a helper, validates it with dscl, stages browser credentials, Keychain entries, iCloud and Telegram data, wallets and small documents in a temporary folder, compresses and exfiltrates them and deletes the staging files, then persists as a LaunchAgent disguised as a Google software-update agent that runs Base64 commands returned by its C2 (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). The script campaign, seen in April 2026, streams a remote script straight into the shell from a one-line pipeline and persists an obfuscated AppleScript in a LaunchAgent that probes hard-coded C2 candidates with curl, falls back to a server identifier hidden on a Telegram bot page and pipes the server's response into osascript (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). The helper campaign (AMOS), seen since late January 2026, decodes and gunzips a first stage that downloads a Mach-O executable, strips its extended attributes, checks for virtualisation with system_profiler, copies Keychain databases and Chromium browser passwords and session cookies, exfiltrates a ZIP archive and installs a LaunchDaemon that runs a bash wrapper with root privileges at every boot to keep a backdoor running (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). In the loader and helper campaigns the stealer replaces installed Ledger Wallet and Trezor Suite apps, and in the loader campaign also Exodus, with trojanized versions fetched from its C2 (Microsoft, 2026-05-06); Malwarebytes documented SHub Stealer modifying wallet apps after a Terminal-paste lure on a fake CleanMyMac site in March 2026 (Malwarebytes, 2026-03-06).

Exposure
Mac users who can paste commands into Terminal; Apple has updated XProtect signatures, and macOS 26.4 and later blocks the paste of a potentially malicious command into Terminal, so earlier releases lack that mitigation (Microsoft, 2026-05-06).
Detection
Process lineage: Terminal or shell sessions spawned by installers or user apps, and unusual sequences of curl, base64, gunzip, osascript and dscl; file telemetry for LaunchAgent and LaunchDaemon plists written by script interpreters; archive creation of collected data followed by an HTTP POST with curl (Microsoft, 2026-05-06).
Defender takeaway
Managed Macs on macOS 26.4 or later get Apple's paste blocking against this delivery; on a Mac where the chain ran, treat the Keychain, browser passwords and session cookies as stolen and reinstall wallet apps from their vendors, because the stealer replaces Ledger Wallet, Trezor Suite and Exodus with trojanized copies (Microsoft, 2026-05-06).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:25 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

The campaign did not newly expand to macOS: its earlier iterations already delivered the stealers to Macs in disk-image files, and the change Microsoft reported is the move to Terminal commands that fetch remote content and run a script-based loader (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). Only the script campaign uses a one-line pipeline into the shell; the loader campaign runs a zsh loader through eval and the helper campaign downloads a Mach-O executable (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). The wallet tampering replaces installed Ledger Wallet, Trezor Suite and Exodus apps with trojanized archives fetched from the C2 (Microsoft, 2026-05-06). Detection rests on Microsoft's guidance: Terminal or shell sessions spawned by installers or user apps, unusual curl, base64, gunzip, osascript and dscl sequences, and archive creation followed by an HTTP POST (Microsoft, 2026-05-06).

entries.headline: Sophos: "Beagle" backdoor distributed via fake Claude AI site using DonutLoader + DLL sideloading on a signed G DATA AV updater
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Sophos: "Beagle" backdoor distributed via fake Claude AI site using DonutLoader + DLL sideloading on a signed G DATA AV updater

Sophos X-Ops published a write-up on 2026-05-07 of a counterfeit Claude AI site distributing a previously undocumented Windows backdoor it named Beagle, and assesses that the site is likely part of an active malvertising campaign (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07). The chain delivers a roughly 505 MB ZIP archive containing a malicious MSI that drops a legitimate, signed G DATA antivirus updater executable, an encrypted data file and an attacker-controlled DLL into the user's startup folder, so the updater sideloads the malicious DLL (DLL side-loading) (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07). The DLL decrypts the data file and executes the resulting Donut (DonutLoader) shellcode, an open-source in-memory loader, which loads Beagle (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07). Beagle communicates with a subdomain of the same lookalike site over TCP/443 and UDP/8080 with AES-encrypted payloads, and its eight commands are uninstall, cmd, upload, download, mkdir, rename, ls and rm (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07). Sophos notes that an almost identical G DATA sideloading chain has previously been associated with PlugX, which several threat groups use, and suggests the Beagle payload may reflect an actor retooling or imitating another actor's chain. It does not attribute the campaign (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07). A possible hosting server was set up in March 2026, and Sophos found related samples reusing the same XOR key from February, March and April 2026, while cautioning that further evidence would be needed to link them to the same actor (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07).

Sophos places the campaign in a wider pattern of threat actors crafting lures that imitate legitimate AI sites, often through malvertising (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07).

Contradiction: Malwarebytes, describing the same archive, identifies the payload as PlugX, by analogy with an earlier campaign that used the same G DATA sideloading files (Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10), while Sophos analysed it as a previously undocumented backdoor it named Beagle (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07).

Exposure
Windows hosts where a user ran a Claude installer taken from a lookalike site or an ad rather than the official download page. The trojanized installer puts a working copy of Claude under a misspelled lookalike of the Claude directory name inside the Anthropic program folder, which Malwarebytes gives as a check alongside the sideloading files in the user's Startup folder (Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10).
Detection
In file-creation and process telemetry, a signed G DATA antivirus updater, an encrypted data file and a DLL written together into a user's Startup folder after the fake installer's MSI runs (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07). Malwarebytes, describing the same archive, adds that the MSI installs a desktop shortcut that launches a VBScript dropper, run through WScript.exe, which copies the three files into the Startup folder, and that the updater made an outbound connection within seconds (22 seconds in its sandbox run). The dropper script deletes itself, so the Startup-folder files and the running updater process are what persist (Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10).

Triage: the updater is a legitimately signed G DATA binary, so the parent process can look benign to endpoint tools; by inference from Malwarebytes' sandbox and dropper-script analysis, the discriminator is the sequence, in which WScript.exe writes the updater, the DLL it loads from its own directory and an encrypted data file into a user's Startup folder and starts the updater with a hidden window while the freshly installed Claude application opens in the foreground (Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10).

Defender takeaway
Treat AI-tool installers as a high-risk download class. Sophos advises downloading Claude only from the legitimate site and being wary of links from ads and sponsored search results (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07), and Malwarebytes names claude.com/download as the official download page (Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10).
Correction30 Sep 2026 06:54 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-auditsummarybodyclassificationtechniques

The description above previously tied the campaign to Sophos's STAC4713 cluster, which Sophos mentions only for AdaptixC2 activity linked to a separate March sample. Sophos lists eight Beagle commands, dates the related samples to February, March and April 2026, and does not claim TTP similarity with named PlugX clusters or say who the lures target. It assesses the lookalike site as likely, not confirmed, part of an active malvertising campaign (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07).

Malwarebytes' report of 2026-04-10 covers the same attack, not an earlier wave. Sophos refers to it as coverage of this attack, and both describe the same download archive (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-05-07; Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10).

Improvement21 Oct 2026 08:17 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-audittagssectorstechniquesbody

Malwarebytes gives a host check for the trojanized installer: it puts a working copy of Claude under a misspelled lookalike of the Claude directory name inside the Anthropic program folder. Its VBScript dropper, run by WScript.exe, copies the three sideloading files into the user's Startup folder and starts the signed G DATA updater with a hidden window, and a signed parent like this can look benign to endpoint tools (Malwarebytes, 2026-04-10).

entries.action_label: Leaked Bauman University files show GRU officers…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Leaked Bauman University files show GRU officers run a hacking course that places graduates in Sandworm and Fancy Bear
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOB2

Bauman University "Department No. 4": leaked documents show a GRU training pipeline that places graduates in Sandworm and Fancy Bear units

Department No. 4 of the military training centre at Bauman Moscow State Technical University trains hackers and saboteurs for the GRU, according to a joint investigation by The Insider, The Guardian, Le Monde, Der Spiegel, Frontstory and VSquare whose journalists reviewed more than two thousand internal documents from the department (Meduza, 2026-05-07); the Guardian names Delfi among the six outlets and says the files cover several years of activity up to 2025 (The Guardian, 2026-05-07). The documents indicate that the GRU sends its own officers to conduct exams, approve candidates and oversee placements (The Guardian, 2026-05-07). A 144-hour course over two semesters, "Defence against technical reconnaissance", teaches password attacks, software vulnerabilities and trojans, and students must carry out practical penetration tests and develop a computer virus to pass (The Guardian, 2026-05-07). Heise, citing Der Spiegel, adds DDoS attacks, the hacking of a test server at the end of the course and a one-month training camp that all students attend (heise online, 2026-05-07). Students study the protected networks of the US Department of Defense and are trained to exploit vulnerabilities in them with Metasploit (VSquare, 2026-05-07).

Between 10 and 15 students from the department are assigned to GRU units each year, some to military unit 74455, which belongs to Sandworm, and others to Fancy Bear (Meduza, 2026-05-07). The Guardian traces one 2024 graduate to Fancy Bear and another to Unit 74455 in Anapa, and names Viktor Netyksho, a former commander of Fancy Bear's Unit 26165, among the teachers (The Guardian, 2026-05-07). The operations attached to the two units are western accusations, and the outlets differ on one of them: the Guardian says Sandworm has been accused of targeting Ukraine's power grid in 2015 and Emmanuel Macron's 2017 presidential campaign (The Guardian, 2026-05-07), while Le Monde says Fancy Bear (APT28) is accused of stealing emails from Macron's team in early 2017 and, more recently, of targeting institutions involved in organising the Paris 2024 Olympic Games (Le Monde, 2026-05-07). Heise reports, citing Der Spiegel, that one graduate apparently joined a unit said to be behind the 2017 NotPetya malware (heise online, 2026-05-07). Bauman is one pipeline among several: the Guardian's source, a former senior Russian defence official, calls it one of a handful of elite universities used to identify gifted students and says another university, Mirea, was even more crucial in training hackers (The Guardian, 2026-05-07).

Defender takeaway
No change to detection or patching priorities; the files show Sandworm and Fancy Bear staffed through a supervised university course, and the latest cohort of trainees does not graduate until the end of the 2027 academic year (The Guardian, 2026-05-07).
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:21 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationconfidenceentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitlepriority

The consortium's journalists reviewed more than two thousand internal documents from the department and reported on them (Meduza, 2026-05-07). The outlets attach the 2017 Macron campaign breach to different units: the Guardian lists it among Sandworm's accused operations (The Guardian, 2026-05-07), while Le Monde accuses Fancy Bear (APT28), whose most recent alleged activity it names is the targeting of institutions organising the Paris 2024 Olympic Games (Le Monde, 2026-05-07); none of the cited outlets reports continuing 2025 to 2026 APT28 activity against EU government or election targets. The Metasploit training against US Department of Defense networks is VSquare's reporting (VSquare, 2026-05-07), and the one-month camp is one all students attend, per heise citing Der Spiegel (heise online, 2026-05-07).

Between 10 and 15 of its students a year are assigned to GRU units, including Unit 74455 (Sandworm) and Fancy Bear (APT28).

entries.classification_html: NATOA1
entries.headline: JDownloader site hack repointed Windows alternative-installer and Linux shell links to malware on 6 and 7 May 2026
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA1

JDownloader website compromise: "Download Alternative Installer" and Linux shell installer links pointed to malware on 6 and 7 May 2026

Attackers exploited an unpatched vulnerability in the website of JDownloader, a free download manager with millions of users across Windows, macOS and Linux (CyberKendra, 2026-05-08), that let them change access control lists and content without authentication (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-09). After a test on a low-traffic page at about 23:55 UTC on 2026-05-05, they repointed the Windows "Download Alternative Installer" links and the Linux shell installer link to unrelated malicious files at about 00:01 UTC on 2026-05-06; the developers were alerted through Reddit on 2026-05-07 and shut the server down that day, and the site returned with verified links on the night of 8 to 9 May (JDownloader). The genuine installer packages were not modified, the changes stayed within the content management system without access to the host file system, and the other installers on the site, the RSA-signed built-in updater and the winget, Flatpak, Snap and Docker channels were not affected (JDownloader). The developers said the malicious Windows installers lacked a valid digital signature (Security Affairs, 2026-05-10), and users reported unfamiliar publisher names such as Zipline LLC, The Water Team and Peace Team (PiunikaWeb, 2026-05-08).

Researcher Thomas Klemenc found the Windows files to be a loader for a heavily obfuscated Python-based RAT that runs Python code delivered from its C2 servers; the Linux installer downloads an archive disguised as an SVG file, installs one of two extracted binaries as a SUID-root binary under /usr/bin, creates a persistence script under /etc/profile.d and launches a Pyarmor-obfuscated payload masquerading as a system daemon (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-09). An ANY.RUN analysis shows an 8-minute delay before the payload activates (Security Affairs, 2026-05-10).

Exposure
Machines on which an installer downloaded through the "Download Alternative Installer" links or the Linux shell installer link of jdownloader.org on 6 or 7 May 2026 (UTC) was run; downloading without running, other installers from the site, in-app updates and store or package channels are not at risk (JDownloader).
Detection
Code-signing state in process and file telemetry: a JDownloader installer that is unsigned or signed by anyone other than AppWork GmbH (JDownloader); on Linux hosts that ran the shell installer, a new script under /etc/profile.d and a new SUID-root binary under /usr/bin (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-09).

Triage: genuine JDownloader installers are signed by AppWork GmbH; the same installer unsigned or carrying another publisher's name is the substitute (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-09).

Defender takeaway
On any machine where a substitute installer ran, reinstall the operating system and change passwords for important accounts from another device, as JDownloader advises (JDownloader); machines that only took in-app or store updates need no action.
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:33 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationevent_dateevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitle

The malicious links were live from about 00:01 UTC on 2026-05-06 until the server was shut down on 2026-05-07, and the risk window JDownloader names is 6 to 7 May, not about 48 hours to 8 May (JDownloader). JDownloader's notice lists SHA256 checksums of the malicious substitute installer files (JDownloader), and the check for a downloaded Windows installer is its signature: genuine installers are signed by AppWork GmbH, the substitutes are unsigned or carry another publisher's name (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-09). The Python RAT is researcher Thomas Klemenc's analysis of the Windows files; on Linux the tampered shell installer installs a SUID-root binary under /usr/bin and a persistence script under /etc/profile.d (BleepingComputer, 2026-05-09), which are the artefacts to look for on Linux hosts rather than Python child processes of a JDownloader parent. Anyone who ran a substitute installer is advised to reinstall the operating system and change important passwords from another device (JDownloader).

entries.summary: Attackers exploited an unpatched flaw in the content management system of jdownloader.org, the site of the free JDownloader download manager, and from about 00:01 UTC on 2026-05-06 until the server was shut down on 2026-05-07 pointed its Windows "Download Alternative Installer" links and its Linux shell installer link to malicious files. The Windows files load a Python-based RAT and the Linux installer plants a SUID-root binary and a login-script persistence; anyone who ran one is advised to reinstall the operating system.

The vendor's notice lists checksums of the malicious substitutes, and the check it gives is the AppWork GmbH signature; an independent analyst identified the Windows payload as a loader for a Python-based RAT, while the Linux installer plants a SUID-root binary and a login-script persistence.

entries.action_label: Braintrust AWS account breach likely exposed…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Braintrust AWS account breach likely exposed customers' stored AI provider keys; every customer asked to rotate them
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Braintrust AI evaluation platform AWS account breach: customer-stored AI provider API keys likely exposed, all customers urged to rotate org-level keys

Braintrust, an AI evaluation and observability platform, discovered on 2026-05-04, after a report of suspicious behaviour, that attackers had accessed one of its AWS accounts (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08). It emailed customers on Monday 2026-05-04 and disclosed the incident on its website on Tuesday 2026-05-05 (TechCrunch, 2026-05-06); SecurityWeek dates the customer email to 2026-05-05 (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08). The internal AWS account likely gave the attackers access to the org-level API keys customers store with Braintrust to access AI models; at least one customer was affected and three others reported suspicious spikes in AI provider usage, while Braintrust said it had not identified broader customer exposure (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08). Braintrust locked down the compromised account, audited and restricted access across related systems and rotated internal secrets; the cause of the breach is under investigation (TechCrunch, 2026-05-06). Nudge Security CTO Jaime Blasco told SecurityWeek the exposed keys were likely stored for AI-forward companies such as Box, Cloudflare, Dropbox, Notion, Ramp and Stripe, and called every AI evaluation, observability and gateway tool a company adopts a credential warehouse (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08).

Exposure
Organisations that stored org-level AI provider keys in Braintrust; Braintrust informed all org admins with stored AI provider secrets (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08).
Detection
AI provider usage and billing telemetry for the keys that were stored in Braintrust: the signal three customers reported was a suspicious spike in AI provider usage (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08).
Defender takeaway
Braintrust customers delete or revoke the existing AI provider secrets on the org-level settings page, configure new ones and confirm the rotation from their timestamps, as Braintrust recommends (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08), and review the provider-side usage of the old keys up to their revocation; organisations that stored no keys in Braintrust have no decision to make.
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:23 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditaffected_productsbodyclassificationconfidenceevent_dateevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

Braintrust discovered the incident on 2026-05-04 after a report of suspicious behaviour (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08) and disclosed it on its website on 2026-05-05 (TechCrunch, 2026-05-06); 2026-05-04 is not the date of the attackers' access, which no source gives, so there is no known access window to search audit logs against. The exposed secrets were the API keys customers use to access AI models, with no AI provider named, and the email asked every customer to rotate them (TechCrunch, 2026-05-06); Braintrust's notice calls them org-level AI provider keys (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08). Box, Cloudflare, Dropbox, Notion, Ramp and Stripe are companies whose AI provider keys were likely stored in Braintrust, in the estimate of Nudge Security's CTO, not SaaS services whose credentials were at risk (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08). At least one customer was affected and three others reported suspicious spikes in AI provider usage (SecurityWeek, 2026-05-08), so the check that matters is the provider-side usage of the keys that were stored in Braintrust.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Copy Fail turns an unprivileged Linux shell into root with one portable script; CISA lists it as exploited
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-31431exploitedupdatedNATOB2

CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail: Linux kernel AF_ALG page-cache write gives any local user root on mainstream distributions, public exploit, CISA KEV-listed (CVSS 7.8)

Xint (Theori) disclosed "Copy Fail" on 2026-04-29: a flaw in the Linux kernel's algif_aead, reachable through AF_ALG, the socket type that exposes the kernel crypto subsystem to unprivileged userspace, lets a local unprivileged user trigger a deterministic, controlled 4-byte write into the page cache by combining AF_ALG with splice() (Xint, 2026-04-29). Corrupting the cached copy of a setuid binary such as su turns that write into root, and the same exploit script worked unchanged on Ubuntu 24.04, Amazon Linux 2023, RHEL 10.1 and SUSE 16 (Xint, 2026-04-29). The bug comes from a 2017 in-place optimization that mainline removed by reverting algif_aead to out-of-place operation (Xint, 2026-04-29). CERT-EU rates it CVSS 7.8 (CERT-EU, 2026-04-29), CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-05-01 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-01), and Ubuntu ships fixed kernels 5.15.0-179.189 for 22.04 and 6.8.0-117.117 for 24.04 (Ubuntu, 2026-04-22); Red Hat states that all its fixes are available (Red Hat RHSB-2026-002). Microsoft reports limited in-the-wild privilege escalation involving su that may be associated with either Dirty Frag or Copy Fail (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-08).

Exposure
Any Linux host where an attacker can run code as an unprivileged local user, including inside a container sharing the host kernel, on a kernel without the fix (Xint, 2026-04-29).
Detection
File-integrity tools comparing on-disk checksums miss the corruption, because the on-disk file is unchanged and only the page cache is modified (Xint, 2026-04-29). The escalation shows up as an unprivileged process opening AF_ALG sockets and calling splice(), followed by a setuid binary such as su granting root without a matching authentication event; after patching, look back for root shells spawned from su by unexpected accounts since late April (Xint, 2026-04-29) (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-08).
Defender takeaway
A public, distribution-portable root exploit for local users puts every multi-user, container or web-facing Linux host on the patch-now list; where a fixed kernel cannot be deployed immediately, blocking AF_ALG socket creation with seccomp or blacklisting algif_aead closes the path (Xint, 2026-04-29). On RHEL the module is built into the kernel and cannot be blocklisted, so Red Hat gives the boot argument initcall_blacklist=algif_aead_init instead, warning that it may affect the performance of functionality that uses kernel cryptographic functions (Red Hat RHSB-2026-002).
Correction11 Oct 2026 14:23 UTCrun 2026-10-11T1307Z-auditkindtitleheadlinesummaryevent_datetagscvesaffected_productstechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_noteclassificationbodyreferences

CISA added CVE-2026-31431 to its catalog on 2026-05-01 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-01). Ubuntu's fixed kernels are 5.15.0-179.189 for 22.04 and 6.8.0-117.117 for 24.04 (Ubuntu, 2026-04-22); the earlier kernel versions had no source. Microsoft reports limited su-based privilege escalation that "may be indicative of techniques associated with either" Dirty Frag or Copy Fail (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-08); it does not describe the two being used as a complementary pair or an initial access through SSH credential stuffing.

Correction21 Oct 2026 12:08 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1149Z-auditsummarybodysourcesevidence

Blacklisting algif_aead does not work on Red Hat Enterprise Linux: Red Hat states that the module "cannot be blocklisted due to being built into the kernel" and gives the boot argument initcall_blacklist=algif_aead_init to block the affected functions, with initcall_blacklist=af_alg_init as an alternative that blocks the AF_ALG interface itself; it warns of possible performance impact on functionality that uses kernel cryptographic functions, and states that all its fixes are available (Red Hat RHSB-2026-002). Xint also gives blocking AF_ALG socket creation with seccomp as an interim measure (Xint, 2026-04-29).

Builds on: WordPress core's REST batch endpoint + a WP_Query SQL injection chain to unauthenticated RCE on…

entries.summary: CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail, CVSS 7.8) lets an unprivileged local user make a controlled 4-byte write into the page cache through the kernel's AF_ALG crypto socket interface and splice(), corrupting a setuid binary to gain root. Xint published a portable exploit on 2026-04-29 that works unchanged on Ubuntu, Amazon Linux, RHEL and SUSE; CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 2026-05-01. Until a fixed kernel is installed, blacklisting the algif_aead module blocks it where the module is loadable; on RHEL it is built into the kernel, and Red Hat gives a boot argument that blocks it instead.
entries.title: CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail: Linux kernel AF_ALG page-cache write gives any local user root on mainstream distributions, public exploit, CISA KEV-listed (CVSS 7.8)

updates.summary: The entry was a bare migrated update that never said what Copy Fail is. CISA added the flaw to its catalog on 2026-05-01, not 2026-05-06; the Ubuntu and RHEL kernel versions given were not the vendors' fixed builds; and Microsoft does not describe the two flaws as used complementarily or via SSH credential stuffing, only limited su escalation that may be either. CERT-EU's advisory is dated 2026-04-29, the KEV catalogue landing page is dropped, and the entry is rewritten as a vulnerability entry from Xint's disclosure, CERT-EU, the KEV record and Ubuntu's tracker, with the CVE record, a rating, an ATT&CK mapping, and labelled guidance, including the module blacklist as the interim measure. A reference to the WordPress WP2Shell entry, which also cites this CVE, is added.

The interim mitigation was given as a module blacklist for every distribution, but Red Hat builds algif_aead into its kernel, where it cannot be blocklisted; Red Hat's boot argument that blocks the affected functions is now given for RHEL, together with Xint's seccomp option and Red Hat's statement that all its fixes are available.

entries.action_label: ABW reports breaches at five Polish water plants in…
entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: ABW reports breaches at five Polish water plants in 2025, with equipment settings altered in some cases, naming no actor or access route
entries.html:
NOTABLEexploitedupdatedNATOA2

Poland's ABW: attackers breached five municipal water treatment plants in 2025 and in some cases altered equipment parameters, and hacktivists exploited weak passwords on exposed management panels at municipal sites

Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) reports in its 2024-2025 activity review that in 2025 "security breaches were reported at water treatment plants in the following towns: Jabłonna Lacka, Szczytno, Małdyty, Tolkmicko and Sierakowo", and that "by gaining access, in some cases, to industrial control systems, the attackers were able to alter the technical parameters of the equipment", a direct risk to the plants' continued operation and to water supply (ABW, 2026-05-25). ABW describes hacktivist groups as particularly active against municipal infrastructure and says they "exploited glaring vulnerabilities in the form of poor password policies and unsecured device management panels, accessible directly via the public internet" (ABW, 2026-05-25). The report names no actor and no access vector for the water-plant breaches and does not tie them to the hacktivist activity. The state-sponsored groups it names, APT28, APT29 and UNC1151, are described as carrying out "sophisticated, long-term espionage and sabotage operations" (ABW, 2026-05-25). ABW's press office told CyberDefence24 that the potentially compromised water and sewage operators had IT resources reachable from the public internet, including HMI panels controlling their processes (CyberDefence24, 2025-10-08). CyberDefence24, which lists the five plants among the sites hit, describes the attacks on the Polish water sector as the work of pro-Russian hacktivists (CyberDefence24, 2025-10-08).

Exposure
Municipal infrastructure operators, which ABW says include sewage and water treatment plants and waste incinerators, whose device management panels answer from the internet and accept weak passwords, the weaknesses ABW says hacktivist groups exploited (ABW, 2026-05-25).
Detection
Successful logins to HMI, PLC or device management interfaces from internet addresses, and changes to setpoints or equipment parameters that match no operator log.
Defender takeaway
ABW's report does not say how the five plants were breached, but its press office points to internet-reachable IT resources and HMI panels at the potentially compromised operators (CyberDefence24, 2025-10-08). The route ABW describes for hacktivists against municipal infrastructure, an internet-reachable management panel with a weak password (ABW, 2026-05-25), is closed by removing direct internet exposure of OT interfaces and enforcing unique strong credentials on them.
Update09 May 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-05-09-migratedentitiessectorssourcesbody

ABW's 2024-2025 activity review, published in Polish on 2026-05-06 with an English edition dated 2026-05-25 (ABW, 2026-05-06), names the five affected facilities: Jabłonna Lacka, Szczytno, Małdyty, Tolkmicko and Sierakowo (ABW, 2026-05-25). It names no actor and no access vector for the water-plant intrusions (ABW, 2026-05-25).

Correction30 Sep 2026 07:12 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-audittitleheadlinesummaryevent_dateprioritytagsentitiestechniquessourcesevidenceclassificationbodyverification

The earlier text said pro-Russian hacktivists modified pump settings at all five facilities and that manual overrides prevented disruption. It also said ABW attributed these intrusions to APT28, APT29 and UNC1151, and that ABW attributed the five plant breaches to pro-Russian hacktivists exploiting flat IT/OT networks, in a pattern like NoName057(16) and Cyber Army of Russia Reborn campaigns, and it detailed Poland's NIS2 transposition. It dated ABW's report 2026-05-07. ABW released the review in Polish on 2026-05-06 and in English on 2026-05-25 (ABW, 2026-05-06). ABW's report names no actor and no access vector for the water-plant breaches. It says breaches were reported at the five plants and that, "in some cases", the attackers reached industrial control systems and altered the technical parameters of the equipment (ABW, 2026-05-25).
